# dsh-plugins

Public [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) plugins by [Chris Johnson](https://github.com/chrisjohnson). One repository, independently installable plugins — each with its own README, its own tests, its own changelog and its own version.

## Install

**Nothing here is published to npm.** Every release is a git tag on this repository, named `<package>-v<version>` (for example `dsh-model-switch-v0.2.1`), and you install a plugin by pinning that tag plus the package's subdirectory:

```sh
dsh plugin --profile web add "git+https://github.com/chrisjohnson/dsh-plugins.git#<package>-v<version>&path:/packages/<dir>"
```

`dsh plugin add` hands that spec to pnpm and also lists the package under the profile's `dsh.profile.bundles`, which is what activates its configuration layer. If you manage a profile's `package.json` yourself, the same spec works with pnpm directly — but then add the package name to `dsh.profile.bundles` by hand, because a plain `pnpm add` installs the plugin without enabling it:

```sh
pnpm add "git+https://github.com/chrisjohnson/dsh-plugins.git#<package>-v<version>&path:/packages/<dir>"
```

Pick the tag from [the repository's tags](https://github.com/chrisjohnson/dsh-plugins/tags); `<dir>` is the folder under `packages/` in the index below.

> **Warning — do not install these by bare name.** `pnpm add dsh-model-switch` (or `dsh plugin add dsh-model-switch`) resolves against the npm registry, and the npm package called `dsh-model-switch` belongs to an unrelated author: it is **not** this plugin. The same can happen to any unscoped `dsh-*` name. Always use the git-tag spec above.

## Index

| Plugin | What it is for | Latest | Directory |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **[dsh-model-switch](./packages/model-switch/)** | Let the agent switch its own model mid-session, with a context-window fit guard so neither it nor a human in the composer can strand a conversation on a model too small to read it. | 0.2.1 | `packages/model-switch` |
| **[dsh-image-search-searxng](./packages/image-search-searxng/)** | A model-facing `image_search` tool over your own SearXNG, rendered inline in the Web GUI. | 0.2.0 | `packages/image-search-searxng` |
| **[dsh-continue-kicker](./packages/continue-kicker/)** | Automatically send "continue" when a turn halts on the output-token limit (or after a crash, or on a reasoning-only empty stop), with a runaway guard that stops after repeated kicks with no progress. | 0.2.0 | `packages/continue-kicker` |
| **[dsh-loop-watchdog](./packages/loop-watchdog/)** | Detect an agent stuck in a loop before each step (a deterministic repetition check plus an optional model judge), keep an audit ledger of every check, optionally steer the session, and chart the ledger in a `dsh-better-sidebar` panel. | 0.1.0 | `packages/loop-watchdog` |
| **[dsh-scheduled-queue](./packages/scheduled-queue/)** | Schedule the composer's draft to be sent to its own session later, with a per-session dock to edit, cancel or send now. Runs alongside the official schedule bundle. | 0.1.0 | `packages/scheduled-queue` |
| **[dsh-better-git-worktree](./packages/better-git-worktree/)** | Run a session in its own self-contained git working copy: a composer Worktree switch, a `worktree_convert` tool, session-list status badges, a header menu, and an archive prompt that decides the working copy's fate. | 0.1.1 | `packages/better-git-worktree` |

Install lines for the latest release of each package:

```sh
dsh plugin --profile web add "git+https://github.com/chrisjohnson/dsh-plugins.git#dsh-model-switch-v0.2.1&path:/packages/model-switch"
dsh plugin --profile web add "git+https://github.com/chrisjohnson/dsh-plugins.git#dsh-image-search-searxng-v0.2.0&path:/packages/image-search-searxng"
dsh plugin --profile web add "git+https://github.com/chrisjohnson/dsh-plugins.git#dsh-continue-kicker-v0.2.0&path:/packages/continue-kicker"
dsh plugin --profile web add "git+https://github.com/chrisjohnson/dsh-plugins.git#dsh-loop-watchdog-v0.1.0&path:/packages/loop-watchdog"
dsh plugin --profile web add "git+https://github.com/chrisjohnson/dsh-plugins.git#dsh-scheduled-queue-v0.1.0&path:/packages/scheduled-queue"
dsh plugin --profile web add "git+https://github.com/chrisjohnson/dsh-plugins.git#dsh-better-git-worktree-v0.1.1&path:/packages/better-git-worktree"
```

Each package's README is the contract: what it does, every configuration key and what happens when it is unset, how it fails, how to install it, and how to run its checks. Nothing important lives only here.

## Releases

1. A release is a normal pull request that bumps one package's version and moves its CHANGELOG `Unreleased` entry under that version.
2. After it merges, the tag `<package>-v<version>` is cut on that merge commit and pushed. Nothing is committed directly to `main`.
3. Consumers pin the tag with the install spec above. A tag is never moved or rewritten once pushed.

Details: [docs/releasing.md](./docs/releasing.md).

## What "a plugin from this repo" means

- **Plain ESM, no build step.** `git clone && npm test` works with nothing installed. No bundler, no TypeScript layer, no generated client — what the harness loads is what is in `src/`.
- **Every plugin declares `dsh.bundle.patch`**, so one command installs *and* activates it; nothing here needs a hand-edited `cordis.yml`.
- **Deployment-specific values are configuration, never defaults.** A plugin that "works on my machine" because it hard-codes my provider ids is broken for everyone else. `node scripts/verify.mjs` fails the build on author-local paths and provider ids.
- **Nothing is required to be configured.** Optional features report themselves unavailable and name the key that enables them, instead of throwing at boot or failing at first use.
- **Every decision worth testing lives in a module that imports nothing from dsh**, which is what makes the tests real rather than decorative.

## Checking this repository

```sh
npm run check          # verify + hook gate + all tests, no install needed
node scripts/verify.mjs            # the release contract (see below)
node scripts/compose-smoke.mjs     # install into a throwaway profile, import, compose
```

`scripts/verify.mjs` is the interesting one: it enforces the rules that make a plugin installable and trustworthy — `dsh.bundle.patch` present and loading the package by name, `dsh.client` matched by an `./client` export, one harness peer range across every package (`>=0.2.0-rc.2 <0.3.0-0 || >=0.3.0-0`; dsh checks it with prereleases included, while plain node-semver/pnpm admit only `0.2.0-rc.*` and `0.3.0-*` prereleases from it), every shipped file inside the `files` allowlist (all a git-tag install ships), a git-tag install line (and no bare-name one) in every package README, every config key documented in its README, every package listed in the index above, and no deployment leakage. It runs on CI for every push and it runs on a bare clone.

## Contributing

Issues and pull requests are welcome — see [CONTRIBUTING.md](./CONTRIBUTING.md). If you are an agent working in this repository, read [AGENTS.md](./AGENTS.md) first; it is short and it exists because these plugins run with your user's credentials.

For how these plugins get developed, tested against a live harness, released and consumed by the deployment they came from, see [docs/testing.md](./docs/testing.md) and [docs/releasing.md](./docs/releasing.md).

## License

MIT — see [LICENSE](./LICENSE).

# dsh-continue-kicker

**Automatically send "continue" when a turn halts, and stop when that is not helping.**

A host-plane plugin for [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness). A session that hits its output-token limit just stops, silently, until somebody notices. This plugin notices: it sends one follow-up user message that tells the model to stop re-deriving its reasoning and act, and it gives up after a configurable number of kicks with no progress in between, so a task genuinely too big for its budget surfaces in the log instead of burning GPU-hours.

## What it kicks on

| Halt | Detected as | Kick |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Output budget exhausted | last `turn/end` reason `max-tokens` | "Do NOT re-derive your thinking: state your conclusion, then act. Be succinct." |
| Reasoning-only empty stop | `completed` turn whose final assistant message has no text and no tool call, with at least `emptyCompletionMinReasoningChars` of reasoning | Same "be decisive" framing |
| Failed turn (opt-in: `kickOnError`) | last `turn/end` reason `error` (the model backend dropped, a provider error) | "The previous turn failed with an error and was cut off before it finished. Please continue from where you left off." |
| Crash-orphaned turn | last `turn/end` reason `interrupted` (synthesized when a session is loaded) | "Please continue from where you left off." |

It never kicks over `aborted` (an explicit Stop, a parent or hook cancel, a disposal), `error` unless `kickOnError` is on, `blocked`, `forked`, a completed turn with real content, or a tail already followed by a user or assistant message.

Two doors feed one decision: `agent/created` (reopening a session, crash recovery) and a live watcher that re-analyses the tail `liveKickDelayMs` after every turn end, so an unattended halt is caught without anyone reopening the session.

## Install

Installed from a git tag of this repository — it is not published to npm. Replace `<version>` with a released version (tags are named `dsh-continue-kicker-v<version>`; see [the tag list](https://github.com/chrisjohnson/dsh-plugins/tags)):

```sh
dsh plugin --profile web add "git+https://github.com/chrisjohnson/dsh-plugins.git#dsh-continue-kicker-v<version>&path:/packages/continue-kicker"
```

That installs the package into the profile and enables its bundle. If you manage the profile's `package.json` yourself, the pnpm equivalent is below — then also add `dsh-continue-kicker` to the profile's `dsh.profile.bundles`, because `pnpm add` alone installs the plugin without enabling it:

```sh
pnpm add "git+https://github.com/chrisjohnson/dsh-plugins.git#dsh-continue-kicker-v<version>&path:/packages/continue-kicker"
```

> **Warning:** never `pnpm add dsh-continue-kicker` (or `dsh plugin add dsh-continue-kicker`) by bare name. That resolves from the npm registry, where an unscoped `dsh-*` name may belong to an unrelated author and is **not** this plugin.

Restart dsh. With no configuration it works with the defaults below.

## Configuration

Set these on the plugin's row in your own profile patch (`config:` block). **A top-level row with a `config:` block replaces the whole config object**, so list every key you want to differ from the default in the same row; unlisted keys fall back to the defaults below. The bundle's own layer carries no config for the same reason.

| Key | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `cooldownMs` | `60000` | Minimum time between kicks for the same session. |
| `liveKickDelayMs` | `3000` | Delay between a live turn end and the tail re-analysis. Lets a fast manual recovery land first. |
| `maxConsecutiveKicks` | `5` | Runaway guard: after this many kicks (all flavors together, counted from the session's event log) with no normally completed turn and no genuine user message in between, the plugin stops kicking that session and logs an error. `0` disables kicking entirely, quietly (the `kickOn*` flags are the finer-grained off switches). |
| `kickOnInterrupted` | `true` | Kick crash-orphaned turns. |
| `kickOnMaxTokens` | `true` | Kick output-token-limit halts. |
| `kickOnEmptyCompletion` | `true` | Kick reasoning-only completed turns. |
| `kickOnError` | `false` | Kick turns that ended with `reason.kind: 'error'`. Off by default because blindly retrying a failing backend can loop; the runaway guard and cooldown bound it. You would want it for unattended work on a backend that drops now and then (a gateway restart, a network blip): the session resumes by itself once the backend is back instead of sitting dead until someone notices. |
| `includeSubagents` | `false` | Also kick delegated child sessions (`origin: subagent` or `delegationDepth > 0`). Off by default: auto-kicking a child fights the parent's own delegation and retry flow. |
| `logToStderr` | `false` | Write this plugin's log lines to stderr (see Logging). Needed to see them at all on dsh 0.2.0-rc.2. |
| `emptyCompletionMinReasoningChars` | `500` | Reasoning length below which a content-empty completed turn is left alone. |
| `interruptedKickText` | built in | Text sent for an interrupted turn. |
| `maxTokensKickText` | built in | Text sent for a max-tokens halt. Forbids re-deriving the lost reasoning; a plain "please continue" invites another long think straight back into the wall. |
| `emptyCompletionKickText` | built in | Text sent for a reasoning-only empty stop. |
| `errorKickText` | built in | Text sent for a failed turn when `kickOnError` is on. |

Resolution lives in [`src/config.mjs`](./src/config.mjs) and is [tested](./test/config.test.mjs). An unknown key, a string where a number belongs, or an empty text prints one warning at boot and falls back to the default.

Example row (the default for `maxConsecutiveKicks` is 5; 3 here is just an example):

```yaml
- id: continue-kicker
  name: dsh-continue-kicker
  config:
    cooldownMs: 60000
    liveKickDelayMs: 3000
    maxConsecutiveKicks: 3
    kickOnInterrupted: true
    kickOnMaxTokens: true
    kickOnEmptyCompletion: true
    kickOnError: true
    includeSubagents: false
    logToStderr: true
```

## Which turn-end reasons kick

From `TurnEndReasonMap` in `@deepseek-ai/dsh-session`:

| `reason.kind` | Meaning | Kicked? |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `max-tokens` | output budget hit | yes, `kickOnMaxTokens` |
| `interrupted` | crash-orphaned turn closed on load | yes, `kickOnInterrupted` |
| `completed` | model stopped itself | only a reasoning-only empty one, `kickOnEmptyCompletion` |
| `error` | the turn failed (`error` holds message and code) | yes, only with `kickOnError` |
| `aborted` | cancelled on purpose (`user`, `parent`, `hook`, `disposed`, `legacy`) | never |
| `blocked` | a step was rejected before running | never |
| `forked` | fork-seed marker, never emitted live | never |

## The runaway guard

A kick can itself end in the same halt, so the plugin counts kicks and stops at `maxConsecutiveKicks`.

The count is derived from the session's own event log on every analysis, not kept in memory, so it survives a dsh restart and the live and reopen paths always agree. It is the number of this plugin's kick messages (source kind `plugin:continue-kicker`; the retired bare `plugin` kind counts only when it names this plugin and carries one of the known kick texts) found walking back from the end of the log, up to the nearest reset signal:

- a **genuine user message**: source kind `user` and nothing else. The plugin's own kicks and any other producer's user-role messages (goals, other plugins) neither reset nor count.
- a turn that **completed normally**. A reasoning-only completion is a kickable halt, not progress, so it does not reset.

Every flavor counts together: max-tokens, empty-completion, error and interrupted. So the cap also bounds a crash loop: a session that keeps getting killed mid-turn and resumed stops being resumed after `maxConsecutiveKicks` kicks until a user message or a completed turn arrives. At the cap the plugin logs an error naming the session ("needs human attention") and does not kick. Only the cooldown timestamp is in memory; a restart forgets it, which at worst allows one extra kick that the stateless cap still bounds.

Changed from 0.1.0: the old reset fired only when a genuine user message was the *last* event, but a halted turn always ends in `turn/end`, so a new prompt after the cap never reset it; the count lived in memory and was lost on restart; and interrupted kicks were not counted at all.

The kick is written with source kind `plugin:continue-kicker`. Session format V4 refuses the bare kind `plugin`, so a session carrying such a message could not be reopened after a restart.

## Logging

Every decision, kick or skip, is logged with its reason, through the host logger under the name `continue-kicker`.

**Where those lines go (dsh 0.2.0-rc.2):** nowhere you can read. The harness registers no console or file exporter on the logger; plugin lines only land in an in-memory ring buffer (`ctx.logger.buffer`, 1000 entries) that nothing displays, and only startup warnings and errors are surfaced, inside a startup failure. So `journalctl -u dsh | grep continue-kicker` finds nothing by default. Set `logToStderr: true` and the plugin registers its own exporter that writes only its own lines to stderr, which a service manager (journald under systemd) captures:

```
2026-10-15T18:28:05.590Z INFO continue-kicker created: kicked session s1 (flavor=max-tokens, consecutive=1)
```

The kick itself is also visible in the conversation as a notice row ("Auto-resumed after a max-tokens halt (2/5)"), but the "needs human attention" error at the cap appears only in the log. A general fix (surface plugin logs in the harness) belongs upstream or in a separate plugin.

## Compatibility

Requires dsh 0.2.0-rc.2 or later. Declared in `package.json` under `engines.dsh` and on every `@deepseek-ai/dsh*` peer as `>=0.2.0-rc.2 <0.3.0-0 || >=0.3.0-0`. dsh checks these ranges itself, counting prereleases, so it accepts every harness build from 0.2.0-rc.2 on; on a harness outside them `dsh plugin add` refuses the install, and a profile that already has it skips the bundle with a log line. pnpm's own peer check is narrower: it admits only `0.2.0-rc.*` and `0.3.0-*` prereleases (plus every stable release from 0.2.0), so on other prereleases it reports a peer mismatch that dsh does not.

## Development

```sh
node --test packages/continue-kicker/test/*.test.mjs   # decisions + config
node scripts/verify.mjs --package dsh-continue-kicker  # release contract
node scripts/compose-smoke.mjs continue-kicker         # real dsh composition
```

`src/decide.mjs` and `src/config.mjs` import nothing from dsh; `src/host.mjs` is the thin Cordis wiring. See [`../../docs/authoring.md`](../../docs/authoring.md).

## License

MIT

```sh
dsh plugin --profile web add "git+https://github.com/chrisjohnson/dsh-plugins.git#dsh-better-git-worktree-v0.1.1&path:/packages/better-git-worktree"
```

Each package's README is the contract: what it does, every configuration key and what happens when it is unset, how it fails, how to install it, and how to run its checks. Nothing important lives only here.

## Releases

1. A release is a normal pull request that bumps one package's version and moves its CHANGELOG `Unreleased` entry under that version.
2. After it merges, the tag `<package>-v<version>` is cut on that merge commit and pushed. Nothing is committed directly to `main`.
3. Consumers pin the tag with the install spec above. A tag is never moved or rewritten once pushed.

Details: [docs/releasing.md](./docs/releasing.md).

## What "a plugin from this repo" means

- **Plain ESM, no build step.** `git clone && npm test` works with nothing installed. No bundler, no TypeScript layer, no generated client — what the harness loads is what is in `src/`.
- **Every plugin declares `dsh.bundle.patch`**, so one command installs *and* activates it; nothing here needs a hand-edited `cordis.yml`.
- **Deployment-specific values are configuration, never defaults.** A plugin that "works on my machine" because it hard-codes my provider ids is broken for everyone else. `node scripts/verify.mjs` fails the build on author-local paths and provider ids.
- **Nothing is required to be configured.** Optional features report themselves unavailable and name the key that enables them, instead of throwing at boot or failing at first use.
- **Every decision worth testing lives in a module that imports nothing from dsh**, which is what makes the tests real rather than decorative.

## Checking this repository

```sh
npm run check          # verify + hook gate + all tests, no install needed
node scripts/verify.mjs            # the release contract (see below)
node scripts/compose-smoke.mjs     # install into a throwaway profile, import, compose
```

`scripts/verify.mjs` is the interesting one: it enforces the rules that make a plugin installable and trustworthy — `dsh.bundle.patch` present and loading the package by name, `dsh.client` matched by an `./client` export, one harness peer range across every package (`>=0.2.0-rc.2 <0.3.0-0 || >=0.3.0-0`; dsh checks it with prereleases included, while plain node-semver/pnpm admit only `0.2.0-rc.*` and `0.3.0-*` prereleases from it), every shipped file inside the `files` allowlist (all a git-tag install ships), a git-tag install line (and no bare-name one) in every package README, every config key documented in its README, every package listed in the index above, and no deployment leakage. It runs on CI for every push and it runs on a bare clone.

## Contributing

Issues and pull requests are welcome — see [CONTRIBUTING.md](./CONTRIBUTING.md). If you are an agent working in this repository, read [AGENTS.md](./AGENTS.md) first; it is short and it exists because these plugins run with your user's credentials.

For how these plugins get developed, tested against a live harness, released and consumed by the deployment they came from, see [docs/testing.md](./docs/testing.md) and [docs/releasing.md](./docs/releasing.md).

evidence.readmeExcerpt: # dsh-image-search-searxng **Give the agent image search against a SearXNG you already run — and give the user the pictures inline.** A single model-facing `image_search` tool for [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness), pointed at the `images` category of your own [SearXNG](https://docs.searxng.org/) instance. No API key vendor, no third party in the request path, nothing leaves your network that you did not already let SearXNG reach. ``` You: find a wiring diagram for a NEMA 14-50 receptacle Agent: [image_search] → 3 results, each a markdown image link GUI: renders them as real inline pictures ``` ## Install Installed from a git tag of this repository — it is not published to npm. Replace `` with a released version (tags are named `dsh-image-search-searxng-v`; see [the tag list](https://github.com/chrisjohnson/dsh-plugins/tags)): ```sh dsh plugin --profile web add "git+https://github.com/chrisjohnson/dsh-plugins.git#dsh-image-search-searxng-v&path:/packages/image-search-searxng" ``` That installs the package into the profile and enables its bundle. If you manage the profile's `package.json` yourself, the pnpm equivalent is below — then also add `dsh-image-search-searxng` to the profile's `dsh.profile.bundles`, because `pnpm add` alone installs the plugin without enabling it: ```sh pnpm add "git+https://github.com/chrisjohnson/dsh-plugins.git#dsh-image-search-searxng-v&path:/packages/image-search-searxng" ``` > **Warning:** never install this plugin by bare name from the npm registry. Nothing from this repository is published there, so whatever a bare `pnpm add dsh-image-search-searxng` resolves to — now or later — is not this plugin. (The sibling name `dsh-model-switch` is already taken on npm by an unrelated author.) Restart dsh. The tool is then available to every agent preset — the bundle's patch layer mounts the plugin at the profile level, so no per-preset `agent.cordis.yml` editing is involved. Zero configuration is required if your SearXNG answers on `http://localhost:8888`. ## Configuration | Key | Environment | Default | What it does | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `baseURL` | `SEARXNG_BASE_URL` | `http://localhost:8888` | Where your SearXNG lives. Trailing slashes are trimmed; a value that is not an `http(s)` URL is rejected at boot rather than failing at the first search. | | `apiKey` | `SEARXNG_API_KEY` | — | Sent as `preference[api_key]`, for SearXNG instances with API support enabled. | | `maxResults` | `SEARXNG_NUM_RESULTS` | `8` | Default result count the model gets if it does not ask. A per-call `maxResults` argument still wins, clamped to 1–30. | Precedence is **config → environment → default**. To override in your profile patch, add the keys to the row this plugin inserts: ```yaml - id: image-search-searxng name: dsh-image-search-searxng config: baseURL: http://searxng.internal:8080 maxResults: 5 ``` If the plugin is already mounted by its bundle, a config-only row keyed by `id` is enough, and `!!js` lets the row pass environment variables through. Unset variables arrive as `undefined` and fall back exactly as an absent key would: ```yaml - id: image-search-searxng config: baseURL: !!js process.env.SEARXNG_BASE_URL ``` One caveat worth knowing about patch layers generally: a patch **replaces a row's entire `config` object**, it does not deep-merge. Restating `baseURL` in a later layer drops `apiKey` unless you restate that too — which is why this plugin ships its row with no `config` block at all and resolves defaults in code. ## What the model actually receives Titles, source pages, resolutions, and one markdown image link per result: ``` 1. **NEMA 14-50 wiring** ![NEMA 14-50 wiring](https://example.com/diagram.png) Source: https://example.com/receptacles Resolution: 1024x768 ``` The tool's canonical value is `{ results: [{ title?, imgSrc, sourceUrl, resolution? }] }`, and its model-facing result is that list rendered as a single `text` content block — no `image` blocks, no attachments. The plugin writes no session messages of its own. That link is not decoration. dsh's own `dsh-client-ui-primitives` renderer turns `![alt](url)` into a real `` for any `http(s)` URL — there is no domain allowlist — and falls back to alt text only when the browser's own image request fails (hotlink protection, dead link). So results appear as pictures whenever the source host cooperates, with no code-level distinction between the two cases. The tool description tells the model to copy the links verbatim precisely because rewriting one into a plain `[text](url)` link removes the picture. ## Why a separate tool instead of extending `web_search` Because the shared web seam has nowhere to put an image. `WebSearchRequest` and `WebSearchSource` in `@deepseek-ai/dsh-web` carry no category and no image fields, so adding them means patching multiple upstream packages that every future dsh upgrade would then have to be re-verified against. A standalone tool with its own schema costs one registration and stays working across upgrades. This is the same shape `dsh-web-search-searxng` chose. ## What this plugin deliberately does not do - **It does not show the model the images.** The model receives text: titles and URLs. It cannot describe, compare, or verify what is depicted, and the tool description says so in as many words, because "I looked at the diagram and it shows…" is otherwise a very tempting hallucination. - **It does not fetch images through your model's attachment pipeline.** Real image *attachments* would route arbitrary third-party URLs through the vision/attachment path — a much larger blast radius than "the user can see search results" warrants. - **It does not fall back to a hosted search API.** If SearXNG is unreachable the tool call fails with the HTTP status, rather than silently querying somebody else's service. ## Compatibility Requires dsh 0.2.0-rc.2 or later. evidence.readmeExcerpt:
# dsh-loop-watchdog

**A stuck-session signal for agents you leave running — an audit ledger first, an intervention only if you ask for one.**

A host plugin for [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) that checks a session before each agent step and writes one record per check saying whether it looks stuck, with the evidence. It ships a panel (for `dsh-better-sidebar`) that draws that ledger for the current session.

Precision over recall. A false positive tells a working agent to abandon its strategy; a false negative costs a few minutes. So the watchdog is built around evidence that cannot hallucinate, and what it does about a verdict is off until you turn it on.

| Layer | What it does | Cost |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Repetition check** (deterministic) | Hashes `(tool, normalised arguments)` over the last `fpWindowEvents` events. The same call repeated with *no new information* is stuck: 3 or more repeats with at most one distinct result, or 5 or more with at most two. | No model call. |
| **Model adjudication** (optional) | For windows the first layer did not settle, asks a model you configure whether the last few steps produced **new information** (a new file read, a new error, a result that differs) or re-ran work that already failed. It answers `LOOP:N` or `PROGRESS:N`. | One small completion, at most once per `cooldownMs`, skipped while the previous one was slow. |
| **Intervention** (off by default) | In the *stuck* band, sustained over two consecutive checks, in act mode, once per stuck episode: steers one non-destructive note into the session asking the agent to state what it has established and take the cheapest check that could falsify its approach. | One message. |

Similar-looking commands with new results are progress; the same command returning the same nothing is a loop. That distinction is the whole design.

## Install

Installed from a git tag of this repository — it is not published to npm. Replace `<version>` with a released version (tags are named `dsh-loop-watchdog-v<version>`; see [the tag list](https://github.com/chrisjohnson/dsh-plugins/tags)):

```sh
dsh plugin --profile web add "git+https://github.com/chrisjohnson/dsh-plugins.git#dsh-loop-watchdog-v<version>&path:/packages/loop-watchdog"
```

That installs the package into the profile and enables its bundle. If you manage the profile's `package.json` yourself, the pnpm equivalent is below — then also add `dsh-loop-watchdog` to the profile's `dsh.profile.bundles`, because `pnpm add` alone installs the plugin without enabling it:

```sh
pnpm add "git+https://github.com/chrisjohnson/dsh-plugins.git#dsh-loop-watchdog-v<version>&path:/packages/loop-watchdog"
```

> **Warning:** never `pnpm add dsh-loop-watchdog` (or `dsh plugin add dsh-loop-watchdog`) by bare name. That resolves from the npm registry, where an unscoped `dsh-*` name can belong to an unrelated author and is **not** this plugin.

Restart dsh. With no configuration the repetition check runs, every check is ledgered, and nothing intervenes. Model adjudication stays off until you give it an endpoint and a model (below), and the boot log says so.

## Configuration

Set these on the row in your own profile patch (`config:` block). **A patch layer replaces a row's whole `config` object**, so a row that sets one key must restate every key it wants to differ from the default.

| Key | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `interventionEnabled` | `false` | Whether to steer a sustained-stuck session. Log-only by default. The [mode file](#the-mode-file) overrides this at runtime. |
| `llmBaseUrl` | *unset* | Base URL of an OpenAI-compatible API; `/chat/completions` is appended. **Unset (or `llmModel` unset) turns model adjudication off**: the repetition check still runs, and ambiguous windows are ledgered as skipped (`no-llm`). |
| `llmModel` | *unset* | Model id sent to that endpoint. |
| `llmApiKeyEnv` | *unset* | The **name** of the environment variable that holds the API key — never the key. Read at call time. Unset, or an empty variable, sends no `Authorization` header (the boot log warns for the empty case). |
| `llmExtraBody` | `{}` | Extra fields merged under the request body, for a backend-specific switch — for example `chat_template_kwargs: {enable_thinking: false}` to stop a thinking model reasoning before a one-line answer. The fixed fields (`model`, `max_tokens`, `temperature: 0`, `messages`) win. |
| `llmMaxTokens` | `128` | Completion budget for the one-line verdict. |
| `ledgerFile` | `$DSH_HOME/storages/loop-watchdog/evaluations.jsonl` | The [evaluation ledger](#the-ledger). Always written. A relative value resolves against `$DSH_HOME`. |
| `modeFile` | `$DSH_HOME/storages/loop-watchdog/mode.json` | The runtime act/log override. This plugin only reads it. A relative value resolves against `$DSH_HOME`. |
| `cooldownMs` | `30000` | Minimum gap between two evaluations of one session. |
| `maxTranscriptLines` | `6` | Substantive events shown to the model (and recorded in the ledger window). |
| `fpWindowEvents` | `60` | Raw events the repetition check scans (~15 tool calls). |
| `watchdogTimeoutMs` | `25000` | Abort a model call after this long. The check fails open. |
| `busyYieldMs` | `15000` | After a model call slower than this, the next model check is skipped so the watchdog does not compete with the session it supervises. |
| `bandStuck` / `bandWatch` | `90` / `70` | Confidence thresholds for the `stuck` (actionable) and `watch` bands, for a `LOOP` verdict. Anything lower, or any `PROGRESS` verdict, is `noise`. |
| `includeSubagents` | `false` | Subagent sessions are skipped unless this is `true`. |
| `logFile` | `true` | Write the verbose stage trail to `logFilePath`. **The trail includes the transcript window sent to the model, so tool output and file contents land in that file by default**; set `false` if the log directory is not as private as the session. |
| `logFilePath` | `$DSH_HOME/storages/loop-watchdog/watchdog.log` | Where that trail goes. Relative values resolve against `$DSH_HOME`. |
| `logConsole` | `false` | Also print the trail to stdout (the journal under systemd). Off because it fires on every step of every session. |
| `logDsh` | `false` | Send the trail to dsh's own logger. |
| `logDshErrors` | `true` | Keep genuine errors on dsh's logger even when `logDsh` is off. |

`$DSH_HOME` is the environment variable when set (blank counts as unset), else `~/.dsh`, resolved the way the harness resolves it (a leading `~` expands). Every path key accepts an absolute path (used verbatim), a `~` path, or a path **relative to `$DSH_HOME`** — never relative to the working directory. `watchdogTimeoutMs` and `llmMaxTokens` must be above zero. A `llmBaseUrl` with a query string warns, and the logged endpoint never carries credentials or a query. Resolution lives in [`src/config.mjs`](./src/config.mjs) and is [tested](./test/config.test.mjs); a misspelled key, a YAML `"30000"`, a base URL that is not http(s), or a model with no endpoint each print one warning at boot.

Example, on a deployment with a local OpenAI-compatible gateway:

```yaml
- id: loop-watchdog
  name: dsh-loop-watchdog
  config:
    llmBaseUrl: http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1
    llmModel: small-model
    llmApiKeyEnv: GATEWAY_API_KEY
    llmExtraBody:
      chat_template_kwargs:
        enable_thinking: false
    interventionEnabled: false
```

## The ledger

Every evaluation appends one JSON line to `ledgerFile` (schema `v: 2`), carrying both layers:

- `code` — the repetition check's full result, including "ran, scanned N calls, found nothing", which decides nothing and would otherwise leave no trace;
- `model` — the model's verdict, present only when the first layer was inconclusive and the model was consulted;
- `verdict`, `confidence`, `band`, `streak`, `mode`, `outcome` (`logged`, `intervened`, `intervene-error`, `skipped`), the matched `fingerprints`, latency, and the exact transcript `window` that was judged.

Steps deliberately not evaluated are recorded too, but **only the first of a stretch** (a stretch of a different kind in between, such as a cooldown, starts a new one), so the ledger does not gain a row every few seconds: `no-signal` (fewer than two substantive events), `cooldown`, `busy` (the previous model check was slow), and `no-llm` (nothing left to ask). A real evaluation ends the stretch.

### Existing history: pointing at the old locations

The defaults above are this package's own directory. A deployment that already ran the original in-tree watchdog has history and a mode toggle elsewhere, and **without the mapping the watchdog starts a new empty ledger and ignores the old toggle**. Either set the keys (relative to `$DSH_HOME`):

```yaml
    ledgerFile: storages/semantic-loop-kicker/evaluations.jsonl
    modeFile: profiles/web/watchdog-mode.json
```

or move the old data once — `mv $DSH_HOME/storages/semantic-loop-kicker $DSH_HOME/storages/loop-watchdog` (the file inside keeps its name, `evaluations.jsonl`) — and leave the keys unset. Remove the old in-tree rows in the same change: two watchers appending to one ledger would double every record.

The file is the interface. Anything may read it; the evals panel is one reader. Older `v: 1` (decisions-only) lines stay readable: the reader normalises them into the current shape. The watchdog never rotates or truncates it.

## The mode file

`interventionEnabled` is the default. Whatever UI or script you like can override it at runtime by writing `modeFile`:

```json
{ "interventionEnabled": true }
```

The file is read on **every check**, so a toggle takes effect within one cooldown window, no restart. Absent, unreadable, or without a boolean `interventionEnabled` means "no override". This plugin never writes the file and ships no toggle UI of its own.

## The evals panel

The same package serves a read-only view of the ledger to a `dsh-better-sidebar` tab, "Loop evals": a timing graph with a code lane, a model lane and a dim skip lane, a synced ledger list, and a detail view of one evaluation (fingerprint groups, the model's raw reply, latency, the transcript window). It defaults to the current session, with a toggle for all.

`dsh-better-sidebar` is an **optional** integration. The panel module declares that service as a requirement, so without better-sidebar installed it stays inactive and registers nothing; the watchdog and its ledger are unaffected. It uses better-sidebar 0.25.0's `ctx.betterSidebar.registerTab(descriptor)`, whose registration is disposed with this plugin's fiber. The panel reads the ledger through a plugin-owned route, `/loopWatchdog/<list|sessions|detail>`, behind the connection service's trust check.

## Session format V4

Dsh 0.2.0 sessions are format V4, and the watchdog reads V4 events: a `user/message` event's `data` **is** the message; a `tool/result` event's `data.message` is a first-class `{role: 'tool', toolCallId, content}` message, whose text is its content blocks. The steering note is written with source kind `plugin:loop-watchdog` — V4 refuses the bare kind `plugin` on read, so a session carrying such a message could not be reopened after a restart.

## Failure modes

- **Fails open, always.** A model timeout, HTTP error or unparseable reply yields no verdict (band `noise`) and the turn proceeds. A thrown error is logged and never reaches the agent loop; the `agent/pre-step` listener awaits the waterfall first and runs the check without blocking it.
- **No model configured:** the repetition check still decides on its own; ambiguous windows are ledgered as `no-llm`.
- **Ledger or log not writable:** writes are best effort and silently skipped; the agent is never affected.
- **A model that reasons before answering** may spend `llmMaxTokens` on thinking and return nothing; pass the backend's switch in `llmExtraBody`.

## Compatibility

Requires dsh 0.2.0-rc.2 or later. Declared in `package.json` under `engines.dsh` and on the `@deepseek-ai/dsh-llm` peer as `>=0.2.0-rc.2 <0.3.0-0 || >=0.3.0-0`. dsh checks these ranges itself, counting prereleases; pnpm's own peer check is narrower and may report a mismatch on other prereleases that dsh does not.

## Troubleshooting

**Nothing is ever ledgered.** The ledger needs at least two substantive events and a clear cooldown. Check `logFilePath` for `[B]` lines: `skip … only N substantive events` or `COOLDOWN_SKIP` say why.

**Every ambiguous window is a `no-llm` skip.** Model adjudication is off. The boot log names the keys: `llmBaseUrl` and `llmModel`.

**The panel tab is missing.** `dsh-better-sidebar` is not installed or not yet loaded. Check the browser console for a `loop-watchdog` line, and that better-sidebar's own tab bar works.

**The panel says "ledger-missing".** The watchdog has not written yet, or the panel and the host disagree on `ledgerFile` — they read the same row's config, so check that the path exists and is writable by the dsh user.

## Development

Plain ESM, no build step:

```sh
node --test packages/loop-watchdog/test/*.test.mjs    # decisions, reading V4 events, ledger, config, client contract
node scripts/verify.mjs --package dsh-loop-watchdog   # release contract
node scripts/compose-smoke.mjs loop-watchdog          # real dsh composition
node scripts/check-plugin-hooks.mjs                   # React hook-order gate for the client half
```

`src/decide.mjs`, `src/summarize.mjs`, `src/ledger.mjs` and `src/config.mjs` hold every decision worth testing and import nothing from dsh. `src/host.mjs` is the Cordis wiring; `src/client.mjs` is the browser half. The tests that need `@deepseek-ai/dsh-llm` (the host wiring, parity with the harness's own constructors) skip on a bare clone. See [`../../docs/authoring.md`](../../docs/authoring.md).

## License

MIT

# dsh-plugins

Public [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) plugins by [Chris Johnson](https://github.com/chrisjohnson). One repository, independently installable plugins — each with its own README, its own tests, its own changelog and its own version.

## Install

**Nothing here is published to npm.** Every release is a git tag on this repository, named `<package>-v<version>` (for example `dsh-model-switch-v0.2.1`), and you install a plugin by pinning that tag plus the package's subdirectory:

```sh
dsh plugin --profile web add "git+https://github.com/chrisjohnson/dsh-plugins.git#<package>-v<version>&path:/packages/<dir>"
```

`dsh plugin add` hands that spec to pnpm and also lists the package under the profile's `dsh.profile.bundles`, which is what activates its configuration layer. If you manage a profile's `package.json` yourself, the same spec works with pnpm directly — but then add the package name to `dsh.profile.bundles` by hand, because a plain `pnpm add` installs the plugin without enabling it:

```sh
pnpm add "git+https://github.com/chrisjohnson/dsh-plugins.git#<package>-v<version>&path:/packages/<dir>"
```

Pick the tag from [the repository's tags](https://github.com/chrisjohnson/dsh-plugins/tags); `<dir>` is the folder under `packages/` in the index below.

> **Warning — do not install these by bare name.** `pnpm add dsh-model-switch` (or `dsh plugin add dsh-model-switch`) resolves against the npm registry, and the npm package called `dsh-model-switch` belongs to an unrelated author: it is **not** this plugin. The same can happen to any unscoped `dsh-*` name. Always use the git-tag spec above.

## Index

| Plugin | What it is for | Latest | Directory |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **[dsh-model-switch](./packages/model-switch/)** | Let the agent switch its own model mid-session, with a context-window fit guard so neither it nor a human in the composer can strand a conversation on a model too small to read it. | 0.2.1 | `packages/model-switch` |
| **[dsh-image-search-searxng](./packages/image-search-searxng/)** | A model-facing `image_search` tool over your own SearXNG, rendered inline in the Web GUI. | 0.2.0 | `packages/image-search-searxng` |
| **[dsh-continue-kicker](./packages/continue-kicker/)** | Automatically send "continue" when a turn halts on the output-token limit (or after a crash, or on a reasoning-only empty stop), with a runaway guard that stops after repeated kicks with no progress. | 0.2.0 | `packages/continue-kicker` |
| **[dsh-loop-watchdog](./packages/loop-watchdog/)** | Detect an agent stuck in a loop before each step (a deterministic repetition check plus an optional model judge), keep an audit ledger of every check, optionally steer the session, and chart the ledger in a `dsh-better-sidebar` panel. | 0.1.0 | `packages/loop-watchdog` |
| **[dsh-scheduled-queue](./packages/scheduled-queue/)** | Schedule the composer's draft to be sent to its own session later, with a per-session dock to edit, cancel or send now. Runs alongside the official schedule bundle. | 0.1.0 | `packages/scheduled-queue` |
| **[dsh-better-git-worktree](./packages/better-git-worktree/)** | Run a session in its own self-contained git working copy: a composer Worktree switch, a `worktree_convert` tool, session-list status badges, a header menu, and an archive prompt that decides the working copy's fate. | 0.1.1 | `packages/better-git-worktree` |

Install lines for the latest release of each package:

```sh
dsh plugin --profile web add "git+https://github.com/chrisjohnson/dsh-plugins.git#dsh-model-switch-v0.2.1&path:/packages/model-switch"
dsh plugin --profile web add "git+https://github.com/chrisjohnson/dsh-plugins.git#dsh-image-search-searxng-v0.2.0&path:/packages/image-search-searxng"
dsh plugin --profile web add "git+https://github.com/chrisjohnson/dsh-plugins.git#dsh-continue-kicker-v0.2.0&path:/packages/continue-kicker"
dsh plugin --profile web add "git+https://github.com/chrisjohnson/dsh-plugins.git#dsh-loop-watchdog-v0.1.0&path:/packages/loop-watchdog"
dsh plugin --profile web add "git+https://github.com/chrisjohnson/dsh-plugins.git#dsh-scheduled-queue-v0.1.0&path:/packages/scheduled-queue"
dsh plugin --profile web add "git+https://github.com/chrisjohnson/dsh-plugins.git#dsh-better-git-worktree-v0.1.1&path:/packages/better-git-worktree"
```

Each package's README is the contract: what it does, every configuration key and what happens when it is unset, how it fails, how to install it, and how to run its checks. Nothing important lives only here.

## Releases

1. A release is a normal pull request that bumps one package's version and moves its CHANGELOG `Unreleased` entry under that version.
2. After it merges, the tag `<package>-v<version>` is cut on that merge commit and pushed. Nothing is committed directly to `main`.
3. Consumers pin the tag with the install spec above. A tag is never moved or rewritten once pushed.

Details: [docs/releasing.md](./docs/releasing.md).

## What "a plugin from this repo" means

- **Plain ESM, no build step.** `git clone && npm test` works with nothing installed. No bundler, no TypeScript layer, no generated client — what the harness loads is what is in `src/`.
- **Every plugin declares `dsh.bundle.patch`**, so one command installs *and* activates it; nothing here needs a hand-edited `cordis.yml`.
- **Deployment-specific values are configuration, never defaults.** A plugin that "works on my machine" because it hard-codes my provider ids is broken for everyone else. `node scripts/verify.mjs` fails the build on author-local paths and provider ids.
- **Nothing is required to be configured.** Optional features report themselves unavailable and name the key that enables them, instead of throwing at boot or failing at first use.
- **Every decision worth testing lives in a module that imports nothing from dsh**, which is what makes the tests real rather than decorative.

## Checking this repository

```sh
npm run check          # verify + hook gate + all tests, no install needed
node scripts/verify.mjs            # the release contract (see below)
node scripts/compose-smoke.mjs     # install into a throwaway profile, import, compose
```

`scripts/verify.mjs` is the interesting one: it enforces the rules that make a plugin installable and trustworthy — `dsh.bundle.patch` present and loading the package by name, `dsh.client` matched by an `./client` export, one harness peer range across every package (`>=0.2.0-rc.2 <0.3.0-0 || >=0.3.0-0`; dsh checks it with prereleases included, while plain node-semver/pnpm admit only `0.2.0-rc.*` and `0.3.0-*` prereleases from it), every shipped file inside the `files` allowlist (all a git-tag install ships), a git-tag install line (and no bare-name one) in every package README, every config key documented in its README, every package listed in the index above, and no deployment leakage. It runs on CI for every push and it runs on a bare clone.

## Contributing

Issues and pull requests are welcome — see [CONTRIBUTING.md](./CONTRIBUTING.md). If you are an agent working in this repository, read [AGENTS.md](./AGENTS.md) first; it is short and it exists because these plugins run with your user's credentials.

For how these plugins get developed, tested against a live harness, released and consumed by the deployment they came from, see [docs/testing.md](./docs/testing.md) and [docs/releasing.md](./docs/releasing.md).

## License

MIT — see [LICENSE](./LICENSE).

# dsh-model-switch

**Let the agent change its own model mid-session — and make it impossible to strand the conversation on a model too small to read it.**

Two tools and two interface surfaces for [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness), built for deployments that route the same session across models with wildly different context windows (a 1M-token cloud route and a 262k local one, say):

| What | Who | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `switch_model` tool | agent | Moves this session to `provider/model` and sends it a self-contained handoff message. Full history carries over. |
| `switch_model_escalate` tool | agent | "I'm stuck" escape hatch to a route **you** designate. The model does not choose the destination — deployment policy does. |
| Context badge | human | Appears beside the composer's model picker the moment the routed model cannot hold the session — amber `210k / 262.1k — compacts at 209.7k`, or red `300k > 262.1k — won't fit`. Its tooltip lists the routes that still fit, and clicking it is how you open the repair panel below. |
| Repair panel | human | Collapsed by default, because past the auto-compact line nothing fails: the next request compacts on the route that can still read it. Click the badge for one-click repair — move to a route that can read the transcript, compact there, return. The one case that cannot wait for a click (past the route's own window, where the next request 400s and overflow recovery summarises with the route that just overflowed) opens itself once. |

The guard applies to the agent's tools **and** the human's picker. It has to be in both places, for a reason that is not obvious: the composer calls `sessionController.selectModel` directly and cannot be intercepted, so the interactive path is warned-and-repaired rather than blocked.

## Why this exists

A real session, 2026-09-28. It had run to ~421k tokens on a route with a 1,048,576-token window. The user switched it to a local model with a 262,144-token window and sent one message:

```
attempt 1  → Request timed out.
attempt 2  → 400 ContextWindowExceededError: request (420948 tokens)
             exceeds the available context size (262144 tokens)
compaction/start   ← the harness classified it and started overflow recovery
compaction/end     ← error: the same 400, at 421,300 tokens
retry              → same 400 → surfaced to the user
```

Two harness behaviours combine to make that unrecoverable:

1. The pre-step pressure gate resolves its target from the **last minted request**, which right after a switch is still the *old* model — so the threshold it compares against is 0.8 × 1,048,576, nothing compacts, and the first request on the new, smaller route is structurally unguarded.
2. Overflow recovery summarizes with the **route that just overflowed**. The rescue call had to push 421k tokens through a 262k model.

A model must *read* a conversation in order to summarize it. That is a physical ceiling, not a tuning problem: the only moment a 421k session can be condensed is while a big-window model is still routed. Hence the rule this plugin enforces — **compact to fit before switching, and refuse with actionable numbers when even that is impossible.**

Every number in the refusal messages is deliberate. A model told "cannot switch" tries again; a model told "delegate this to a local subagent, or pick a larger-window route, here are the token counts" stops burning turns on it.

## Install

Installed from a git tag of this repository — it is not published to npm. Replace `<version>` with a released version (tags are named `dsh-model-switch-v<version>`; see [the tag list](https://github.com/chrisjohnson/dsh-plugins/tags)):

```sh
dsh plugin --profile web add "git+https://github.com/chrisjohnson/dsh-plugins.git#dsh-model-switch-v<version>&path:/packages/model-switch"
```

That installs the package into the profile and enables its bundle. If you manage the profile's `package.json` yourself, the pnpm equivalent is below — then also add `dsh-model-switch` to the profile's `dsh.profile.bundles`, because `pnpm add` alone installs the plugin without enabling it:

```sh
pnpm add "git+https://github.com/chrisjohnson/dsh-plugins.git#dsh-model-switch-v<version>&path:/packages/model-switch"
```

> **Warning:** never `pnpm add dsh-model-switch` (or `dsh plugin add dsh-model-switch`) by bare name. That resolves from the npm registry, where the package called `dsh-model-switch` belongs to an unrelated author and is **not** this plugin.

Restart dsh. With no configuration you get `switch_model`, the fit guard, the pill and the banner. `switch_model_escalate` is **not** offered until you designate the escalation route — see below.

## Configuration

Set these on the row in your own profile patch (`config:` block), or via your deployment's equivalent:

| Key | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `escalationProvider` + `escalationModel` | *unset* | Where `switch_model_escalate` hands the session. **Unset means the tool is not registered at all** — a model that cannot see it will not reach for it, which beats a tool whose every call fails. |
| `readerProvider` + `readerModel` | *unset* | A route whose window can read the whole conversation. The one-click repair moves there, compacts, and returns. Without it the repair refuses and says exactly what to configure. |
| `preferredRoutes` | `[reader]` | Ordered `provider/model` recommendations when a conversation outgrows its route. Needed because "smallest window that still fits" often lands on a different provider that merely declares the same number. |
| `fitRatio` | `0.8` | Fraction of a destination window treated as usable. It is dsh-compaction-basic's own default compaction point, so the guard agrees with what the harness would do anyway. |
| `summaryReserveTokens` | `10000` | Room left for the summary checkpoint compaction writes. |
| `autoCompact` | `true` | When `false`, the guard never compacts on its own: a too-big switch is refused with the `/compact` instruction instead. |

Compaction retries are fixed internal limits, not configuration (`maxRegionAttempts` is 8 and `maxCompactionAttempts` is 3; setting either in the row is ignored with an unknown-key warning).

Resolution lives in [`src/config.mjs`](./src/config.mjs) and is [tested](./test/config.test.mjs). It is stricter than most plugins on purpose: a misspelled key, a YAML `"0.8"`, or an escalation provider with no model each print one warning at boot, because a misconfiguration you see once is worth much less debugging than one you discover at the first switch.

Example, on a deployment with a cloud big-window route and a local workhorse:

```yaml
- id: model-switch
  name: dsh-model-switch
  config:
    escalationProvider: cloud
    escalationModel: cloud-frontier
    readerProvider: cloud
    readerModel: cloud-long-context
    preferredRoutes:
      - cloud/cloud-long-context
      - cloud/cloud-frontier
```

## How the guard decides

`switch_model` measures the session (via dsh's replay-based token meter — no model call), resolves the destination window, and picks one of five outcomes in [`src/fit.mjs`](./src/fit.mjs):

| Situation | Outcome |
| --- | --- |
| No measurement, or the destination declares no window | **allow** with a note. The guard never blocks a switch it cannot evaluate. |
| Fits under the margin | **allow** |
| Doesn't fit, and the current route cannot compact it (transcript over `fitRatio` of its window) | **refuse**, with token counts and the delegate-to-subagent alternative |
| Doesn't fit, `autoCompact: false` | **refuse**, with the `/compact` instruction |
| Doesn't fit but is compactable here | **compact first**, re-measure, then allow — reporting how much was freed |

One subtlety that cost a bug each way: the *fit* margin (0.8) decides whether to compact, while "can this route read the transcript" uses the **route's own window**. Using the margin for both meant a session at 85% of its own window was shipped off to another route and back for a compaction it could have done itself.

## Compatibility

Requires dsh 0.2.0-rc.2 or later. Declared in `package.json` under `engines.dsh` and on every `@deepseek-ai/dsh*` peer as `>=0.2.0-rc.2 <0.3.0-0 || >=0.3.0-0`. dsh checks these ranges itself, counting prereleases, so it accepts every harness build from 0.2.0-rc.2 on; on a harness outside them `dsh plugin add` refuses the install, and a profile that already has it skips the bundle with a log line. pnpm's own peer check is narrower: it admits only `0.2.0-rc.*` and `0.3.0-*` prereleases (plus every stable release from 0.2.0), so on other prereleases it reports a peer mismatch that dsh does not.

## Session format

The handoff message this plugin steers into a session after a switch carries
`source: { kind: 'plugin:model-switch', form: 'notice', summary }`. dsh 0.2.0
sessions (format V4) reject the shared `'plugin'` kind on read, so the producer name
lives in `kind`. Sessions written by dsh 0.1.x with the old kind are rewritten to
this same value by dsh's own migrator.

## Troubleshooting

**"switch_model_escalate" is not offered.** Expected until `escalationProvider`/`escalationModel` are set. The boot log says so.

**A switch was refused that should have worked.** Read the numbers in the refusal. If it says the current route cannot read the conversation, that is real: ask for a compact while still on a big-window route, or delegate to a subagent (which starts with a fresh, small context) instead.

**The pill/banner shows nothing.** It needs a *routed request* — a session that has not sent a message yet has no measurement. It also needs the plugin's client half to load: check the browser console for a `slot entry crashed` line naming this plugin.

**The repair button is missing.** Repair needs compaction reachable through `dsh-compaction-basic` (or the `/compact` command). A profile without compaction composed cannot offer it.

## Development

Plain ESM, no build step:

```sh
node --test packages/model-switch/test/*.test.mjs    # fit guard + config resolution
node scripts/verify.mjs --package dsh-model-switch   # release contract
node scripts/compose-smoke.mjs model-switch          # real dsh composition
node scripts/check-plugin-hooks.mjs                  # React hook-order gate for the client half
```

# dsh-scheduled-queue

**Schedule the message in your composer to be sent later, into the same session.**

A composer feature for [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness): type a message, press the clock button beside Send, choose how many minutes from now, and the message is delivered to that session when the time comes — even if the session has been stopped in the meantime, and even if the harness restarts first.

| What | Where | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Clock button | composer, before the Send action | Enabled while the draft has text. Opens a small dialog: send in N minutes, optionally as **force steer**. |
| Scheduled-messages dock | above the composer card | Lists **this session's** scheduled messages with a live countdown. Each row can be edited (text, minutes, force steer — editing restarts the countdown), removed, or sent now. Hidden when the session has none. |
| Delivery | host | A scanner checks for due items; each is sent exactly like a normal composer send. |

A scheduled message is the user's own text. It arrives in the transcript as an ordinary user message (source kind `user`), not as a plugin notice.

## Per-session scope

Both composer slots are scoped to one session window and are handed that session's id. The dock shows, and the host returns, only the items scheduled for that session: a message scheduled in session A is not visible in, and cannot be edited, removed or sent from, session B. A call that does not name a session gets no items back rather than everything.

## Delivery

When an item is due the host calls `sessionController.prompt` with the item's id as the request id — the same call the composer's Send button makes.

- **Normal item** — a follow-up: it runs as its own turn after the current one.
- **Force steer item** — steering: it interrupts the current turn at the next step.
- **Session not running** — the session is resumed first, then the message is delivered.
- **Retries** — a delivery that fails stays queued and is retried with a back-off (5 s, doubling, capped at 5 min). A delivery that gets no answer within `deliveryTimeoutMs` is given up on and counts as a failure, so one hung session cannot hold up the others; the item is retried later. The harness only checks the abort signal before it admits a prompt, so a prompt that was already admitted may still land. The retry then carries the same request id, which `prompt` dedupes on, so it cannot send twice.
- **Session not found** — the harness also reports this transiently (a session disposed while the message was being admitted), so the host asks once more after two seconds. Only if the session is still not found is the item dropped, with a warning that includes the message text (first 500 characters).
- **Rejected by the harness** (`gateway/bad-request`, e.g. empty content) — retrying cannot help, so the item is dropped with a warning that includes its text.
- **Sorting** — due items are delivered oldest-due first.
- **Time zone** — the browser's time zone is stored with the item when it is scheduled and passed as `clientTimeZone`, so time-aware context sees a zone. Only `UTC` and `Area/Location` names are kept (the harness rejects anything else, such as `GMT`, `EST` or `+05:00`); otherwise the field is left off. If the harness still refuses a stored zone, the send is retried once without it. Items without one (queued by earlier versions) are sent without.
- **Disposal** — when the plugin is unloaded the scanner stops, in-flight calls are aborted, and nothing more is sent or written.

## How this differs from the official schedule bundle

dsh 0.2.0 ships an optional `@deepseek-ai/dsh-experimental-schedule-bundle` (rows `time-context`, `schedule`, `ui-schedule`). Both can be enabled together. They solve different problems:

| | `dsh-scheduled-queue` (this) | `@deepseek-ai/dsh-experimental-schedule-bundle` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Who schedules | **You**, from the composer | **The agent**, through tools (`schedule_create`, `schedule_list`, `schedule_update`, `schedule_delete`), and you, from the task page |
| What | One-shot "send this text in N minutes" | One-shot, fixed-rate, daily, weekly and cron reminders with titles and delivery history |
| Surface | Clock button and dock in the composer | Task page, session-row marks, header utilities |
| Storage | `<dsh home>/storages/scheduled-queue.json` | `schedule.json` in the harness's storage domain |

Why both exist: the official bundle is a task manager for recurring and agent-created reminders. This plugin is a "send this later" button on the draft you are looking at, with the pending messages visible beside the composer. Neither replaces the other.

Nothing collides, so no setup is needed to run them side by side. Checked against 0.2.0-rc.2:

- **Plugin rows:** this plugin is `scheduled-queue`; the bundle inserts `time-context`, `schedule`, `ui-schedule`.
- **Tools:** this plugin registers none; the bundle's are `schedule_create`, `schedule_list`, `schedule_update`, `schedule_delete`.
- **Slots:** this plugin uses `conversation.input.right` (id `sq-clock`) and `conversation.input.dock` (id `sq-dock`), both additive list slots. The bundle's client mounts into `conversation.session.header.utilities`, `conversation.chat.turnTail`, `sidebar.*` and `shell.overlay`, not these.
- **Routes:** this plugin owns `/api/scheduledQueue/*`; the bundle's service uses the typed `schedule` remote namespace.
- **Storage:** different files, different formats.
- **Client module id and styles:** `dsh-scheduled-queue`, style tag `sq-styles`, CSS classes `sq-*`.

One practical consequence: a message queued here is not visible to the agent's `schedule_list`, and a reminder created through the bundle does not show in this plugin's dock.

## Replacing the in-tree plugin

If your deployment still carries the earlier copy (dsh-deploy's `.dsh/profiles/web/plugins/scheduled-queue` and its `scheduled-queue` row in `cordis.patch.yml`), remove or keep disabled that row **before** enabling this package. Two plugins would register the same `/api/scheduledQueue/*` routes (the second registration fails) and scan the same queue file. The queue file is shared and compatible, so items already queued carry over.

## Install

Installed from a git tag of this repository — it is not published to npm. Replace `<version>` with a released version (tags are named `dsh-scheduled-queue-v<version>`; see [the tag list](https://github.com/chrisjohnson/dsh-plugins/tags)):

```sh
dsh plugin --profile web add "git+https://github.com/chrisjohnson/dsh-plugins.git#dsh-scheduled-queue-v<version>&path:/packages/scheduled-queue"
```

That installs the package into the profile and enables its bundle. If you manage the profile's `package.json` yourself, the pnpm equivalent is below — then also add `dsh-scheduled-queue` to the profile's `dsh.profile.bundles`, because `pnpm add` alone installs the plugin without enabling it:

```sh
pnpm add "git+https://github.com/chrisjohnson/dsh-plugins.git#dsh-scheduled-queue-v<version>&path:/packages/scheduled-queue"
```

> **Warning:** never `pnpm add dsh-scheduled-queue` (or `dsh plugin add dsh-scheduled-queue`) by bare name. That resolves from the npm registry, where an unscoped `dsh-*` name can belong to an unrelated author and is **not** this plugin.

Restart dsh. With no configuration you get the clock button, the dock and delivery.

## Configuration

Set these on the row in your own profile patch (`config:` block). A top-level config-only row replaces the whole `config` object, so list every key you want.

| Key | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `scanIntervalMs` | `5000` | How often, in milliseconds, the host looks for due items. Clamped to 1000–60000; a value that is not a number is ignored with a warning naming the key. Unset = 5000. |
| `deliveryTimeoutMs` | `60000` | How long one delivery may take before it is given up on and retried. Clamped to 1000–600000; same handling of bad values. Unset = 60000. |

Unknown keys are ignored with one warning each. Nothing is required.

## Persistence

The queue is one JSON file, `<dsh home>/storages/scheduled-queue.json`, where the dsh home is `$DSH_HOME` (a leading `~` is expanded), else `~/.dsh`. It is an array of

```json
{ "id": "…", "messageId": "…", "sessionId": "…", "text": "…", "minutes": 5, "forceSteer": false, "dueAt": 1700000000000, "createdAt": 1699999700000 }
```

Items are written on every change (to a temporary file, then renamed into place) and read at startup, before any request or delivery is served. Items queued by earlier versions use this same format and location and are picked up as they are; `timeZone` is an optional field added later. A file that is not a JSON array is moved aside to `scheduled-queue.json.corrupt-<time>` and the queue starts empty, rather than being overwritten. A file that exists but cannot be read (permissions, I/O error) is logged loudly and **never written over**: the in-memory queue keeps working, nothing is persisted, and the read is retried on every scan; once it succeeds the restored items are merged in and the file is written.

## Host endpoints

Exact Fetch routes under the authenticated `/api` fence; the browser half calls them as `connection.rpc.call('/api', 'scheduledQueue/<endpoint>', payload)`.

| Endpoint | Payload | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `schedule` | `sessionId`, `text`, `minutes`, `forceSteer` | `{ id, dueAt, queue }` for that session |
| `list` | `sessionId` (required) | `{ queue }` for that session |
| `remove` | `id`, `sessionId` | `{ removed, queue }` |
| `sendNow` | `id`, `sessionId` | `{ delivered, queue }` |
| `edit` | `id`, `sessionId`, any of `text`, `minutes`, `forceSteer` | `{ queue }`; empty text is refused |

Every endpoint requires `sessionId`; a call without one gets `bad-request`. `remove`, `edit` and `sendNow` answer `being-sent` for an item whose delivery is in flight.

## Known limits

- If the queue file exists but cannot be read, scheduling still works in memory and the dock warns that messages are not being saved yet. Nothing is written over the file; once it is readable again the restored items are merged in, without bringing back items that were delivered or removed in the meantime.

- **Archived sessions** accept the message and park it until the session is unarchived, exactly as a normal composer send does.
- **Overdue items** (due while the harness was down) wake and resume their sessions on the first scan after start-up. Several overdue items are delivered oldest-due first, one after another.
- **Send now** reports what happened: sent, "stays queued and is retried automatically", or "could not be delivered and was removed" (its text is in the host log). The notice appears even when the dock has no rows left.
- Scheduling does not clear the composer draft.
- The dock lists scheduled messages only for the session window it is in; there is no cross-session view.

## Checks

```sh
node --test packages/scheduled-queue/test/*.test.mjs
```

Covers the per-session filter (host and browser copies), scheduling and edit rules, back-off, the delivery request, reading earlier versions' queue files, and the host wiring against a stand-in harness. The browser rendering and a real delivery into a running session need a live harness and are checked by hand.

## Compatibility

dsh `>=0.2.0-rc.2`. Uses the `conversation.input.right` and `conversation.input.dock` slots, `connection.fetch.register`, and `sessionController.prompt`.

`scripts/verify.mjs` is the interesting one: it enforces the rules that make a plugin installable and trustworthy — `dsh.bundle.patch` present and loading the package by name, `dsh.client` matched by an `./client` export, one harness peer range across every package (`>=0.2.0-rc.2 <0.3.0-0 || >=0.3.0-0`; dsh checks it with prereleases included, while plain node-semver/pnpm admit only `0.2.0-rc.*` and `0.3.0-*` prereleases from it), every shipped file inside the `files` allowlist (all a git-tag install ships), a git-tag install line (and no bare-name one) in every package README, every config key documented in its README, every package listed in the index above, and no deployment leakage. It runs on CI for every push and it runs on a bare clone.

## Contributing

Issues and pull requests are welcome — see [CONTRIBUTING.md](./CONTRIBUTING.md). If you are an agent working in this repository, read [AGENTS.md](./AGENTS.md) first; it is short and it exists because these plugins run with your user's credentials.

For how these plugins get developed, tested against a live harness, released and consumed by the deployment they came from, see [docs/testing.md](./docs/testing.md) and [docs/releasing.md](./docs/releasing.md).

## License

MIT — see [LICENSE](./LICENSE).
