# @quill507/dsh-orchestrator-preset **A thin-shell agent preset for DeepSeek Harness** *The aegis method pack for methodology · a self-authored orchestration layer for delegation* [![npm](https://img.shields.io/npm/v/@quill507%2Fdsh-orchestrator-preset?style=flat-square&label=npm&labelColor=454a54)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@quill507/dsh-orchestrator-preset) [![downloads](https://img.shields.io/npm/dm/@quill507%2Fdsh-orchestrator-preset?style=flat-square&labelColor=454a54)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@quill507/dsh-orchestrator-preset) ![DSH](https://img.shields.io/badge/DSH-0.2.0--rc.2%20%7C%200.2.1--alpha.3%20%7C%200.2.1--alpha.4-4c6ef5?style=flat-square&labelColor=454a54) [![license](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-3da639?style=flat-square&labelColor=454a54)](https://opensource.org/licenses/MIT) [中文](README.zh.md) · [Notices](THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md) · [Issues](https://github.com/cuddly-guacamole/dsh-orchestrator-preset/issues)
A thin-shell agent preset for [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness): the **aegis methodology pack** (upstream, consumed at runtime, unmodified) plus a **self-authored orchestration layer** — nine named lanes with mechanically declared tool boundaries, resident routing sections, a plan-aware persona, and an evidence-based completion gate. The repository root **is** the bundle. There is no `bundle/` subdirectory: the files here are exactly the files that get installed. --- ## Design > **This section is the current and complete authority for what this preset is and how it > works.** There is no separate design specification in this repository: the full design > draft this grew out of — about 280K of design history, decision trail and rejected > alternatives — is **not distributed here**. It is held back, and this section is the > design description in its place. If you want the deeper reasoning, ask; it is not linked > because a link to a file this repository does not contain would look authoritative and > fail on click. ### What it is DSH has no notion of an agent that delegates. A preset declares a set of tools and a persona; nothing in that vocabulary says "this work belongs to someone else". This preset supplies that missing layer. The orchestrator does not write code, search a codebase, or review its own output — it routes each piece to a lane that is *declared* to be allowed to do it, and then judges the result against evidence on disk. ### Lanes and their tool boundaries Nine lanes are rows of the preset itself: `planner`, `scout`, `archivist`, `seer`, `reader`, `analyst`, `auditor`, `wright`, `forge`. Each carries its own persona file and its own `toolFilter`, so a lane's capability boundary is **declarative, not advisory** — a read-only lane's `deny` list removes `write`, `edit`, `todo_write`, every other lane's dispatch tool, and the lead-side child-addressing tools from its seat. The deny lists are what keep a lane from re-entering the coordinator role. `lane-composition.mjs` closes a gap the host leaves open. A Team assembly gives the lead `send_message` / `list_agents` / `interrupt_agent`, which address teammates **by name** and cannot reach a `subagent_*` child at all — so a lead delegating through `subagent_*` lanes would have no way to list, continue, or interrupt them. This bundle registers exactly those three actions under distinct names (`subagent_children`, `subagent_send`, `subagent_interrupt`), addressed by **durable agent id**. Two id namespaces, never mixed. The three names are registered *globally* on purpose: `tools.restrict()` resolves against the global registry, so a scoped registration would make every lane's deny entry illegal and take the whole lane family down. ### Routing sections `routing-sections.mjs` registers four **static** text sections that are reassembled every turn by the host's `systemPrompt` registry: the domain-owner table, the trigger-arbitration table, a short index of standing judgements, and the MCP discipline. They are static constants on purpose — a dynamic system prefix invalidates the session cache wholesale. The single-owner rule is the point. The MCP discipline lives in exactly one section, the orchestrator persona carries one pointer to it, and a delegation brief may *reference* it but must never restate it. The same discipline governs the orchestration layer's own content: the orchestrator persona explicitly disclaims the lane roster and the MCP rules, because a second copy is a second owner. **The four `orch-*` skill names are load-bearing, and renaming one is a two-file edit.** `routing-sections.mjs` and `personas/orchestrator.md` both name `orch-evidence-protocol` and `orch-delegation-brief` explicitly, and the routing table's rows resolve by that exact string. Rename a skill directory and its frontmatter but not those references, and the row keeps pointing at a name nothing provides — which is a silent failure, because a routing entry that matches no skill simply never fires. `node tools/gen-cordis-patch.mjs` and `node tools/audit-personas.mjs` catch a half-finished rename; neither is run automatically, so run one after touching a skill name. The `orch-` prefix itself is not decoration: these skills land in a registry that also holds whatever else a given machine has installed, so an unprefixed `evidence-protocol` would be a name waiting to collide. ### Evidence and state Completion is a file, not a sentence. A task counts as done only when `.dsh/evidence/-.md` exists, is non-empty, and carries exactly one anchored verdict line as its last line. Every path touched in a turn is classified at completion as `in_scope`, `out_of_scope`, `undeclared` or `illegal`, and anything but `in_scope` blocks the completion claim. State that must outlive a session — the lane ledger (`.dsh/state/lanes.md`), direction-level ownership claims (`.dsh/state/claims.md`) and goal frames (`.dsh/goals/.md`) — lives in files, so that a claim can be checked against what other writers also see. ### How this differs from the upstream aegis pack aegis supplies **method**: how to write a plan, run strict TDD, debug systematically, run a review, verify before claiming done. It is a library of skills, and it assumes a single coordinator doing the work. This preset supplies **topology**: who does what, under which tool restrictions, with which evidence. The two are orthogonal and complementary — aegis skills are routed *to* lanes rather than executed in place. What the preset adds that aegis structurally cannot is everything that presupposes more than one agent: the lane ledger and its three states, the direction-level atomic claim with a staleness criterion for cross-session ownership, and the independent-review rule. Those are not extensions to aegis; they are a different axis, and no aegis skill is modified to accommodate them. --- ## Sourcing: what is upstream, what was measured here Being precise about this matters more than it usually does, because a preset is a pile of claims about someone else's runtime. | Claim | Status | |---|---| | A bundle declares a patch via the `dsh.bundle.patch` field in its `package.json`, e.g. `"patch": "./cordis.patch.yml"`. | **Upstream contract.** Verbatim in the published `@deepseek-ai/dsh-base` manifest, which also exports the patch as a subpath. | | Later patch layers win, and a patch **replaces the whole row** rather than deep-merging it — so a row overriding `config` must restate every key it needs. | **Corroborated twice, independently.** | | Exact layer order: bundle patches in `dsh.profile.bundles` order, then the profile's own `cordis.patch.yml`, then `$DSH_HOME/cordis.patch.yml`, then each `--patch` overlay. | **Verified on host version 0.2.0-rc.1.** Not confirmed against upstream documentation. | | A profile lives at `~/.dsh/profiles//` containing `cordis.yml`, `cordis.patch.yml` and `package.json`. | **Verified on host version 0.2.0-rc.1.** Not confirmed against upstream documentation. | | `config.selectedDefault` is in the preset schema and is the effective value; the schema also carries `config.default`, and `defaultId` resolves `selectedDefault ?? default`. | **Verified on host version 0.2.0-rc.1**, against `@deepseek-ai/dsh-agent-preset-registry`. | | `{{cwd}}` is a registered prompt variable; an unknown `{{…}}` reference throws during assembly. | **Version-dependent, and measured on each version.** Registered on `0.2.0-rc.2` (`dsh-agent-loop` registers `provider`/`model`/`cwd`), **absent from `0.2.1-alpha.2` onward** (only `provider`/`model` — re-checked on the installed `0.2.1-alpha.4`). Reproduced against the installed host's own `renderPrompt`: `unknown prompt variable "{{cwd}}" in section "deployment:persona-suffix"`. Upstream `dsh-system-prompt/README.md` now tells users to remove the clause. This is why the `persona` row carries no `suffix` on **any** supported version — see [Host version gate](#0-host-version-gate). | | `tool-subagent`'s `Config` accepts `backgroundMode`. | **Version-dependent.** Present on `0.2.1-alpha.1` (`lib/index.js:257`), **absent from `0.2.1-alpha.2` onward**. schemastery tolerates the unknown key, so the removal is silent — verified by feeding both forms through the installed schema. Continuable is now decided by the provider's `prepareContinuable`, implemented by both the spawn and fork providers on every supported version (re-checked on the installed `0.2.1-alpha.4`). The lane rows therefore write no `backgroundMode` at all. | | The `standard` preset skeleton is the authority for which rows exist. | **Verified on each version.** It shrank from 162 lines (`0.2.0-rc.2`, `0.2.1-alpha.1`) to 137 (`0.2.1-alpha.2`), dropping `tool-ralph`, `tool-subagent-codex` and `tool-subagent-claude-code`; `tool-schedule` was added — **on alpha.1, not on rc.2**. Re-measured on the installed `0.2.1-alpha.4`: 128 lines, still carrying `time-context` and `tool-schedule`, still without the three dropped rows. | | `@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-schedule` exists on every supported host. | **False, and it is the reason this preset's only version-gated row exists.** npm publishes it at `0.0.1-rc.2` (a different generation) and at `0.2.1-alpha.1` … `0.2.1-alpha.4` — there is **no `0.2.0-rc.2`**. `dsh@0.2.0-rc.2` does not depend on it, none of its app packages do, and rc.2's skeleton has no such row; rc.2's reminder tools are the *optional, off-by-default* `dsh-experimental-schedule-bundle`, which inserts `time-context`/`schedule`/`ui-schedule` and **not** `tool-schedule`. | | A lane `toolFilter.deny` naming a tool the host does not register fails loudly at delegation, not at mount. | **Verified on `0.2.0-rc.2` and `0.2.1-alpha.2`, identical behaviour.** `tools.restrict()` throws `names unknown global tool` (`dsh-tools/lib/index.js:2895-2908`), and `dsh-subagent` calls it unguarded when a child is composed (`lib/index.js:401`) — so a hardcoded `schedule_*` deny list would break **every lane delegation** on `latest`. This still holds on `0.2.1-alpha.3`/`alpha.4`, where it is the reason the legacy branch's deny tail stays conditional. | | `tool-subagent`'s row `Config` still accepts `persona` and `toolFilter`. | **False from `0.2.1-alpha.3` onward, and this is the second version-gated mechanism.** `dsh-tool-subagent/lib/index.js:311` no longer declares either key, and `:355` hard-throws on both at mount. The bundle therefore ships **two lane forms** behind one host gate — see [The alpha.3 lane migration](#the-alpha3-lane-migration). | | An Agent Preset can express a tool **exclusion**. | **False, and it is why the bundle ships `lane-tool-gate.mjs`.** A preset's `plugins[]` can only ADD. Measured on `0.2.1-alpha.3`: a persona-only preset gave the child **25** tools including `edit`/`bash`/`send_message`/`interrupt_agent`, and marking `tool-bash` `disabled: true` inside the preset left `bash` present (23 tools). `toolFilter` is also unreachable on that path: fresh dispatch sends `composition: { agentPreset }` only (`dsh-subagent/lib/index.js:1452`), and the single consumer at `:395` reads the field the **resume** path restores from a persisted descriptor (`:2177`). | DeepSeek Harness is MIT-licensed: [`github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness). Unrelated projects sharing a similar name are not a source for anything in this repository. --- ## Repository layout | Path | What it is | |---|---| | `cordis.patch.yml` | **Generated.** The preset's rows. Do not edit by hand — see below. | | `tools/preset-declaration.mjs` | **The single source of truth** for the preset's rows. | | `tools/gen-cordis-patch.mjs` | Generates `cordis.patch.yml` from the declaration. | | `tools/audit-personas.mjs` | Static audit of the persona files (originality thresholds against an excluded upstream corpus). | | `plan-aware-persona.mjs` | Swaps the persona between Orchestrator and Planner per assembly. | | `routing-sections.mjs` | The four resident routing sections. | | `lane-composition.mjs` | The three durable-agent-id child-addressing tools. | | `lane-tool-gate.mjs` | **New on `0.2.1-alpha.3`.** The lane tool gate: `tools.guard()`, mounted inside each lane's Agent Preset, because a preset cannot express a tool exclusion. See [The alpha.3 lane migration](#the-alpha3-lane-migration). | | `personas/` | Ten persona files: orchestrator, planner, and one per lane. | | `skills/` | The four self-authored `orch-*` skills. This directory is the authoritative list of them. | | `extensions/dsh/` | The bundle's two plugins: the skills provider, and the aegis prefix bridge. | | `docs/` | **Not distributed.** The design history is held back; the Design section above is the specification. | | `install.sh` | Installs everything below into a DSH home. | | `tools/verify-install.sh` | Thirteen read-only checks that the preset is installed and selected. | | `README.zh.md` | The Chinese README. Same content, same obligations. | | `LICENSE` | MIT, plus third-party attribution. | **Editing the preset.** `cordis.patch.yml` carries a "DO NOT EDIT BY HAND" header and is regenerated. Change `tools/preset-declaration.mjs` and run: ```sh node tools/gen-cordis-patch.mjs ``` The generator needs a skeleton patch to merge against; it looks for `--skeleton `, then `$DSH_SKELETON`, then the host's own `standard.patch.yml`, and it refuses to invent one if none is found. The `cordis.patch.yml` in this repository is byte-for-byte what that command produces from the committed declaration. --- ## Installation The install method is a **`link:`** dependency, and the package is **also published to npm** as `@quill507/dsh-orchestrator-preset` (current version `0.1.6`, the `latest` dist-tag). `package.json` carries **no** `"private"` key. A profile projects the bundle under **the same name** the registry publishes it under, so a local projection and the published package are told apart by **where they point**, not by their names — see [Publishing to npm](#publishing-to-npm) for what that costs and why it was accepted. The package declares **no** `dependencies` — the host supplies everything at runtime. It does declare `peerDependencies`, all four marked `optional`, so that what it was tested against is written down without any install being able to fail over it: | Package | Range | Why | |---|---|---| | `@deepseek-ai/dsh-skill-filesystem` | `>=0.2.0-rc.2 <2` | the provider this bundle mounts | | `@deepseek-ai/dsh-tools` | `>=0.2.0-rc.2 <2` | `defineTool`, used by `lane-composition.mjs` | | `@deepseek-ai/cordis` | `>=4.0.1 <5` | the plugin contract; a real major boundary | | `@deepseek-ai/schemastery` | `>=3.18.0 <4` | the `Config` schema the settings card is built from | The lower bounds name **the oldest host version this is supported on** — 0.2.0-rc.2, which is also what `latest` still resolves to — not an earlier one the design happened to reference, and not the newest, because the preset is supported on `0.2.1-alpha.3` **and `0.2.1-alpha.4`** too (see [Host version gate](#0-host-version-gate)). The upper bounds follow the convention the published `@quill507/dsh-auto-approval-llm` uses on the same host packages. `optional: true` is what keeps the declaration honest: the coupling here is deep — `ctx.skills.registerProvider` is a host API — so a major change could break this silently, and saying so is worth more than pretending the range is enforced. It is not. **The supported set is three versions, and that is a measured claim, not a copied one.** Each was checked against its own published tarball rather than assumed to follow from its neighbour. Two host releases broke something this preset relied on, and they broke it in two different ways — which is the whole reason the artifact now has a gate in it: - **`0.2.1-alpha.2` removed two keys.** `{{cwd}}` stopped being a registered prompt variable, and `backgroundMode` disappeared from `tool-subagent`'s `Config`. Both removals were *absorbable*: the preset stopped writing either one, and the resulting `persona` row and lane row are legal on **every** supported version. One form, three hosts. - **`0.2.1-alpha.3` removed the mechanism, not a key.** `persona` and `toolFilter` left `tool-subagent`'s row `Config` entirely, and `apply()` now hard-throws if either is present. That one is **not** absorbable: the replacement (an Agent Preset) does not exist before alpha.3, and it cannot express a tool *exclusion* at all. So the lane rows ship in **two forms behind one host gate**, and the new form carries a self-authored gate plugin. See [The alpha.3 lane migration](#the-alpha3-lane-migration). Nothing that differs between the three versions is silently tolerated (see [Sourcing](#sourcing-what-is-upstream-what-was-measured-here)), because a preset that is only correct on its newest host is not supported on the other two — and a preset that is only correct on its newest host *while appearing to load* is worse than one that fails. One **capability** is host-gated instead of uniform, and it is worth knowing which: the Lead's durable reminders (`schedule_create` / `schedule_list` / `schedule_update` / `schedule_delete`) come from `@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-schedule`, which **does not exist on `0.2.0-rc.2`**. The row that mounts it is therefore declared with a `disabled` expression that asks the host whether that package resolves; the lanes' deny tail asks the same question and adds the four names only where they exist. On `0.2.0-rc.2` the preset behaves exactly as 0.1.5 did — the capability is simply absent there, because it is absent from that host. On the two alpha hosts the Lead has the reminders, and **no delegated child does**: the nine named lanes deny them, and so does the `subagent_fork` control row (a forked child is a child too — the same shape the host's own `standard` preset uses on both of its subagent rows). This gate is older than the lane migration and independent of it: it survives on all three supported versions, and on `0.2.0-rc.2` it is the only reason the reminder row and the lanes' deny tail are conditional. It is not the only gate in the artifact any more — the lane form has one of its own, described in the next section. The two ask different questions and must not be conflated. `tools/verify-install.sh`'s check 13 simulates the host without the package and fails if those names appear on it, so this cannot regress quietly. ### 0. Host version gate ```sh dsh --version # install.sh refuses below 0.1.7-rc.1 ``` This is a hard check inside `install.sh`, and it is deliberately **looser** than the `peerDependencies` above: 0.1.7-rc.1 is the version the design was written against, and it is the floor for installing at all — not a claim of support. The honest "untested" band the old wording described, the stretch between the design version and the first version actually exercised, is closed from the top; it is no longer a gap you can fall into by installing the current release. **The supported set is exactly three host versions:** | Host version | npm dist-tag | What you get | |---|---|---| | `0.2.0-rc.2` | `latest` (also `next`) | what a plain `npm i -g @deepseek-ai/dsh` installs, and the runtime the Desktop app bundles | | `0.2.1-alpha.3` | — | superseded on the `alpha` tag; install it by exact version | | `0.2.1-alpha.4` | `alpha` | the newest release; **not** on `latest` — ask for the tag explicitly | `0.2.1-alpha.1` and `0.2.1-alpha.2` are **no longer in the supported set**. They are not broken — they belong to the legacy lane branch and keep working — but they are not tested here any more, and the badge above lists the three that are. The `alpha` tag has moved three times, alpha.1 → alpha.2 → alpha.3 → alpha.4, so the table keeps a row for a version no tag points at any more: `0.2.1-alpha.3` is the version that introduced the lane migration, and it is the one worth being able to install deliberately. None of the three is the single "current" release. Support is not a guess. Every config key this preset hands to a host package — checked field-by-field against all three published versions, not inferred — exists on each with the same type, the same default and the same schema shape, and `plan-mode` rejects unknown keys on all three, so the declared `section` text cannot be silently dropped by a schema that tolerates stray keys. `install.sh --check` runs the version gate and writes nothing. **Two keys did not survive that check, and the preset no longer writes them.** They are worth naming because both failed *silently*, which is the only interesting way for a config key to fail: | Key | Where it went | Why it is not a downgrade | |---|---|---| | `suffix: 'Your working directory is {{cwd}}.'` on the `persona` row | `{{cwd}}` was a registered prompt variable on rc.2 and alpha.1, and **is not one on alpha.2 or anything newer**. `dsh-system-prompt` throws on an unknown variable, so this was not a missing clause — it was a **hard failure during prompt assembly, before any model request**. Upstream now instructs users to delete the clause outright. | The directory is supplied by the `dsh-working-directory` service, which has been in the `dsh-base` skeleton since rc.2 and which alpha.2 exposes through the new `working_directory` tool. The suffix was redundant with it on every version. | | `backgroundMode: continuable` on the ten subagent rows | alpha.2's `tool-subagent` `Config` no longer has the key at all (alpha.1's did), and it is absent on alpha.3 and alpha.4 too. schemastery does not reject unknown keys, so it became a dead key that nothing read. | Continuable is now a **provider capability**, not a row setting: `apply()` reads `subagentProvider.prepareContinuable`, and both the spawn and fork providers implement it on every supported version. The lanes keep their durable-id continuation. | Both removals are safe on all three versions, which is the point: the clause-free `persona` row and the `backgroundMode`-free lane row are legal everywhere, whereas the old forms were legal only on the older hosts. `tools/patch-contract.test.mjs` now fails if `{{cwd}}` reappears in the artifact, so this one cannot come back by accident. The measurements above name alpha.1 and alpha.2 because that is where they were taken, and they are kept verbatim for that reason: they are the evidence for two decisions that still stand on every supported version. Neither version is supported any more — see the table above. ### The alpha.3 lane migration `0.2.1-alpha.3` did not remove a config key. It removed the **mechanism** a lane used to declare its own persona and tool surface, and replaced it with one that cannot express the same thing. This section is the contract, not the history: it is what the artifact looks like on the two alpha hosts, and why. **What changed.** `persona` and `toolFilter` are gone from `dsh-tool-subagent`'s row `Config` (`dsh-tool-subagent/lib/index.js:311` no longer declares either), and `apply()` hard-throws on both (`:355`): ``` tool-subagent: persona is no longer supported; configure persona and tool plugins in an Agent Preset and select it with agentPreset (spawn only) ``` That is a **per-entry activation failure, not a startup crash**: the session still starts, and every affected lane silently fails to activate. On a host where the bundle still wrote the old form, all nine lanes would be dead at once while the session looked healthy. **What replaced it.** Each lane's persona and tool surface now live in an **Agent Preset**, selected from the lane row by `agentPreset`. That brings two hard requirements with it: | Requirement | Why | |---|---| | `allowedAgentPresets` must contain the `agentPreset` id | `dsh-tool-subagent/lib/index.js:209` throws `agentPreset must be included in allowedAgentPresets` at mount otherwise. The two keys must be written **as a pair**. | | The `agent-presets` service must be mounted | `:357` throws `agent preset selection requires the agent-presets service` otherwise. Not every profile provides it. | **Why there are two lane forms.** The preset mechanism does not exist before alpha.3, and the row-config mechanism is rejected from alpha.3 onward. There is no single row shape that is legal on both, so `tools/gen-cordis-patch.mjs` renders each lane in **two forms behind one host gate** and `tools/preset-declaration.mjs` declares both: | | Legacy form (`0.2.0-rc.2`) | New form (`0.2.1-alpha.3`, `0.2.1-alpha.4`) | |---|---|---| | Gate reads | `Config = z.object({…})` **contains** `persona:` | it **does not** | | Persona | `persona: !!js …` on the lane row | a `@deepseek-ai/dsh-persona` plugin inside the lane's preset | | Tool narrowing | `toolFilter.deny` / `.allow` on the lane row | `lane-tool-gate.mjs` inside the lane's preset | | Narrowing reaches the child via | `tools.restrict()`, called by `dsh-subagent` | `tools.guard()`, evaluated along the calling agent's scope chain | The gate is a **structural fact, not a text guess**: it reads whether the `Config` object literal declares `persona:`. The two obvious alternatives were measured and rejected — probing the schema always answers "supported", because schemastery accepts unknown keys and only `apply()` throws; matching the throw's wording is fragile against an upstream reword. The gate is checked in both directions by `tools/patch-contract.test.mjs`. **Failure direction.** If the gate cannot resolve `@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-subagent` at all, it evaluates to **legacy**. That is deliberate: the legacy form fails **loudly** on a new host (the lanes do not activate, and the host says why), whereas guessing the new form on a host that has no preset mechanism would leave the lanes composed with **no narrowing at all** — a silent grant of write access. A loud failure is the direction to fail in. **Two known degradations, stated plainly.** The new form is not an equivalent replacement for the old one. Both of these are deliberate, accepted, and visible in the artifact: - **`reader`'s allow-list has no equivalent.** `tools.guard()` is deny-only — there is no `allow`. The old form gave the `reader` lane `allow: ['read', 'read_image']`, meaning "keep only these". The new form can only enumerate names to refuse, and that list would have to be the entire host tool surface minus two, which drifts with every host release. So on alpha.3 and alpha.4 the `reader` lane's gate blocks only the lane-addressing names, and its **general tool surface is wider than it was on the legacy hosts**. The addressing names *are* blocked unconditionally (`LANE_ADDRESSING_DENY`), because the old allow-list excluded them by construction and letting them through would be a grant, not a degradation. - **The gate hides nothing.** The new form's gate keeps a denied tool **visible and refuses it at call time**, with a readable reason. The legacy `restrict({deny})` **removed it from the visible surface** instead. This is not a like-for-like swap: a lane on alpha.3+ can see a tool it may not use. It is the strongest means alpha.3+ offers — a preset's `plugins[]` can only ADD plugins, so there is no declarative way to exclude a host tool at all. The two forms are gated by one expression and asserted on both sides, so neither can regress into the other's host silently. ### 1–4. Install ```sh ./install.sh # into $DSH_HOME, or ~/.dsh DSH_HOME=/some/other/home ./install.sh ``` From a clone, that stages the bundle into `/plugins/dsh-orchestrator-preset-bundle/` and verifies the per-profile symlink. Nothing is copied into `~/.dsh/skills/`, and there is no companion plugin: the four skills are served by the bundle's own provider, and the aegis prefix bridge is mounted by a row the generator emits. Doing it by hand: ```sh # 1. copy the bundle cp -r . ~/.dsh/plugins/dsh-orchestrator-preset-bundle/ # 2. link it into a profile (see step 5 for the package.json line that makes this work) # and run `pnpm install` there — pnpm creates the symlink from the `link:` dependency. # Verify with test -L, never test -e: Git Bash can silently degrade a link into a # copy, and a copy passes test -e while freezing every later edit to the bundle. test -L ~/.dsh/profiles/web/node_modules/@quill507/dsh-orchestrator-preset && echo "real symlink" # 3. the four self-authored skills need NO install step — they ship inside the # bundle and are served by extensions/dsh/index.js, a filesystem skill provider # mounted by the generated patch with includeDefaultRoots:false. Nothing is # written to ~/.dsh/skills/. # 4. nothing to install. The aegis prefix bridge ships inside the bundle as # extensions/dsh/aegis-prefix.js, mounted by a generated patch row with two # settings: prefixAegisSkills (default on) and describeAegisSkillsInZh # (default off, turned on in your own layer — see below). ``` **Nothing is copied into `~/.

decision.reason: Static evidence chain reviewed. MIT with retained attribution and exact npm gitHead. Versioned DSH 0.2.0-rc.2 plus 0.2.1 alpha peer/documentation evidence. Six native modules and relative source closure are present; no lifecycle hooks. Registers personas, routing, lane tool guards and namespaced skills; read-only settings route uses connection.fetch with request fencing. Prompt/agent orchestration is not independent enforcement or runtime validation. No candidate code or lifecycle hooks were executed; runtime safety and compatibility are unproven.

# dsh-smart-commit

DeepSeek Harness (DSH) 标准插件 — **智能 Git 提交**。

在对话中使用斜杠命令，让 agent 分析当前工作区的 Git 变更，并生成符合 [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/) 规范的中文提交信息，支持 **WIP / amend / squash** 三种提交流程。

## 命令

| 命令 | 作用 |
|------|------|
| `/commit [补充说明]` | 分析变更并创建规范提交（含推送询问） |
| `/commit-wip [补充说明]` | 快速暂存全部变更并创建 `wip:` 临时提交 |
| `/commit-amend [补充说明]` | 修改最近一次提交（追加变更或修改 message） |
| `/commit-squash [N]` | 将最近 N 个提交压缩为一个（N 可省略，届时由 agent 建议范围） |

四个命令是 host 命令，因此：命令后可以带行内参数（`/commit 只提交 lib 目录`、`/commit-squash 3`）；
每次执行都会在会话日志里留下 `command/run` → `command/done` 记录，刷新页面后仍可回溯。

提交由两个模型可见工具完成，全程**不需要 shell**：

- `smart_commit_inspect`（只读）：agent 用它自己看清仓库状态，返回**原始 git 回显**
  （`$ git status --porcelain=v1 -uall` + 真实输出；支持 diff / log / show / branch / remote）
- `smart_commit`（执行）：提交与推送，结果同样是原始回显（`$ git add` / `$ git commit` /
  `$ git push` / `$ git log --stat` + 真实输出）；提交成功但推送失败属于**部分成功**，
  已完成提交会保留、失败原文附在结果里

命令触发后，**流程模板与唤醒消息都以可折叠的「上下文注入」行出现**（两者都用插件自有的
`source.kind`），不会在对话里留下伪装成用户发言的提示；流程启动的可见提示由命令行
（`已启动智能提交流程…`）承担。

## 安装

前置：已安装 DeepSeek Harness（Web 或桌面版）。**agent 不需要 shell 或 git 工具**——
git 由插件宿主进程直接执行。

### Web 版

```sh
dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-smart-commit
```

重启 dsh 服务后生效，在对话中输入 `/commit` 即可使用。

### 桌面版

1. 打开桌面端 → 侧边栏 **Plugins / 插件** 页
2. 安装来源填 `dsh-smart-commit`（或本地 tarball 的 `file:` 路径）
3. 按提示重启桌面端生效

### 从 GitHub 安装（未发布 npm 时）

```sh
dsh plugin --profile web add github:CuiKuLaXiua/dsh-smart-commit
```

> 本插件是 bundle 型包（声明了 `dsh.bundle.patch`），`dsh plugin add` 会自动把它加进
> profile 的 `dsh.profile.bundles` 并应用 `cordis.patch.yml`，**不需要手工加 loader 行**。

## 安全特性

- **推送需明确确认**：`/commit` 流程末尾必须经 `ask_user_question` 用户选择「推送到远程」后才执行 `git push`，始终禁止 force 推送
- **禁止危险命令**：模板禁止 `reset --hard`、`clean -fd`、`push --force` 等
- **不改写 git 配置**：不自动设置 `user.name` / `user.email`
- **敏感文件防护**：提交前检查 `.env`、密钥、token 等敏感文件并排除
- **输入收敛**：补充说明截断 500 字，squash 数量限制 1–50
- **不改写仓库状态**：不做 `git config`、不切换工作区、不动用户已有暂存区之外的内容

## 架构（0.6 起）

命令面是 **host 命令**，执行面是**两个模型可见工具**（agent 全程不需要 shell）：

- **命令面**：四个命令通过 `ctx.commands.register` 注册，声明 `input` 提示。因此
  `/` 菜单行、行内参数（`/commit 补充说明`、`/commit-squash 5`）与官方命令生命周期
  （`command/run` → `command/done`，记录进会话日志）都在；刷新后仍可回溯。
  命令处理体只做两件事：校验工作区在 git 仓库内 → 注入「执行约定 + 模板」→ 唤醒 agent。
- **探查面**：`ctx.tools.register` 注册**只读**工具 `smart_commit_inspect`
  （`status` / `diff` / `log` / `show` / `branch` / `remote`）。agent 自己按需探查，
  返回**原始 git 回显**——与在 Zenith 里 agent 自己跑 `git status` / `git diff` 看到的一致。
- **执行面**：工具 `smart_commit` 在宿主进程用 `node:child_process` 直跑 git（`lib/git.js`），
  **不经过 agent 的命令沙箱**；结果同样是原始回显。提交成功但推送失败属于**部分成功**。
- **自包含**：只用 `node:` 内建模块与相对文件，禁止裸 `@deepseek-ai/*` import。

### 工具入参

agent 先探查看清状态，再调用一次 `smart_commit`：

```json
{
  "commits": [
    { "files": ["lib/index.js"], "message": "refactor(plugin): 示例\n\n## What\n- ...", "amend": false, "squash": 3 }
  ],
  "push": false
}
```

- `files` 省略 / `[]` 表示全部变更（敏感文件自动排除）；显式列出敏感文件会被拒绝
- `amend` 仅 amend 流程（且必须为 `true`）；`squash` 仅 squash 流程（1–50，必须给出）
- `push` 仅 commit 流程，且需用户明确确认

### 宿主强制的安全约束

- **权限随流程收窄、单次生效**：`smart_commit` 只在本会话刚触发过命令后可用；
  `/commit` 允许 push、`/commit-amend` 允许 amend、`/commit-squash` 允许 squash；
  成功即失效，超过 60 分钟或超过 3 次尝试即失效
- 敏感文件拒绝/排除、只允许普通 push（无上游时一次 `-u origin <branch>`，永不 force）、
  禁止 `reset --hard` / `clean -fd` / `checkout -- .`、squash 只允许 `reset --soft`、
  文件路径必须在会话仓库内
- 流程形态校验：squash 流程缺 `squash` 数量、amend 流程缺 `amend: true` 都会被拒绝，
  避免模型漏字段时「悄悄」新建提交

### 版本沿革

| 版本 | 命令面 | 探查 | git 执行 |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0.1 | host 命令 | agent 自己的 shell | agent 自己的 shell（受沙箱影响） |
| 0.2 | 客户端 `action` 贡献（拿菜单样式，丢行内参数与生命周期） | agent 自己的 shell | agent 自己的 shell |
| 0.3 | 客户端贡献 | 宿主预注入「Git 事实」 | 插件宿主进程（宿主校验 + SSE 推结果） |
| 0.4 | 客户端贡献 | 宿主预注入「Git 事实」 | 宿主进程，提交计划走围栏协议 |
| 0.5 | host 命令（行内参数 + 生命周期结果行） | 宿主预注入「Git 事实」 | 宿主进程，由 `smart_commit` 工具触发 |
| **0.6** | 同 0.5 | **`smart_commit_inspect` 只读探查（原始 git 回显）** | **宿主进程，结果原始回显 + 部分成功** |

本地化：菜单行文案来自 host 命令的 `description`（`lib/index.js` 的 `COMMANDS` 表）；
`locale/*.json` 提供插件列表里的标题与描述。

## 排障：PowerShell 启动即崩溃（退出码 3221225794）

Windows 上 DSH 用 ACL 受限令牌沙箱（Low 完整性 + `WRITE_RESTRICTED`）执行 agent 的每条 pwsh
命令，该后端有已知限制：受限令牌下创建的子进程可能在 DLL 初始化阶段直接死亡，退出码
`3221225794`（`0xC0000142`，STATUS_DLL_INIT_FAILED）。这是 DSH 平台问题，与本插件无关。

**0.3 起本插件完全不受它影响**：git 由插件宿主进程直接执行（`node:child_process`），
不经过 agent 的命令沙箱；agent 只读 host 采集的 git 事实、生成 commit message、
用 `ask_user_question` 向你确认，然后调用 `smart_commit` 工具——这些都不需要 shell。

如果会话里**其他**功能（让 agent 跑命令）遇到该崩溃：它是瞬时性的（通常几分钟内自行恢复），
可以稍后重试，或把该会话的文件策略切到 `danger-full-access`；`read-only` 模式下写操作被拒
是设计行为，与崩溃无关。

## 开发

```sh
npm run smoke     # 语法 + 模板断言 + 伪 ctx 挂载 + 真实临时 git 仓库端到端
npm pack          # 打包检查
```

- 纯 Node ESM，零运行时依赖，host 半只用 `node:` 内建模块
- 流程模板位于 `lib/templates/*.md`（`execution-rules.md` 为四流程共用），是 agent 行为的权威约束
- 命令族表与两个工具的定义位于 `lib/index.js`（`COMMANDS` + `PLAN_PARAMETERS` + `runPlan`）
- 宿主侧 git 层位于 `lib/git.js`：`inspectRepo`（只读探查，白名单子命令）+
  `validatePlan`（计划校验）+ `executePlan`（执行，返回原始回显与部分成功信息）
- 本地安装测试：`dsh plugin --profile desktop add file:<本目录>`
  （`file:` 依赖是**拷贝**而非软链，改完代码要重新 install 并重启客户端才生效）

## 发布（维护者）

见 `docs/PUBLISHING.md`。

## License

MIT

# dsh-doudizhu

DeepSeek Harness 的插件：**三人局域网斗地主**。三个人各自在自己那台 DSH 里用浮窗打牌，
其中一台当权威服务，另外两台连过来。

> **当前进度：规则引擎、牌局状态机、权威房间服务与传输、DSH 插件两个半区（host + 浮窗/标签页
> 客户端）都已完成并有测试覆盖；三机实机验收与开源推送尚未开始。**
> 具体的完成边界见「进度」一节，不要按 README 的愿景当成已实现的能力。

## 规则口径

一副 54 张牌（52 张 + 大小王），花色不分大小。
大小顺序：**大王 > 小王 > 2 > A > K > Q > J > 10 > 9 > 8 > 7 > 6 > 5 > 4 > 3**。

| 环节 | 口径 |
| --- | --- |
| 发牌 | 随机洗牌，三家各 17 张，留 3 张底牌 |
| 叫分 | 从首叫位起顺时针，依次叫 1 / 2 / 3 分或「不叫」；**必须比当前最高分更高** |
| 定地主 | 叫到 3 分立刻成地主；否则三家各叫一次，最高分者当地主并拿走 3 张底牌（20 张） |
| 流局 | 三家都不叫则重新发牌，**首叫位不变** |
| 轮换 | 每局结束后，首叫位顺时针轮换一位 |
| 出牌 | 地主先出，之后顺时针；同牌型同长度比点数；炸弹压普通牌型，王炸压一切 |
| 不出 | 只在跟牌时可以「不出」；先手必须出牌 |
| 收回台面 | 连续两家不出，台面清空，出牌权回到最后出牌的那家，可自由选牌型 |
| 胜负 | 地主先出完 → 地主赢；任一农民先出完 → 农民赢 |

### 你给的规则里没写、由本项目钉死的边界

这些都在 `test/rules.test.mjs` 里标了 `PINNED`，改行为前先改测试：

- `10JQKA` **合法**；`JQKA2`、`A2345`、任何带 2 或王的顺子/连对/飞机**非法**。
- 顺子 ≥5 张、连对 ≥3 对、飞机 ≥2 个连续三张。
- 飞机的核心三张必须来自**正好三张**的点数；手里四张同点不能拆出核心。
- 飞机的翅膀数量必须等于核心组数（三个单张，或三个对子）。
- 飞机带单时，翅膀里出现一对也算「两个单张」。
- 四带二（四张 + 两张单牌 / 两对）**不是炸弹**，压不了炸弹，也不能压普通牌型。
- 王炸最大且唯一，没有任何牌能压王炸。
- 两张王的 id 是 `LJ` / `BJ`：`SJ` 是黑桃 J，复用它会让牌堆少一张（有回归测试）。

### 让它出现在 GUI 里（实测：不用重启）

**这一节我上一轮写错过，在这里纠正。** 我原先说"`dsh.client` 元数据在启动时读一次，
所以必须重启 DSH 才会扫描到客户端半区"，依据是探测 `/plugins/<id>/client.js` 返回 404。
那个探测**不可诊断**：已经正常工作的 `dsh-holdem` 同样 404（桌面版走的是 shell 自己的
carrier，不是那条 HTTP 路由）。**结论是错的。**

真实情况：**把插件关掉再打开一次就够了**，运行中的页面会通过 HMR 拿到新的 Loader entry，
并按 `dsh.client` 组合出客户端半区（官方文档 `dsh-client-modules` 的原话：
*"Enabling an ordinary plugin adds its Loader entry … Re-enabling loads one instance with its styles"*）。
本机桌面版实测：

```
plugin_manager set_plugin  include:dsh-doudizhu  enabled=false   -> application: applied
plugin_manager set_plugin  include:dsh-doudizhu  enabled=true    -> application: applied
```

之后**没有重启**，客户端槽位树里立刻出现上面那两个 `active` 的占用者。

所以判断"客户端半区到底装上没有"，要看**客户端槽位树**（`cordis_inspect_query`
→ `client/Slots.listSubTree`，root 填 `shell.overlay` 或 `conversation.view`），
不要看 HTTP 探测。

### 真实浏览器里验过什么

`scripts/browser-harness.mjs` 是个**桩宿主**：它在真实 Chrome 里用真实 React UMD 加载**真实的
`lib/client.js`**，并把 `/dsh-doudizhu/*` 代理到**真实运行中的插件**。唯一 stub 掉的是 DSH 自己的
槽位外壳，其余全是真的。用它（经 Kimi WebBridge 驱动你的 Chrome）走完的过程：

1. 两个槽位注册成功，浮窗与标签页同时渲染出大厅：`🃏 斗地主 · 未进桌`、`我开房/我加入`、

2. 真点 `开房` → **`POST /dsh-doudizhu/host -> 200`**，房间码、局域网地址、
   分享行、三人座位、事件日志 `我 入座` 全部渲染出来。
3. 另外两家经局域网端口真的入座 → 自动发牌，界面显示三家各 17 张、`行动中`、
   `轮到你叫分`、不叫/1/2/3 分四个按钮、`叫分` 阶段徽标。
4. 真点 `3 分` → 变成 `地主`、**20 张**、`你先手，必须出牌`、底牌 `K♥ 9♥ 3♠` 亮出、
   `出牌`/`不出` 并排且显示 `先选牌`；浮窗 651px 高，`left:1566px; top:286px`，整窗在屏幕内。

这一步抓到了两个真 bug，都是单测和 Node 渲染测不出来的：

- **`prefsFrom` 把 `null` 当成了坐标 0。** `Number(null)` 是 `0` 而不是 `NaN`，所以一旦
  `{"x":null,"y":null}` 被写进 `localStorage`，再刷新浮窗就跳到左上角。首次进入（存储为空，
  `Number(undefined)` 才是 NaN）看着正常，所以只在第二次加载才暴露。
- **浮窗按固定高度定位，20 张牌时底部被顶出屏幕。** 窗口真实高度随内容变化（样式表上限 78vh），
  而 `clampPosition` 用的是常量 `MINI_H`。现在先量真实盒子再夹取。

### 已验的安全性质

防泄牌不是靠约定，是靠断言。每个用例在**每一手之后**把三家收到的快照里所有字符串收集成集合，
再断言其中不含任何「此刻属于别人、且尚未公开」的牌面 id：

- `test/room.test.mjs` —— 一盘完整对局的每一步都查一遍（含叫分、炸弹、王炸、过牌、胜负）。
- `test/net.test.mjs` —— 三个 follower 走**真实 HTTP** 打完一盘，每一步都查一遍，
  并且要求每家的快照 `seq` 与权威一致（既查泄露，也查同步）。
- `test/fixtures/follower-probe.mjs` —— 独立 **OS 进程**入座后，`otherHands` 必须是 `[null, null]`。

公开的牌（打出去的牌、地主拿走后的 3 张底牌）不算泄露；一局结束后全明牌是**刻意**的复盘行为，
由 `secretsRevealed` 标记，且有测试钉住它只在结束后为真。

## 架构

```
机器 A（房主 / authority）            机器 B、C（客人 / follower）
┌──────────────────────┐            ┌──────────────────────┐
│ DSH + 本插件          │            │ DSH + 本插件          │
│  浮窗 shell.overlay   │            │  浮窗 shell.overlay   │
│        │ 回环 HTTP     │            │        │ 回环 HTTP     │
│  host 半区 authority  │◄───────────┤  host 半区 follower   │
│  牌堆 / 判定 / 座位过滤 │  长轮询 LAN │  转发 + 本地快照      │
│  0.0.0.0:<port>       │            │                      │
└──────────────────────┘            └──────────────────────┘
```

- **浮窗只跟自己那台机器的 host 半区说话**：一份客户端代码，两种角色通用；浏览器不跨机直连。
- **传输用零依赖 HTTP 长轮询**，不引入 WebSocket。回合制 + 不限时，延迟足够。
- 权威服务**按座位过滤快照**：每个人只拿自己的手牌，别人只给张数。
- 权威端口**只在开房期间监听**，散局即关。

### host 半区的本地接口（M4 已实现）

浮窗调的是**本机 DSH webServer** 上的 `prefix` 路由，不是局域网端口：

| 方法 | 路径 | 作用 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| GET | `/dsh-doudizhu/state` | 当前角色、房间码/地址、**本座视角的快照**；响应头带本地令牌 |
| POST | `/dsh-doudizhu/host` | 开房并坐 0 号位，返回房间码与所有局域网地址 |
| POST | `/dsh-doudizhu/join` | 以客人身份连到某台权威（`host` + `port` + `code`） |
| POST | `/dsh-doudizhu/probe` | 只探一下某个地址是不是斗地主房间，不入座 |
| POST | `/dsh-doudizhu/act` | 转发一个动作（`start` / `next` / `bid` / `play` / `pass`） |
| POST | `/dsh-doudizhu/leave` | 散局：关掉权威端口并回到 idle |

这些 POST 都要求 `x-dsh-doudizhu-token`（首次 GET 下发），并校验 `Origin` /
`Referer` / `sec-fetch-site`：跨站页面既设不了自定义头，也藏不住自己的来源。
`dsh-app://` 这类非 http(s) 来源被当作「无信息」而不是拒绝，否则桌面壳会被误伤。

两次失败的尝试不会拆掉你已经在打的牌局：开房先绑定端口再关旧房，
加入先入座成功再切换角色。**同名重进会复用原座位令牌**，不会多占一个位子。

### 明确不做

**不把 DSH 自己的 webServer 开到 `0.0.0.0`。** 那个端口后面是完整的 agent API，
局域网里任何人都能驱动宿主的会话。游戏走独立端口，只开牌局端点。

### 一个实测到的边界

DSH 自己的 Web 认证**不覆盖插件用 `ctx.webServer.register` 挂的 prefix 路由**：
本机实测 `/api/boot` 未带会话时返回 401，而 `/dsh-doudizhu/state` 返回 200。
所以这个插件的三道校验（本地令牌、同源、`sec-fetch-site`）不是锦上添花，
而是改状态接口**唯一**的防线。响应不带 CORS 头，因此别的网页读不到响应体；
但要记住：**任何本机进程都能读到 `GET /dsh-doudizhu/state` 里你自己的手牌。**

这没有把攻击面扩大到局域网——路由挂在回环 webServer 上，权威端口另开且只承载牌局端点。
但它是一条值得记住的事实，将来 DSH 改了 webServer 认证覆盖面时应当重新核对。

本插件的 `prefix` 路由挂在 DSH 自己的回环 webServer 上，所以它天然不出局域网；
即便如此，所有改状态的操作仍要过上面那三道校验。

## 三机实机怎么跑（M6）

三个人的机器都要先有 DSH。**主机**就是你现在这台；另外两家各做一次：

1. 装 DSH，再按上面「装进自己的 DSH」把插件装上（一行 Release 地址，不用克隆不用构建）；
2. 关掉插件再打开一次，右下角出现浮窗、标签栏出现「斗地主」；
3. 主机点「开房」，浮窗里会显示房间码和局域网地址，把 `房间码 XXXX · 地址 <ip>:8791`
   那一行发给另外两家；
4. 他们在自己的浮窗里填地址和房间码，点「加入」；
5. **三人到齐才自动发牌**（不补位、无 AI 补位），叫分定地主，顺时针出牌。

**主机这台要放行入站 TCP 8791**，Windows 默认拦入站。管理员 PowerShell：

```
netsh advfirewall firewall add rule name="dsh-doudizhu 8791" dir=in action=allow protocol=TCP localport=8791
```

不再需要时删掉：

```
netsh advfirewall firewall delete rule name="dsh-doudizhu 8791"
```

已经通到哪一步：`scripts/live-check.mjs` 在**这台机器上**对**运行中的插件**走完了整条路径——
真开房、真绑定局域网端口、另外两家作为 Node 客户端经**真实局域网地址**入座、打完一盘
（含 36 次真的压牌）、再开下一局、关房，全程做防泄牌扫描。**但那不等于**另外两家真的在
别的电脑上、真的用浏览器打——那才是 M6 剩下的事。

## 同事连不上怎么排查

**先看这条：v0.1.1 及更早版本的「加入」按钮是坏的。** 浮窗发的是 `baseUrl`，宿主读的是
`url`，字段名对不上，于是 `加入` 永远返回 `请填写房主地址（例如 …）`——**地址填得再对也进不去**，
座位从来没被占到。`检查` 能通（那条路由正好读 `url`），所以症状看着像"网络不通"，实际是本机
两个半区之间的字段错位。v0.1.2 已修。判据：如果同事点 `检查` 得到"连上了"、点 `加入` 得到
`请填写房主地址` 而地址栏里明明有内容，就是这个问题。

装完新版**只需要把插件关掉再打开一次**，不用重启 DSH——客户端半区会经 HMR 换掉。实测这个
边界是分开的：切插件能换客户端半区，**换不掉宿主半区**（切完 `/state` 里缺的仍是新宿主
字段），宿主半区的改动要重启 DSH 才生效。这个 bug 的修复在客户端，所以切一次就够。

其余按顺序排，别一次改三样：

1. **地址是不是虚拟网卡的。** 主机装了 WSL / Docker / 虚拟机 / VPN 时，
   `os.networkInterfaces()` 会把那些网卡的地址一起给出（例如 `172.22.0.1` 是 WSL 的
   `vEthernet`）。它们看着和局域网地址一样，**别的电脑永远连不上**。
   本插件现在只把真实网卡的地址放进「发给另外两家」那一行，虚拟网卡的会在下面用一行
   小字说明「已隐藏」，别手抄。本机实测：修之前给的是 `192.168.1.50 或 172.22.0.1`
   （一半概率抄错），修之后只有 `192.168.1.50`。
   注意 `127.0.0.1` 指的是**他自己**那台机器，发给别人一定连不上——所以那一项标了「（本机）」。
2. **房间是不是开着。** 局域网端口**只在开房期间监听**：`role=idle` 时 8791 上什么都没有。
   关房再开房之后房间码会变，要把新的那一行重新发一次。
3. **防火墙。** 本机入站是 `BlockInbound` 默认策略，但已经有两条 `DeepSeek Harness`
   的入站 Allow 规则（`Protocol: TCP`、`LocalPort: Any`、`Public` 配置文件），而监听 8791 的
   进程正是 `D:\.deepseek\DeepSeek Harness.exe`，你的 WiFi 也正好是 Public——所以放行是够的。
   换机器或换网络后如果不够，用上面 M6 那节的两条 `netsh` 命令。
4. **网络本身。** 公司 / 园区 WiFi 常开**客户端隔离**（同一个 SSID 下的机器互相看不见），
   或者同事挂在另一个 SSID / VLAN 上。这一条在客户端改不了，只能这样确认：让同事直接用浏览器
   打开

   ```
   http://<主机地址>:8791/hello
   ```

   - 出 JSON（`{"ok":true,...}`）→ 网络通，问题在插件里填的地址或房间码；
   - 转圈超时 / 无法访问 → 网络或防火墙，先确认两个人连的是同一个 WiFi。

   实际遇到的案子集中在第 1 条和第 2 条。

## 开发

```sh
node --test "test/*.test.mjs"     # 112 个单测：规则 / 牌局 / 房间 / 传输 / 插件 / 展示逻辑 / 客户端
node scripts/build.mjs            # esbuild 打包：src/host.js -> lib/index.js，src/client.cjs -> lib/client.js
node scripts/live-check.mjs       # 对着运行中的 DSH 实机跑一盘（host 半区端到端）
```

在真实浏览器里看浮窗（`scripts/browser-harness.mjs`）：它需要一个本机运行的 DSH，先把两个
React UMD 构建放进 `_tmp/`，再把夹具起在回环端口上，然后用浏览器打开它。

```sh
curl.exe -s -o _tmp/react.js     https://unpkg.com/react@18.3.1/umd/react.production.min.js
curl.exe -s -o _tmp/react-dom.js https://unpkg.com/react-dom@18.3.1/umd/react-dom.production.min.js
node scripts/browser-harness.mjs --port 8792   # 然后打开 http://127.0.0.1:8792/
```

夹具里的「开房」会真的在运行中的插件上建房，所以看完记得回插件里散局。

`lib/` 是提交进 git 的构建产物：用户装的是预构建包，不该在自己机器上跑 esbuild。
改完 `src/` 必须重新 build，否则跑的还是旧代码。

**热更新边界**：客户端半区（`src/client.cjs`）改完 build，桌面版若在跑 client-hmr
会推给浏览器；host 半区（`src/host.js`）改动要重启 DSH 才加载。
而**给一个原本没有客户端半区的插件新加 `dsh.client` / `exports["./client"]`，
不需要重启**：关掉插件再打开一次就会重新扫描并组合，实测见上面「让它出现在 GUI 里」。
（我原先在这里写"必须重启"，是错的。）

`test/` 下除了 `*.test.mjs` 还有共享断言（`test/helpers/leak.mjs`）和子进程探针
（`test/fixtures/follower-probe.mjs`），所以 test 脚本显式带上 glob——
Node 默认会把 `test/` 目录下**所有** `.mjs` 当测试文件跑。

`scripts/live-check.mjs` 是本轮 M4 验收用过的实机脚本，也留给 M6 复用：
它从外部连上运行中的 DSH，开房、经局域网地址入座、打完一盘、再开下一局，最后关房。
`--keep` 可以留下房间给人看。

本机 `node` 不在 PATH 时用 DSH 自带的：

```sh
& "$env:USERPROFILE\.dsh\dsh-runtimes\dsh-primary-runtime\dependencies\node\bin\node.exe" --test "test/*.test.mjs"
```

MIT。规则层移植自 [Aevi 家庭斗地主](https://github.com/AurexloveU/doudizhu)（MIT，

No candidate code or lifecycle hooks were executed; runtime safety and compatibility are unproven.

# AI 圆桌 · DeepSeek Harness

让多个模型围绕同一个问题讨论，由你决定谁来回答、何时追问。

AI 圆桌为 [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) 的原生聊天窗口增加多模型讨论能力。选择 **2–4 个已配置的模型**，让它们按顺序回应，或只选择其中几位补充、复核、提出不同意见。

模型使用宿主已有的服务和凭据。你始终是主持人：插件不会自动安排辩论轮次或替你决定下一步。每位模型完成自己的回答和工具调用后，才轮到下一位。

## 功能

- **多模型讨论**：固定 2–4 名成员，每轮选择任意成员组合，按配置顺序发言，各自使用支持的思考强度。
- **模型可用性检测**：选择模型后自动发送小型探测请求，显示等待时间、独立结果及具体错误，支持取消和重试。
- **原生输入与回答**：保留本体输入框、附件、命令、草稿、流式回答、思考、Markdown、公式及工具卡片。
- **原生工作区与工具**：复用本体的工作区、会话权限、审批和工具执行管线；参与模型共享当前会话的工作区和权限。
- **讨论管理**：复用本体标题、历史、重命名、归档和分支，支持 Markdown 或 JSON 导出。
- **失败处理与停止**：单个成员失败或超时后继续后续成员，可单独重试；原生停止按钮取消本批剩余发言。
- **上下文与界面**：复用本体上下文计量及压缩，成员固定配色，回复显示模型名称，界面跟随宿主主题。

## 安装

需要已安装的 DeepSeek Harness，以及至少两个已配置的模型。插件本身不提供模型账号或 API 密钥。已验证目标是 Windows 官方桌面版 **0.2.0-rc.2**；其他宿主版本和平台需要另外验证。

本插件尚未发布到 npm，已包含构建后的客户端文件，使用者无需运行构建。

### Windows 桌面版按路径加载

下载或克隆源码到固定目录，确认目录直接包含 `package.json`、`cordis.patch.yml` 和 `lib`。

在桌面应用实际使用的 profile 的 `cordis.patch.yml` 中添加以下配置，将路径替换为插件的实际位置：

```yaml
- insert:
    - id: ai-roundtable
      name: 'C:/plugins/dsh-plugin-ai-roundtable/lib/index.js'
```

完全退出并重新打开桌面应用。已有 `insert` 列表时，将插件项合并进去；若此前已加载旧版圆桌，先备份配置并移除旧加载项，避免重复启用。

### 从 GitHub 或本地目录安装到 CLI profile

使用 Node.js CLI 时要求 Node.js 22 或更新版本，插件安装命令还需要 `pnpm`。以下是 Web profile 的 bundle 安装方式：

```powershell
npx @deepseek-ai/dsh plugin --profile web add 'git+https://github.com/dinggy111/dsh-plugin-ai-roundtable.git'
```

也可从固定本地目录安装：

```powershell
npx @deepseek-ai/dsh plugin --profile web add 'C:/plugins/dsh-plugin-ai-roundtable'
```

安装后停止并重启对应的 Web 宿主：

```powershell
npx @deepseek-ai/dsh web
```

Git 地址默认安装当时的默认分支，也可在末尾加 `#提交SHA` 固定版本。独立 CLI Web 宿主的兼容性尚未完成验证，请先核对宿主版本；这里的安装命令不代表所有 Web 版本均受支持。官方桌面版的 `desktop` profile 由 Electron 应用管理，请使用前面的按路径加载方式。

## 使用

1. 点击本体“新聊天”，选择工作区，在输入区打开 **AI 圆桌** 开关。
2. 点击“选择模型”，按期望的发言顺序选择 2–4 个成员，调整思考强度并查看检测结果。
3. 输入问题，选择本轮发言的模型并发送；多个模型会按成员配置顺序回答。
4. 继续追问、只让某位模型复核，或展开原生工具卡片查看执行过程。
5. 需要时停止当前轮次，在顶部“AI 圆桌”菜单导出讨论记录。

例如，先让全部模型评估一个方案，再只让其中一个检查成本假设，最后让全部模型根据补充信息重新给出结论。

首次发送前可以重新配置或关闭圆桌；发送后固定成员，更换成员请新建圆桌。本体 `/model` 命令不会修改圆桌名单。全部取消发言目标时会阻止发送并保留草稿及附件。

连接检测会调用所选模型，输出上限为 512 token。重新勾选、修改思考强度或重新打开选择窗口时会重新检测；失败不会自动重试付费请求。

## 配置

通常无需添加配置。以下为按路径加载时的示例：

```yaml
- insert:
    - id: ai-roundtable
      name: 'C:/plugins/dsh-plugin-ai-roundtable/lib/index.js'
      config:
        dataDir: 'C:/data/roundtable-native'
        callTimeoutMs: 600000
```

| 配置 | 默认行为 |
| --- | --- |
| `dataDir` | 控制索引保存到 `$DSH_HOME/roundtable-native`；未设置 `DSH_HOME` 时使用用户目录下的 `.dsh/roundtable-native` |
| `callTimeoutMs` | 每名成员一次发言（含工具调用）最多 600000 毫秒，取值为 1–3600000 毫秒 |

工作区、工具和权限在本体会话中设置，不使用旧版的 `workspace`、`tools` 或 `probeTimeoutMs` 配置。目录更名不会自动修改已有数据路径；保留 `roundtable-native` 默认目录以继续读取原生版已有索引。

## 数据与权限

- 正文、思考、工具和标题由本体会话日志保存；插件只保存成员、路由、目标和轮次索引，不复制正文或凭据。
- 正式发言、标题生成和模型检测会调用你配置的服务，产生相应服务用量。参与模型按宿主上下文规则接收历史讨论及工具结果。
- 参与模型共享当前会话的工作区和权限。可使用哪些工具、能否写文件或执行命令，由本体配置、模式及审批决定，圆桌轮转本身不会增加授权。
- JSON 导出包含完整原生会话日志及圆桌索引，Markdown 包含用户与模型正文和工具结果；分享前请检查私人内容、路径和工具输出。
- 包名已从 `dsh-plugin-ai-roundtable-native` 改为 `dsh-plugin-ai-roundtable`，旧版独立圆桌讨论记录不会自动读取或迁移。升级前请导出需要保留的讨论。

## 兼容性与限制

| 环境 | 验证情况 |
| --- | --- |
| Windows 官方桌面版 | DeepSeek Harness `0.2.0-rc.2`，按路径加载；宿主构建 commit `04f392c9ddd144fa426da2045178797da6db6c11` |
| 完整界面验证 | 使用安装版宿主模块启动的隔离 Web profile 和本地可控模型 |
| 独立 CLI Web、其他平台或版本 | 尚未完成验证 |
| Node.js | 要求 `>=22` |

本插件依赖宿主内部会话接口及界面结构，升级宿主后应重新验证接入。每场圆桌支持 2–4 个固定成员，模型顺序发言；重启或卸载后不会自动补跑未完成成员。

可用性检测只是一次小型请求的结果，不保证后续长回答或工具调用一定成功。图片输入能力会在发送前检查；实际服务商差异及真实权限审批弹窗仍需在具体环境中验证。

## 卸载

通过 bundle 安装到 CLI profile 时：

```powershell
npx @deepseek-ai/dsh plugin --profile web remove dsh-plugin-ai-roundtable
```

按路径加载时删除对应的配置行，之后重启宿主。卸载不会主动删除本体历史或圆桌索引；删除数据前请分别备份。

## 开发

源码仓库包含自动化测试和构建脚本，无需安装第三方构建依赖：

```powershell
node scripts/build-client.mjs
node --test --test-isolation=none tests/*.test.mjs
node scripts/run-native-tests.mjs
```

修改 `lib/client/` 后需重新构建并同步提交 `lib/client.js`，Git 安装直接使用这份文件。前两条命令可以独立运行；原生集成检查需要目标桌面版安装在 `%LOCALAPPDATA%/Programs/DeepSeek Harness`，通过 Electron 的 Node 模式读取真实宿主模块，不启动日常桌面窗口、不读取账号配置，使用本地可控模型，产物写入 `.test-results`。

隔离界面验证入口是 `scripts/start-test-web.mjs`，需以安装版 Electron 的 Node 模式运行。它将 `DSH_HOME` 设为本目录 `.test-home-ui`，使用本地测试模型和工作区，端口为 3146。不要把 `tests/fixture` 作为日常插件安装。

源码、测试和可复用脚本保留在仓库；日志、一次性报告、个人配置、宿主提取内容和本地开发记录不进入版本控制。

进一步阅读：[设计说明](docs/design.md)、[验证记录](docs/verification.md)、[圆桌补充提示词](docs/roundtable-system-supplement.txt)。

## 问题反馈

请在 [Issues](https://github.com/dinggy111/dsh-plugin-ai-roundtable/issues) 中提供宿主版本、操作系统和复现步骤。粘贴报错或截图前，去掉 API 密钥、登录 token 和私人讨论内容。

## 许可证

[MIT](LICENSE)

Host/client/service/store/probe files and relative closure present, no hooks. connection.fetch POST IPC whitelists operations; model probes use an explicit timeout. Rotates host-native model/session calls, persists round metadata and cancels stale turns; no external candidate process was started. No candidate code or lifecycle hooks were executed; runtime safety and compatibility are unproven.

A Windows multi-bash plugin for DeepSeek Harness: the `git_bash` / `wsl_bash` model tools, each owning its own Git Bash / WSL executor. The plugin never touches the `ctx.shell` seat — dsh's own pwsh executor keeps it — so pwsh behavior is identical to a deployment without the plugin.

## What it provides

| Tool | Backend | Dialect | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `git_bash` | git-bash | MSYS | Owns a `GitBashExecutor`; Git for Windows toolchain |
| `wsl_bash` | wsl-bash | Linux | Owns a `WslBashExecutor`; WSL distro Linux userland |
| `terminal` | git-bash / wsl-bash / msys2-bash | MSYS / Linux / MSYS2 | Interactive PTY sessions; the backend is whichever dialect `shell` names |
| `pwsh` (dsh's own) | pwsh | — | Served by the base bundle's `pwsh-sandbox` row, untouched by this plugin |

- Each tool constructs and drives its own executor; neither registers as `ctx.shell`, so the seat — and every plugin that injects `shell` (dsh's `tool-pwsh`, `permission-presets`, …) — is unaffected by this plugin being loaded.
- Why there is no selector any more: dsh 0.1.7 dropped `ShellExecRequest.shell`, the routing field the pre-0.1.7 `shell-select` design dispatched on. With no routing input left, the tool is what knows which shell it wants — so the selector has nothing to select on, and is gone.
- Executable resolution and sandbox probing are lazy: a host without Git Bash or WSL does not affect pwsh; failures are loud at first use.
- Git Bash is found automatically, in order: an explicit `gitBash.bashPath`, Git install roots inferred from `git.exe` layout directories on PATH (so an install reachable through `git` is found without a pin, even outside the well-known locations), the well-known Program Files layout on every fixed drive (`C:\Program Files\Git`, `D:\Program Files\Git`, ...), `bash.exe` on PATH, and finally the `HKLM\SOFTWARE\GitForWindows` install path (which the Git for Windows installer always records, covering portable installs). The Windows WSL launcher `System32\bash.exe` and `WindowsApps` app-execution alias directories are **never** selected, and candidates must be real regular files — symlinks/reparse points are rejected — so a stale WSL `bash.exe` alias can never shadow a real Git Bash (this tool is MSYS, not WSL).
- Sandbox `auto`: Git Bash probes the windows-acl runner, WSL probes `bwrap` inside the distro; a failed probe degrades honestly to an unconfined run with no sandbox facts. An explicit `sandbox: bwrap` with bubblewrap missing fails loudly at the first `wsl_bash` command (never at boot), leaving the other backends untouched.
- All rows register host-plane: every session sees the tools regardless of its agent preset.

## Sandbox behavior (important — read first ⚠️)

The three backends do **not** share the same file-sandbox capability:

| Backend | Mechanism | enforcement | On probe failure |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `pwsh` | windows-acl restricted-token runner | partial | no probe — always confined (dsh's own executor) |
| `wsl_bash` | `bwrap` (bubblewrap) inside the distro | full | runs unconfined, no sandbox facts |
| `git_bash` | windows-acl runner wrapping MSYS bash | partial (when the probe passes) | runs unconfined, no sandbox facts when the probe fails |

> ⚠️ **`git_bash` usually cannot be sandboxed in Git for Windows deployments.** The windows-acl runner fails to launch the MSYS `bash.exe` under a restricted token (`CreateProcessAsUserW` returns Win32 error 2; `cmd.exe` and `pwsh.exe` launch fine). With `sandbox: auto`, a failed probe degrades to an **unconfined run** by contract. **Do not assume `git_bash` is protected by the DSH sandbox** — for sensitive operations use `pwsh` (restricted token active) or `wsl_bash` (bwrap active), or take the explicit escalation-approval path.
>
> ⚠️ **`wsl_bash` sandboxing depends on bubblewrap inside the distro.** Without bwrap, `auto` degrades to unconfined as well; the probe verdict is cached for the **host process lifetime** — after installing bwrap you must restart `dsh web` (or reload the tool row by editing the profile patch) before it is re-probed.
>
> ⚠️ **A denial is only classified when the command exits non-zero.** If a blocked write is followed by a successful command (`echo nope > /etc/x; echo done`), the overall exit is 0 and no `[sandbox: file access denied]` marker is emitted — matching the upstream bash-sandbox rule to avoid false positives. What the `sandbox` value then says is deliberately narrow: a **successful** confined run reports `denied: false`; a **failed** one whose stderr matches this backend's denial dialect reports `denied: true`; a failed one that matches nothing reports **no `denied` at all** plus `[sandbox: the command failed without matching this backend's denial dialect; see stderr]` — we do not assert a denial nobody observed. An unwrapped run reports only `{mode, unconfined: true}`, because a run outside a sandbox cannot have been denied by one.
>
> The sandbox constrains **file effects only** (`workspace-write` / `read-only`); network and other resources are not limited.
> **`requireSandbox`: refuse unconfined runs when the probe fails (optional hardening).** Both backends support `requireSandbox: true` (default `false`, keeping the existing degrade-and-run behavior). When enabled, a failed probe (windows-acl unusable for git-bash / bwrap missing for wsl-bash) means: `danger-full-access` runs as usual (an unconfined run is equivalent to an explicit full-access grant), while `read-only` / `workspace-write` calls are **refused** with an error naming the fix and the escalation path. The tool layer also advertises the sandbox and opens the `sandbox_permissions` argument, so the model can take the approval-based escalation. Example:

> ```yaml
> # the win-mb-plugin (core row) / win-mb-tool-git / win-mb-tool-wsl rows in cordis.patch.yml:
> # each tool row carries only its own backend's partition
> - id: win-mb-tool-git
>   name: 'dsh-win-multi-bash/tool-git-bash'
>   config:
>     gitBash: { requireSandbox: true }
>
> - id: win-mb-tool-wsl
>   name: 'dsh-win-multi-bash/tool-wsl-bash'
>   config:
>     wslBash: { requireSandbox: true }
> ```

> `requireSandbox` and `sandbox: none` are mutually exclusive in intent — explicit `none` is a deliberate opt-out and stays allowed; `requireSandbox` only governs the "sandbox wanted but probe failed" case.

- **The windows-acl backend is stateful about exactly one directory.** It materializes ONE private temp root per (session, workspace root) — `%TEMP%\dsh-<6 alphanumerics>` — and caches that path for the whole session; its runner treats `--temp` as an input that must already exist, so a missing path is a hard failure (`windows-acl-run: --temp is not an existing directory: <path>`, exit 127) and every later *wrapped* spawn of that session fails until it is back. Recreating the directory by hand restores **existence only** — the seam's write grant (`tempWriteSid` ACE) does not come back, so a confined child writing its own `%TEMP%` stays denied. This plugin therefore recreates the directory **and re-applies the seam's own write grant** on the next confined run of a `git_bash` / `msys2_bash` row — the `guardSandboxTemp` switch, default on (see “Runtime configuration”). Measured on this machine 2026-10-16 (reproduced by this package's own audit; the ad-hoc device script stays a workspace artifact and is not shipped): without the grant a wrapped `cmd.exe` write into its own `%TEMP%` fails with “Access is denied”; with the grant it succeeds; after deleting the private root the runner exits 127 with that signature; after the heal the wrapped write succeeds again.

### Enabling the bwrap sandbox for `wsl_bash`

`wsl_bash` sandboxing requires bubblewrap inside the distro. On Ubuntu/Debian:

```bash
wsl.exe -d Ubuntu-24.04 -e sudo apt-get install -y bubblewrap   # install straight from Windows
wsl.exe -d Ubuntu-24.04 -e bash -c "command -v bwrap && bwrap --version"   # verify
```

- The probe targets the **first distro** from `wsl -l -q`; if your target distro is not the first, pin it via `wslBash.wslDistro` in `cordis.patch.yml` and install bwrap **inside that distro** (e.g. `Ubuntu-24.04`; `docker-desktop` has no bash and cannot be used).
- `sudo` may require a password (depending on the distro's sudoers configuration); use `apt-get install -y` for scripting.
- Other distro families: Fedora `dnf install bubblewrap`, Alpine `apk add bubblewrap`.
- After installing you **must restart `dsh web`** (or reload the tool row by editing the profile patch) — the probe verdict is cached for the host process lifetime, and `wsl_bash` stays unconfined until then.

## Tool prompts (model-facing descriptions)

Each tool description is deliberately small: it states only what its own dialect owns — the shell and invocation, the dialect's path and environment-variable syntax, and (for `git_bash`) the MSYS note. Everything the family shares is stated once, by the single `tool:win-mb-bash` prompt section owned by the plugin's core row (the package row, `win-mb-plugin`): a fresh shell per call plus the `workdir` rule, `[exit code: N]` markers with the `&&` / `set -o pipefail` gating rule, `$DSH_*` environment facts, sandbox behavior, output truncation, delete/move target verification, the unset-variable `${VAR:?}` guard, background jobs, and the escalation contract. The longer dialect notes (MSYS path rewriting, WSL base64 payloads) live in this README rather than in the model-facing text.

Both tools run `bash -c`, so that safety guidance is worded as in `tool-bash`, not as in `tool-pwsh`: `$HOME` is an ordinary assignable variable in bash, so pwsh's "do not assign to automatic variables" sentence would be wrong here — the bash guard for a computed path is the `${VAR:?}` form above, which makes an unset variable fail instead of silently expanding to an empty string.

`git_bash`'s description additionally carries a path-format hint:

> MSYS paths work inside Git Bash only — dsh's file tools (`read`, `write`, `edit`) on Windows take native `C:\...` paths.

So when a command prints an MSYS path (e.g. `/d/WorkSpace/foo`), convert it to its Windows form (`D:\WorkSpace\foo`) before handing it to dsh's file tools; inside the bash command itself, MSYS paths are what the shell expects.

**`workdir` accepts native, MSYS and WSL-automount forms.** A model told that the dialect's paths are MSYS- or WSL-shaped will naturally write `workdir` that way, so the resolver translates a single-letter drive form (`/c/...`) and the WSL automount form (`/mnt/c/...`) into the native `C:\...` before the executor hands the value to `spawn`; MSYS POSIX roots (`/etc`, `/usr`, `/tmp`) and distro-side paths such as `/mnt/data` are left untouched, and a relative `workdir` still resolves against the session workspace. Before that translation an MSYS-form `workdir` failed as `spawn <shell> ENOENT` — a missing-shell symptom for what is really an unusable cwd.

**One section for the family, not one per tool.** The `tool:win-mb-bash` section — owned by the package row (the plugin's core row), and by neither tool — carries that shared guidance: check the `[exit code: N]` marker on every result and chain dependent steps with `&&` or `set -o pipefail`, because `;` never stops on failure and `cmd | tail` returns the status of `tail`, not of `cmd`. That is guidance about *composing* a multi-step command rather than about one call's arguments, so it belongs to the prompt instead of the per-call schema; the runtime's own tail truncation is also why a call never needs to bound output with a pipe. Prompt sections live in one global layer keyed by name, so two rows registering the same name throw while two names carrying the same text is duplication — on 0.3.1 the two descriptions were 1299 and 2164 characters with 1117 of them byte-identical, and the exit-status paragraph was assembled twice. The section's text is therefore resolved at every assembly from the tools actually mounted (`ctx.tools.get`), so `git_bash` and `wsl_bash` stay independently switchable: either alone, both, or neither each render exactly one correct copy, and a composition with neither renders no shell guidance at all. Its order is the midpoint of dsh's `TOOL_BASH` / `TOOL_PWSH` section orders, read from `ctx.systemPrompt.getSectionOrder`. The escalation contract and the background sentence are included only while a mounted tool actually advertises `sandbox_permissions` / `run_in_background`. The section never reads facts out of another row's description, so it stays self-sufficient whether or not dsh's `tool-pwsh` is in the composition; the sentences pwsh's own description shares with it are the residue a third-party row cannot edit away.

**Row switches: what each combination does.** The bundle ships three rows — the core row plus one per tool — and the Plugins page can switch each one, so the combination space is worth stating. Only one combination changes the *text*; none of them loses information:

| `win-mb-plugin` (core row) | `win-mb-tool-git` / `win-mb-tool-wsl` | Result |
|---|---|---|
| on | any subset | Intended: each tool states its dialect facts, the core row's section states the shared guidance once, following the mounted subset (a tool that advertises no `sandbox_permissions` also gets no escalation paragraph). |
| on | **both off** | No family tool is mounted, so the section resolves to empty text and the rendered prompt contains no shell guidance and no shell section at all. The two Configure pages disappear with their rows. |
| **off** | any subset | The Web client has no package row to find `dsh.client` on, so it serves no browser half and the Plugins page shows no **Configure** control. The tools keep working: with the section gone, each tool description carries the shared guidance itself (the fallback, which also logs a warning). |

The core row cannot be marked read-only: `dsh`'s plugin manager locks only the rows from its own protected-module list, its own row, and rows its profile patch cannot address (`readOnlyReason: "management-required" | "unaddressable"`) — there is no manifest flag a third-party bundle can set. The composition is therefore built so that switching the core row off cannot half-break anything: the tool rows are the ones a user actually toggles, and the third row above is the only consequence. Two rows became three: 0.3.0 and 0.3.1 shipped **only** `win-mb-tool-git` and `win-mb-tool-wsl`, so a hand-wired profile that is not migrated still resolves and loads both tools and behaves the same; the missing core row only means the shared guidance falls back into each tool description (above) and that the Plugins-page Configure control is absent — which 0.3.1 did not have either. Re-run `dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-win-multi-bash`, or add the `win-mb-plugin` row to the profile's `cordis.patch.yml` by hand, to get the core row. The separate `win-mb-shell-prompt` row that existed briefly in the development commits between 0.3.1 and 0.4.0 is simply gone — no published version ever declared it, so 0.4.0 ships no module behind that name. A profile that still carries it boots with one inactive entry (the module no longer resolves) and is otherwise unaffected: both tools load, and with no section owner composed each description carries the shared guidance itself.

Two further caveats. A row switched off *at runtime* takes effect immediately for the section (it is resolved per assembly), but a tool row that was already loaded keeps the description it registered: the fallback therefore appears only after that tool row reloads, or after a restart. And a warning issued at startup goes through cordis's logger, which the boot collector keeps for its failure report but discards on a successful boot at the default log level — so the fallback text, not the log line, is what actually guarantees the model keeps the guidance.

## Interactive terminal sessions (`terminal`)

`terminal` runs a **persistent PTY session** — a real interactive shell that stays alive between calls, so the current directory, exported variables, aliases, functions and background jobs survive. Use it for REPLs, debuggers, `ssh`, database clients, TUI programs, or any workflow that depends on shell state.

| Action | What it does |
|---|---|
| `open` | Starts a session and returns its `sessionId`, pid, cwd and startup output. |
| `send` | Writes `text` (with Enter unless `submit: false`) and returns the reply. |
| `read` | Reads new output without writing; `offset` re-reads from a whole-stream byte offset. |
| `signal` | Delivers a signal to the foreground process group. On this platform only `SIGINT` (Ctrl+C) actually reaches the shell — see the signals bullet below. |
| `close` | Ends the session and waits for its session tree to become quiescent. |
| `list` | The sessions you own. |

- **The backend is the dialect registry.** `shell` names one of the dialects that declare interactive-session capability — `git_bash`, `wsl_bash`, `msys2_bash` — and each executor supplies its own interactive argv (`bash.exe -i`, or `wsl.exe --cd <dir> [-d <distro>] -- bash -i`). `terminal.defaultShell` picks the default; a dialect that declares no session is never offered.
- **One interactive shell per session, using the user's own startup files.** `-i` only — no `--noprofile --norc` — because the aliases and exported functions a session exists to preserve are exactly what those files set up.
- **A wait that ends on silence is not a finished command.** `send` / `signal` return once output has been silent for `quietMs` and report `waitReason: "quiet"`; a tty echoes input within milliseconds, so silence usually starts long before a command finishes. `timeout` means the wait hit `waitMs` and the session is still running. Either way, `read` again for more — `quiet` deliberately does not claim "done".
- **Output is a stream, so it is bounded and honest about it.** Each session retains the last `maxBufferBytes` (default 1 MiB) of *sanitized* text, and reports two facts separately: `truncated` (this session dropped output at some point) and `lossy` (the offset this read asked for had already been dropped, so the whole retained tail came back instead of a delta). ANSI escape sequences are stripped; there is no terminal emulator here, so a program that redraws one line with carriage returns becomes several lines.
- **Sessions are capped, reclaimed, and process-local.** `maxSessions` (default 8) refuses the next `open` by name; a session untouched by `send`/`read`/`signal` for `idleMs` (default 10 minutes) is terminated, and its id afterwards says it was reclaimed by the idle reaper rather than looking unknown. Sessions do **not** survive a `dsh` restart.
- **Sessions are not jobs.** They are not registered in `ctx.jobs`, so `job_kill` cannot reach one: `close` is the only way to end a session, with the idle reaper as the backstop.
- **A PTY session runs unconfined, and says so.** The file sandbox wraps the argv of a spawned command; a terminal session is allocated by a different provider call, and on this host the windows-acl runner cannot start MSYS bash at all (measured here: `0xC0000142`) (above), so there is no honest way to confine one. Every `open` carries that fact, and `terminal.allowUnconfined: false` makes `open` refuse instead of running unprotected.
- **Only `SIGINT` reaches the shell here, and the other four say so.** Measured on this host: a win32 ConPTY terminal reports pid `0`, the provider's foreground-group lookup returns that same 0, and its kill path begins `if (pid <= 0) return` — so `SIGTERM` would RESOLVE (reporting success) while delivering nothing to any process, and `SIGKILL` is refused by the provider for the same reason. This tool therefore refuses `SIGTERM`/`SIGKILL` **by name** rather than returning a success that reached nothing; `SIGTSTP`/`SIGHUP` are refused by the provider and that refusal is reported verbatim; `SIGINT` is delivered as a Ctrl+C byte and does interrupt the foreground command (verified: it stops a `sleep 30` while the session stays usable).
- **Two provider facts to know.** `pid` is `0` on Windows (ConPTY), so it is display-only; and `inspectActivity()` always answers `unknown` there, which is why readiness falls back to output silence — on a provider that can answer, `idle` settles at once and `busy` keeps the wait going.
- **The defaults were measured, not guessed.** `quietMs` 500 ms has ~2.3× headroom over the worst inter-chunk gap seen (216 ms, 18 runs of `ls -la /usr/bin | head -80`); 1 MiB is the boundary a single `seq 1 200000` crosses (1,489,391 B raw; this plugin's escape stripping leaves 1,289,146 B = 1.229 MiB, and the ring counts THAT), which is what makes `truncated` observable; `waitMs` 10 s was verified with a 40×200 ms ticker that returned partial output while the session stayed alive; and the 4 s startup budget covers the first prompt, measured at roughly 0.5–0.7 s on this host (a cold first ConPTY allocation is the slow end). Every one of them is live-editable on the row's Plugins page.

## Runtime configuration (the Plugins page)

Both tool rows carry their own configuration, and every knob is declared `.volatile()` — which is what makes it addressable by the runtime's settings service. The Web **Plugins** page therefore edits it: open **Plugins** in the sidebar, open the `dsh-win-multi-bash` bundle, and each row has a **Configure** page. The browser half (`lib/client.js`, declared as `dsh.client` + the `./client` export) registers that page into the page's `plugins.row.config` slot, keyed `dsh-win-multi-bash#<row id>`; a save goes to the profile's Cordis patch through `settings`/`ctx.configForms` — the same place a hand edit lands, with no HTTP route, no second settings file, and no YAML editing.

That is also why the bundle inserts a third row — `win-mb-plugin`, `name: 'dsh-win-multi-bash'` — and why it is the row it is: `dsh-client-modules` discovers a browser half by resolving a row's **bare package specifier** to its `package.json` and reading `dsh.client` there (`locatePkgJson` → `exactPackageSpecifier`, which answers `undefined` for a subpath). The tool rows are subpaths, so without this core row the client bundle is never served and the rows show no Configure control at all. Its module (`lib/index.js`) is the package main, and it owns the shared prompt section as well — one row for the plugin itself, one row per tool.

| Row | Options (in page order) |
|---|---|
| `git_bash` | Background jobs (`enableRunInBackground`); `cwd`, `timeoutMs`, `maxTimeoutMs`, `maxOutputBytes`, `maxSpillBytes`, `graceMs`; `bashPath`; sandbox stance (`auto` / `none`); `probeTimeoutMs`; `requireSandbox`; unwrapped-run notice (`sandboxNotice`: `once` by default, `always` to keep the short marker on every degraded run) |
| `wsl_bash` | The same tool-layer switch (`enableRunInBackground`) plus the same set under `wslBash`, `wslPath` and `wslDistro`, and the stance list adds `bwrap` |
| `terminal` | Interactive sessions: `defaultShell` (which dialect `open` uses by default); `maxSessions`; `idleMs`; `rows` / `cols`; `maxBufferBytes`; `waitMs` / `quietMs` / `maxWaitMs`; `allowUnconfined`; plus one executable pin per dialect (`gitBash.bashPath`, `wslBash.wslPath` / `wslDistro`, `msys2Bash.bashPath`) |

That list is exactly the volatile projection of each row's `Config` schema — the audit pins both sides (`volatilePaths` of the host configs against the browser half's field table), so a knob added to a backend without `.volatile()` cannot silently stay YAML-only, and the page cannot offer a field the Host would refuse.

- **Live reads.** Volatile fields are live references, and the executors read them through `.get()` at use time. A path, distro, stance, timeout, or hardening change applies to the next command without reloading the row.
- **Two knobs need the row's next load**, because they shape the tool's *schema* rather than one call: `enableRunInBackground` (the advertised `run_in_background` argument) and the escalation surface (`sandbox_permissions`, advertised at load from the probe verdict).
- **One behaviour switch is deliberately not on the page.** `promoteOnTimeout` (default on) keeps a foreground command that reaches its timeout running as a background job — visible and killable through the job tools — instead of killing it, matching dsh's own bash tool. It is non-volatile because it is a deployment stance rather than a live knob: set it in the row's YAML and it applies on the row's next load. With `enableRunInBackground: false`, or with no job registry composed, a timeout kills the command exactly as before.
- **A sandbox private temp directory that was removed out of band heals itself (`guardSandboxTemp`, default on).** Each confined run of a `git_bash` / `msys2_bash` row reads the `--temp` the seam is about to hand the windows-acl runner — the path the backend cached for this (session, workspace root) — and when that exact private root is missing it recreates it and re-applies the seam's own write grant (`tempWriteSid` + `AclWriteGrant`, the same calls `dsh-sandbox-local` makes). It is **idempotent, live, and deletes nothing**: the only accepted target is a missing, absolute `dsh-<6 alphanumerics>` *direct child* of an OS temp root, outside every workspace root; anything else — an ambient temp root, a nested path, a lock or spill directory, a wrongly spelled name, an existing directory — is refused and named. `AclWriteGrant` comes from `@deepseek-ai/dsh-sandbox-windows-acl`, taken through a lazy import (declared as an optional peer, no new runtime dependency); when it cannot be resolved the directory is still recreated (existence only) and the plugin warns that the grant was NOT restored. The switch is listed **once, at the top of the plugin** — on the `dsh-win-multi-bash` page, not on each row — and turning it off stops healing everywhere from the next command.
- **The self-heal switch is listed exactly once, on the plugin's own page** (`dsh-win-multi-bash`), never on a tool row: one deployment-wide value governs the guard, each row's inline pre-spawn check and every row alike. `enableRunInBackground` stays on the tool layer, so that one IS on each row. Two honest limits: `wsl_bash` uses bwrap and never materializes a `--temp` directory, so the knob is inert there; and healing only happens where a confined run happens at all — on a host where the windows-acl runner cannot start MSYS bash (measured here: `git_bash` returns `sandbox.unconfined: true` on every call) the git row never reaches the runner, so it can neither break nor heal through it.
- **An unwrapped run says so — once per row by default.** When a command is not wrapped by a sandbox, the result carries `sandbox.unconfined: true`. When the reason is a failed `sandbox: auto` probe — we degraded on your behalf — the row's **first** such run carries the full explanation: `[sandbox: not applied — the confinement probe found no usable sandbox, so this command ran unconfined under <mode> mode; repair the sandbox or set sandbox: none on this tool row to accept unconfined runs]`. What happens after that is the row's `sandboxNotice` knob: `once` (the default) stays silent — the structured fact still rides on every result, so nothing is hidden, and the same sentence stops pushing real output out of the context window; `always` keeps the short marker `[sandbox: not applied — ran unconfined under <mode> mode; reason and fix stated once per plugin load]` on every degraded run. Whichever form it takes, the announcement goes to the channel the model reads first: a foreground result, a promoted result, or a real background job's terminal detail. An explicit `sandbox: none` carries the fact without any note, and `danger-full-access` carries neither: its `mode` already says what it is.
- **A third dialect ships switched off.** `msys2_bash` (the MSYS2 installation's own `usr/bin/bash.exe`, a second toolchain next to Git Bash) is **opt-in**: enable the `win-mb-tool-msys2` row on the Plugins page to mount it, and pin `msys2Bash.bashPath` when MSYS2 is installed outside its usual location. It inherits the MSYS mechanism rather than copying it, and reports its own facts — `$MSYSTEM`, `pacman` — instead of Git Bash's.
- **Text knobs are trimmed on save, and an unusable value is only reported — never rewritten.** A text field (a path, a distribution name) is saved trimmed and the trimmed value is shown back, so what you see is what is stored; blanking a field clears it.
