# @shinon/shinon-forge > **Status:** current — Paket-Doku Shinon Forge. **Stand:** 2026-10-10 > **Einstieg:** `docs/INDEX.md` · **Zahlen:** `docs/ZAHLEN.md` Memory Sync, Global Runner und Engine Adapters für alle Agents. Das Paket ist gebaut und lädt im Distributionstest, ist aber **nicht** in `dsh.profile.bundles` aktiviert; der Runner startet also nicht von selbst. ## Features ### Memory Sync - Integriert mit bestehendem `notion-agent` (`.agents/notion-agent/memory-sync.mjs`) - Tools: `memory_sync`, `memory_status` - Prüft Stale-Memory gegen `~/.agents/memory.json` - Schreibschutz durch Marker (`MEMORY-VERSION: sha256:...`) ### Global Runner - Pollt Agent Sessions auf `Status = idle` - Claim per Lock gegen Doppelausführung - Dispatch via Engine Adapters (claude, codex, agy, muse, hermes, pi, cline, grok, freebuff) - Tools: `runner_control`, `engine_dispatch` - Heartbeat-Schreiben pro Agent ### Engine Adapters Headless-Execution für alle supported Engines: - `claude -p` (mit USE_ANALYTICS=0) - `codex exec` - `agy -p` - `muse exec` - `hermes -z` - `pi` - `cline --json` - `grok` - `freebuff-app` ## Config ```yaml - id: shinon-shinon-forge name: '@shinon/shinon-forge' config: pollInterval: 5 # Sekunden zwischen Polls notionMcpServer: 'notion' memoryPageId: '' # Leer = nutze memory.json maxEngineFails: 3 # Stops Agent nach N Fails heartbeatTimeout: 60 # Sekunden bis stale ``` ## Tools | Tool | Beschreibung | |------|--------------| | `memory_sync` | Sync von Notion (mit `force`/`verify`) | | `memory_status` | Zeige Freshness, Marker, Quellen | | `runner_control` | `start`/`stop`/`status` des Runners | | `engine_dispatch` | Direkter Engine-Aufruf | ## Architektur ``` Notion (MCP) │ ▼ notion-agent/memory-sync.mjs │ ├─▶ ~/.agents/AGENTS.md (kanonisch) ├─▶ ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md (@-Import) ├─▶ ~/.codex/AGENTS.md (@-Import) ├─▶ ~/.gemini/AGENTS.md (@-Import) ├─▶ ~/.grok/rules/notion-memory.md (Copy) └─▶ ~/.hermes/SOUL.md (Block) Agent Sessions │ ▼ Global Runner (Polling) │ ├─▶ Lock-Check ├─▶ Memory laden ├─▶ Prompt bauen ├─▶ Engine dispatch └─▶ Heartbeat schreiben ``` ## Abhängigkeiten - `@deepseek-ai/schemastery` (Peer, aus DSH) - `notion-agent` (optional, für Memory Sync)

       

     
--- > **Status:** current — Einstieg in das Repository. **Stand:** 2026-10-13 > **Dokumentation:** `docs/INDEX.md` · **Zahlen:** `docs/ZAHLEN.md` --- > **🇩🇪 / 🇬🇧 Dieses README ist bilingual.** Prosa-Sektionen gibt es auf Deutsch und > Englisch; Tabellen, Baum und Statusblock gelten für beide Sprachen gemeinsam. > **🇩🇪 / 🇬🇧 This README is bilingual.** Prose sections come in German and English; > tables, tree and status block are shared. > > **Harte Zahlen stehen nicht in dieser Datei.** Sie haben genau einen Eigentümer: > [`docs/ZAHLEN.md`](docs/ZAHLEN.md) — jede mit dem Befehl, der sie erzeugt. > **Hard numbers do not live in this file.** They have a single owner: > [`docs/ZAHLEN.md`](docs/ZAHLEN.md), each with the command that produces it. --- ## 🇩🇪 Was ist Shinon Forge? **Ein Harness ist die Maschine. Shinon Forge ist das Cockpit.** Shinon Forge ist ein unabhängiger Fork des **DeepSeek Harness (DSH)**. DSH liefert den Kern: Agent-Loop, Tools, Sessions, Provider-Adapter, ein Plugin-System auf **Cordis**-Basis. Wir bauen darauf die Schicht, die man tatsächlich anfasst. Kein Neubau, kein Fremdcode, der hineingepfuscht wird. Wir besetzen DSHs eigene Slots (`sidebar.brand.mark`, `conversation.hero.brand.mark`, `main`, `sidebar.panellist`) statt Code zu patchen: *„Everything is a plugin."* Was DSH nicht anbietet, bauen wir nicht daneben — wir bauen es darauf. Ein Paket ist genau ein Ordner unter `packages/`, ein Bundle ist ein Paket mit `dsh.bundle.patch`, und das kanonische Profil ist `profiles/shinon`. **Wie viele** Pakete es gibt, welche davon aktiv sind und wie viele Layer das Profil hat, steht gemessen in [`docs/ZAHLEN.md`](docs/ZAHLEN.md) — nicht in Fließtext. ## 🇬🇧 What is Shinon Forge? **A harness is the machine. Shinon Forge is the cockpit.** Shinon Forge is an independent fork of the **DeepSeek Harness (DSH)**. DSH provides the core: agent loop, tools, sessions, provider adapters, a plugin system on **Cordis**. We build the layer you actually touch on top of it. Not a rewrite, no foreign code jammed in. We occupy DSH's own slots (`sidebar.brand.mark`, `conversation.hero.brand.mark`, `main`, `sidebar.panellist`) instead of patching code: *"Everything is a plugin."* What DSH does not offer, we do not build beside it — we build on top of it. One package is exactly one folder under `packages/`, a bundle is a package with `dsh.bundle.patch`, and the canonical profile is `profiles/shinon`. **How many** packages exist, which are active and how many profile layers there are is measured in [`docs/ZAHLEN.md`](docs/ZAHLEN.md) — not in prose. --- ## ▶ Quickstart ```bash # 1. DSH installieren (falls noch nicht da) npm install -g @deepseek-ai/dsh # geprüfte Fassung + Pin: docs/ZAHLEN.md §1 # 2. Dieses Repo klonen git clone https://github.com/vannon091118/shinon-forge.git cd shinon-forge # 3. Wurzel-Abhängigkeiten (npm ist die einzige Paketquelle, Schritt 3.5/A1) npm install # 3b. Profil-Dependencies: `profiles/shinon` bindet seine Bundles mit `link:` — # das lehnt npm ab (gemessen: EUNSUPPORTEDPROTOCOL). Bis die Bindungsfrage aus # PLAN.md 3.5/3.6 entschieden ist, sind diese Links von Hand bereitzustellen; # der Profiltest sagt es sichtbar, wenn sie fehlen. # 4. Prüfen, ob das Profil auflöst → in diesem Durchlauf ausgeführt: Exit 0 (Layer und Bundles: docs/ZAHLEN.md §2) DSH_HOME=$PWD dsh --profile shinon --dump-config # 5. Booten (Web-UI) → in diesem Durchlauf NICHT gestartet, also hier auch nicht behauptet DSH_HOME=$PWD dsh --profile shinon ``` Schritt 4 ist belegt (`node scripts/dsh-profile-test.mjs`, Exit 0, Zahl: `docs/ZAHLEN.md` §2). Schritt 3 und 5 sind in diesem Durchlauf **nicht** ausgeführt worden: für Schritte, die einen Modellschlüssel oder einen Browser brauchen, gibt es hier keinen Beleg — sie stehen in `docs/ZAHLEN.md` §4 unter „nicht geprüft“. --- ## 🔌 Boot und Schlüssel Das Repo-Root ist das `DSH_HOME`: dort liegt `profiles/shinon` als echtes DSH-Profil (`package.json` mit `dsh.profile.bundles` und `cordis.patch.yml` — ein `pnpm-workspace.yaml` führt dieses Repo nicht mehr, Schritt 3.5/A1). Der Schlüssel gehört **nie** ins Repo — im Profil steht nur der Referenzname (`apiKeyEnv`), das Secret kommt aus der Umgebung: ```bash export SHINON_API_KEY="…" DSH_HOME=$PWD dsh --profile headless "Sag nur: OK" ``` Ohne gesetzte Variable schlägt der Aufruf fail-closed fehl (beabsichtigt). --- > **Status:** current — Einstieg in das Repository. **Stand:** 2026-10-13 > **Dokumentation:** `docs/INDEX.md` · **Zahlen:** `docs/ZAHLEN.md` --- > **🇩🇪 / 🇬🇧 Dieses README ist bilingual.** Prosa-Sektionen gibt es auf Deutsch und > Englisch; Tabellen, Baum und Statusblock gelten für beide Sprachen gemeinsam. > **🇩🇪 / 🇬🇧 This README is bilingual.** Prose sections come in German and English; > tables, tree and status block are shared. > > **Harte Zahlen stehen nicht in dieser Datei.** Sie haben genau einen Eigentümer: > [`docs/ZAHLEN.md`](docs/ZAHLEN.md) — jede mit dem Befehl, der sie erzeugt. > **Hard numbers do not live in this file.** They have a single owner: > [`docs/ZAHLEN.md`](docs/ZAHLEN.md), each with the command that produces it. --- ## 🇩🇪 Was ist Shinon Forge? **Ein Harness ist die Maschine. Shinon Forge ist das Cockpit.** Shinon Forge ist ein unabhängiger Fork des **DeepSeek Harness (DSH)**. DSH liefert den Kern: Agent-Loop, Tools, Sessions, Provider-Adapter, ein Plugin-System auf **Cordis**-Basis. Wir bauen darauf die Schicht, die man tatsächlich anfasst. Kein Neubau, kein Fremdcode, der hineingepfuscht wird. Wir besetzen DSHs eigene Slots (`sidebar.brand.mark`, `conversation.hero.brand.mark`, `main`, `sidebar.panellist`) statt Code zu patchen: *„Everything is a plugin."* Was DSH nicht anbietet, bauen wir nicht daneben — wir bauen es darauf. Ein Paket ist genau ein Ordner unter `packages/`, ein Bundle ist ein Paket mit `dsh.bundle.patch`, und das kanonische Profil ist `profiles/shinon`. **Wie viele** Pakete es gibt, welche davon aktiv sind und wie viele Layer das Profil hat, steht gemessen in [`docs/ZAHLEN.md`](docs/ZAHLEN.md) — nicht in Fließtext. ## 🇬🇧 What is Shinon Forge? **A harness is the machine. Shinon Forge is the cockpit.** Shinon Forge is an independent fork of the **DeepSeek Harness (DSH)**. DSH provides the core: agent loop, tools, sessions, provider adapters, a plugin system on **Cordis**. We build the layer you actually touch on top of it. Not a rewrite, no foreign code jammed in. We occupy DSH's own slots (`sidebar.brand.mark`, `conversation.hero.brand.mark`, `main`, `sidebar.panellist`) instead of patching code: *"Everything is a plugin."* What DSH does not offer, we do not build beside it — we build on top of it. One package is exactly one folder under `packages/`, a bundle is a package with `dsh.bundle.patch`, and the canonical profile is `profiles/shinon`. **How many** packages exist, which are active and how many profile layers there are is measured in [`docs/ZAHLEN.md`](docs/ZAHLEN.md) — not in prose. --- ## ▶ Quickstart ```bash # 1. DSH installieren (falls noch nicht da) npm install -g @deepseek-ai/dsh # geprüfte Fassung + Pin: docs/ZAHLEN.md §1 # 2. Dieses Repo klonen git clone https://github.com/vannon091118/shinon-forge.git cd shinon-forge # 3. Wurzel-Abhängigkeiten (npm ist die einzige Paketquelle, Schritt 3.5/A1) npm install # 3b. Profil-Dependencies: `profiles/shinon` bindet seine Bundles mit `link:` — # das lehnt npm ab (gemessen: EUNSUPPORTEDPROTOCOL). Bis die Bindungsfrage aus # PLAN.md 3.5/3.6 entschieden ist, sind diese Links von Hand bereitzustellen; # der Profiltest sagt es sichtbar, wenn sie fehlen. # 4. Prüfen, ob das Profil auflöst → in diesem Durchlauf ausgeführt: Exit 0 (Layer und Bundles: docs/ZAHLEN.md §2) DSH_HOME=$PWD dsh --profile shinon --dump-config # 5. Booten (Web-UI) → in diesem Durchlauf NICHT gestartet, also hier auch nicht behauptet DSH_HOME=$PWD dsh --profile shinon ``` Schritt 4 ist belegt (`node scripts/dsh-profile-test.mjs`, Exit 0, Zahl: `docs/ZAHLEN.md` §2). Schritt 3 und 5 sind in diesem Durchlauf **nicht** ausgeführt worden: für Schritte, die einen Modellschlüssel oder einen Browser brauchen, gibt es hier keinen Beleg — sie stehen in `docs/ZAHLEN.md` §4 unter „nicht geprüft“. --- ## 🔌 Boot und Schlüssel Das Repo-Root ist das `DSH_HOME`: dort liegt `profiles/shinon` als echtes DSH-Profil (`package.json` mit `dsh.profile.bundles` und `cordis.patch.yml` — ein `pnpm-workspace.yaml` führt dieses Repo nicht mehr, Schritt 3.5/A1). Der Schlüssel gehört **nie** ins Repo — im Profil steht nur der Referenzname (`apiKeyEnv`), das Secret kommt aus der Umgebung: ```bash export SHINON_API_KEY="…" DSH_HOME=$PWD dsh --profile headless "Sag nur: OK" ``` Ohne gesetzte Variable schlägt der Aufruf fail-closed fehl (beabsichtigt). Ob die konfigurierte Route in deiner Umgebung antwortet, hängt an deinem Schlüssel und ist deshalb **nicht** Teil der belegten Zusagen dieses Repos. --- ## 🧩 Pakete Ein Paket ist ein Ordner unter `packages/`. Vier Rollendateien sind Pflicht (`index.js`, `client.js`, `cordis.patch.yml`, `package.json`); zusätzlich erlaubt sind `assets/`, `test/` und benannte Ausnahmen — die **eine** verbindliche Aussage dazu steht in [`docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`](docs/ARCHITECTURE.md) §2. | Paket | Rolle | Profil | |---|---|---| | **[@shinon/core](packages/core)** | Branding-Overlay: Sidebar- und Hero-Marke, Farbverlauf, Pulse | ✅ | | **[@shinon/persona](packages/persona)** | Shinon als Persona-Schicht im DSH-System-Prompt | ✅ | | **[@shinon/locale-de](packages/locale-de)** | Deutsche Sprache, Namespace `shinon` | ✅ | | **[@shinon/tooltip](packages/tooltip)** | Styles für erweiterte Tooltips (keine Tooltip-Logik) | ✅ | | **[@shinon/events](packages/events)** | Hook/Event-Spine: beobachten, normalisieren, validieren, emittieren | ✅ | | **[@shinon/hook](packages/hook)** | Event-Beobachtung auf der Host-Seite, Replay-Fixture | ✅ | | **[@shinon/markers](packages/markers)** | Marker-Spiegel (Brutalord-Regeln) im nativen Side Panel | ✅ | | **[@shinon/dashboard](packages/dashboard)** | Status-Panel; liest die echten `workspaces`/`sessions`-Dienste | ✅ | | Klassifikation des Enhancers | ✅ | | **[@shinon/project-index](packages/project-index)** | persistenter Projektindex (files, symbols, edges, FTS) außerhalb des Repos | ✅ | | **[@shinon/codingmon](packages/codingmon)** | Pet-/Kampf-System mit dauerhaftem Zustand und Client→Host-Naht | ✅ | | **[@shinon/key-router](packages/key-router)** | Key-Pool mit 429-Rotation: **[@shinon/narrative](packages/narrative)** | Chronicle, Arcs, Relationships, Composite State (Zug 5 aktiviert) | ✅ | | **[@shinon/shinon-forge](packages/shinon-forge)** | Memory Sync, Global Runner, Engine Adapters | — | | **[@shinon/better-errors](packages/better-errors)** | Config-Ebene ohne Logik: `apply()` loggt nur | ✅ | | **[@shinon/token-usage](packages/token-usage)** | zeigt im Sidebar-Fuß die Token-Zahl des JÜNGSTEN Turns (aus dessen eigenen Ereignissen gefaltet, dieselbe Zahl wie DSHs Turn-Zeile) und im Titel daneben die Sitzungssumme (DSH-Sitzungs-Projektion `tokenUsage`, dieselbe Zahl wie DSHs Fußpille) | ✅ | | **[@shinon/openapi](packages/openapi)** | Vertrag (`openapi.yaml`) vorhanden, **kein** Server — bewusst nicht aktiviert | — | | **[@shinon/popup](packages/popup)** | Fortschritts-Overlay im `conversation.composer.dock`: faltet das Ereignisfenster der Sitzung (Schritt, offene Aufrufe, zuletzt benutztes Werkzeug) und übersetzt den Text aus `locale-de` | ✅ | Die Spalte „Profil“ ist gemessen aus `profiles/shinon/package.json` (Zahl: `docs/ZAHLEN.md` §1). `openapi` und `shinon-forge` stehen nicht darin — bei `openapi` ist das eine dokumentierte Entscheidung (`docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` §4), bei `shinon-forge` ein Verdikt (es startet fremde Engines; `PLAN.md` §3.12.1). Beide tragen selbst `"dsh": { "inactive": true }` im eigenen Manifest (`dead-package`-Gate). Alle Pakete sind eingecheckt; ob ein Paket aktiv ist, entscheidet allein `dsh.profile.bundles` im Profil (Bestandszahlen: `docs/ZAHLEN.md` §1). --- ## 🛠 Architektur ```text ┌─────────────────────────┐ │ DSH │ Runtime: Loop, Tools, │ (Agent = Model+Harness)│ Sessions, Provider, Cordis └────────────┬────────────┘ │ Slots · Events · Bundles ┌────────────▼────────────┐ │ SHINON FORGE │ Overlay: Brand, Sprache, │ @shinon/* Bundles │ UI-Schichten, Governance └────────────┬────────────┘ │ ┌────────────────────────┼────────────────────────┐ ▼ ▼ ▼ Governance Branding Schichten scripts/gate/ packages/core locale-de, tooltip, Gates + Slices Slots statt Patches dashboard, events … ``` **Regel:** DSH ist die Laufzeit, wir bauen Schichten darauf — kein zweiter Kernel daneben. Offen bleibt am Key-Router der Provider-Override: er gibt DSH noch keinen rotierenden Schlüssel an die Hand. - **Native App** (Stufe 1 scharf, 2–4 Konzept): [`docs/STARTER-PLAN.md`](docs/STARTER-PLAN.md). - **Belege nachziehen**, wo nur ältere Messungen existieren: `docs/probes/` nennt je Probe sein Datum. --- ## 📚 Struktur ```text Shinon-forge/ ├── packages/ # jedes Paket = ein Ordner: @shinon/ (Anzahl: docs/ZAHLEN.md §1) │ ├── core/ persona/ locale-de/ tooltip/ events/ hook/ markers/ dashboard/ │ ├── prompter/ task-router/ project-index/ codingmon/ key-router/ narrative/ popup/ │ ├── better-errors/ token-usage/ │ └── openapi/ shinon-forge/ # bewusst nicht im Profil (Entscheidung bzw. Verdikt) ├── profiles/ │ ├── shinon/ # kanonisches Profil (dsh.profile.bundles, cordis.patch.yml) │ └── headless/ # One-shot-Profil (Modell-Route) ├── docs/ │ ├── INDEX.md # Einstieg + Statusregel für jedes Dokument │ ├── ZAHLEN.md # einziger Eigentümer aller harten Zahlen │ ├── ARCHITECTURE.md # Namespace, Paketgrenzen, Profil-Vertrag │ ├── COMMIT-REGELN.md # Commit-Regeln und Durchsetzung │ ├── STARTER-PLAN.md # native App (plan) │ ├── PLAN.md · FOUNDATION-PLAN.md · REPO-ANALYSIS.md · SYSTEM-ANALYSIS.md # historical │ ├── contracts/ # Verträge (JSON, mit Statusfeld) │ ├── probes/ # Falsifikations-Proben (JSON, mit Datum) │ ├── archive/ # archivierte Altfassungen (u. a. IDEA-raw-export.md) │ └── legacy-goose-prompts/ # importierte Fremdtexte ├── IDEA.md · shinon-forge-implementierungsplan.md # current bzw. historical (Statusblock im Kopf) ├── scripts/ # Gate-Engine, Build, Tests, Helfer (gate/, lib/, *.mjs) ├── prompts/ · assets/banner.svg └── profiles/shinon/ # out-of-tree-Profil (package.json, cordis.patch.yml, cordis.yml) ``` Jede Datei in `docs/` trägt einen Statusblock; die vollständige Liste steht in [`docs/INDEX.md`](docs/INDEX.md) §3. --- ## 🔗 Referenzen (extern, hier nicht geprüft) - [DSH Architektur](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/master/docs/architecture.md) - [Schemastery Config](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/master/docs/user/develop/basic/config.md) - [Locale Plugin](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/master/packages/client/locale/README.md) - [Plugin Manager](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/master/docs/user/develop/basic/publish.md) ---

evidence.readmeExcerpt: # hindsight-coding-agents Long-term project memory for **coding agents**, backed by [Hindsight](https://vectorize.io/hindsight). One package, several agents: a shared reflect-and-inject core with a thin entry point per agent (**Claude Code**, **Codex CLI**, **DeepAgents Dcode**, **opencode**, **opencode 2**, **Kilo CLI**, **Cursor CLI**, **GitHub Copilot CLI**, **Grok Build**, **Qwen Code**, **Kimi Code**, **Factory Droid**, **ZCode**, **TraeCode**, **Antigravity CLI**, **Devin CLI**, **Cline CLI**, **pi**, **Prime Agent**, **DeepSeek Harness**, **WorkBuddy**, **CodeBuddy**). Ingestion is fully automatic — there is no setup command: a repo's git history and conversations flow into its memory bank in the background as you work. The premise: most of a real fix is derivable from the code, but the _last mile_ often hinges on a project-specific decision that isn't in the code at all — a rounding rule, a retry allowlist, a tie-break policy. Those decisions live in git history and past conversations. This package puts them in front of the agent at the moment it starts working, and keeps a curated set of **knowledge pages** (architecture, conventions, in-flight initiatives) that future sessions start from. [View Changelog →](https://hindsight.vectorize.io/changelog/integrations/coding-agents) ## Does it work? [AMB's sdebench](https://agentmemorybenchmark.ai/dataset/sdebench) is the measurement: a coding agent over 61 real repository tasks, three runs each, with and without memory. Accuracy is not what moves — every run solves 60–61 of the 61 either way. These are tasks a good agent can already do. What memory changes is how much it costs you to get there: how often you have to stop and correct the agent, and what the tokens cost. | Agent | Corrections / task | Cost / task | | ----------- | ------------------ | ------------------- | | Claude Code | 0.85 → **0.36** | $0.445 → **$0.338** | | Codex CLI | 1.34 → **0.47** | $0.577 → **$0.276** | | opencode | 1.20 → **0.80** | $0.634 → **$0.553** | No memory → with Hindsight, mean of 3 runs. Corrections reproduce the labels AMB prints on its own chart; cost is derived from the same per-run table. Both numbers move together, and that is the mechanism rather than a coincidence. A correction is a round trip: the agent guesses a project-specific decision wrong, you stop it, you explain, it redoes the work. Every one of those costs a turn of tokens and a turn of your attention. Handing the agent the decision _before_ it starts — the rounding rule, the retry allowlist, the tie-break policy that was settled in a commit message or a conversation months ago — removes the guess, and the round trip with it. ## Install ```bash npx @vectorize-io/hindsight-coding-agents install all # every detected agent, wired natively npx @vectorize-io/hindsight-coding-agents install claude-code # or just one npx @vectorize-io/hindsight-coding-agents uninstall all # removes exactly what install added npx @vectorize-io/hindsight-coding-agents update # refresh the runtime only, no rewiring npx @vectorize-io/hindsight-coding-agents stats # how often each agent uses Hindsight ``` `install` takes an explicit target — `all`, or one or more harness names. A bare `npx @vectorize-io/hindsight-coding-agents install` changes nothing and prints the choice, so wiring every agent on the machine is never something that happens by accident. **Updating is the same `install` command again** — it re-copies the runtime in place. Day to day you should not have to: once a day, a session start checks npm and re-stages a newer runtime in the background (`autoUpdate`, on by default — set it to `false` to pin the version you have). That is the `update` command above, which refreshes the copy every wired agent already points at and deliberately touches no host config; re-run `install` yourself after a release that adds a new hook, or to wire another agent. On a terminal it also asks **where memory should live** — Hindsight Cloud, a server you run, or a local daemon on this machine (see [Where memory lives](#where-memory-lives)). Scripted installs pass `--server cloud|self-hosted|daemon` instead; it is asked only once, and never again on re-install. ### Per agent Same command, only the harness name changes. Run after installing the package globally. #### Claude Code ```bash npx @vectorize-io/hindsight-coding-agents install claude-code ``` 3 hooks in `~/.claude/settings.json`, MCP via `claude mcp add` (user scope), and the companion skill. #### Codex CLI ```bash npx @vectorize-io/hindsight-coding-agents install codex ``` 3 hooks in `~/.codex/hooks.json` plus `[mcp_servers]` in `config.toml` (needs `codex_hooks = true`). #### DeepAgents Dcode ```bash npx @vectorize-io/hindsight-coding-agents install dcode ``` The installer registers this package as a local marketplace with Dcode, then invokes Dcode's own `plugin install` command. The package is a native Agent Plugin: its root `plugin.json` contributes the shared skill, the Hooks V2 `SessionStart`, `UserPromptSubmit`, and `Stop` lifecycle, and the namespaced `hindsight_*` MCP server. Enable the plugin through Dcode's normal plugin manager; no Dcode config patcher or compatibility bridge is required. Dcode namespaces a plugin's MCP tools, so they appear as `plugin__hindsight-coding-…__hindsight_…` rather than under their bare names — the agent resolves them from the tool guide either way. In headless runs (`dcode -n`) Dcode allows the read-only Hindsight tools and gates the two that write (`hindsight_ingest_document`, `hindsight_capture_initiative`) behind an approval it has no UI for; use the interactive TUI to capture an initiative or ingest a document. For the same reason the one-time codebase survey runs under another installed agent's CLI when there is one, exactly as it does for Cursor, Copilot, Devin, Grok Build, Cline, Kilo and Prime Agent. #### opencode ```bash npx @vectorize-io/hindsight-coding-agents install opencode ``` A plugin entry in `~/.config/opencode/opencode.json` — native tools, no MCP needed. #### opencode 2 ```bash npx @vectorize-io/hindsight-coding-agents install opencode2 ``` opencode v2 (`npm @opencode/cli`) exposes an `opencode2` binary alias **alongside** `opencode` and rewrote the plugin API, so it is a harness of its own. It writes the same plugin entry to the same `~/.config/opencode/opencode.json` — the two CLIs share that file, and v1 rejects the whole config if it sees v2's `plugins` key — and each CLI then loads its own entry point from the one registered path. So installing either harness wires both, and uninstalling either removes the shared entry. Two differences from v1, both because of the host: the one-time codebase survey runs under another installed agent's CLI (v2 plugins cannot define the read-only agent the survey needs), and the seed banner is written to the plugin log instead of a TUI toast (v2 plugins cannot raise one). Recall, injection, the native `hindsight_*` tools and session write-back are identical. The companion skill is identical too, but it is registered in memory through v2's skill API rather than copied into a skills directory — opencode2 has none of its own, and the two it reads belong to other agents. #### Kilo CLI ```bash npx @vectorize-io/hindsight-coding-agents install kilo ``` A plugin entry in `~/.config/kilo/kilo.json[c]`. #### Cursor CLI ```bash npx @vectorize-io/hindsight-coding-agents install cursor-cli ``` Hooks in `~/.cursor/hooks.json`, `~/.cursor/mcp.json`, and the companion skill. #### GitHub Copilot CLI ```bash npx @vectorize-io/hindsight-coding-agents install copilot-cli ``` `~/.copilot/hooks/`, `mcp-config.json`, and the companion skill. #### Grok Build ```bash npx @vectorize-io/hindsight-coding-agents install grok-build ``` Native hooks in `~/.grok/hooks/hindsight.json`, MCP in `~/.grok/config.toml`, plus the companion skill. Grok also runs Claude Code's hooks from `~/.claude/settings.json`; those stay silent inside Grok, so a machine wired for both hosts records each Grok session once. Grok passes hook context to the model only from tool hooks, so the session and prompt context arrive with the result of the agent's first tool call after each prompt (a `PostToolUse` hook). #### Qwen Code ```bash npx @vectorize-io/hindsight-coding-agents install qwen-code ``` Native hooks in `~/.qwen/settings.json`, plus MCP and the companion skill. > Qwen's hook `timeout` is in **milliseconds** (its own docs: "Timeout in milliseconds, default > 60000"), unlike every other supported agent, so the installed values are `30000/30000/60000`. > Recall fires on genuine submissions only — `UserPromptSubmit` also fires on tool-result > continuations, so interactive sessions recall once per prompt while headless (`qwen -p`), > `serve`, SDK and ACP sessions seed and retain but do not recall. #### Kimi Code ```bash npx @vectorize-io/hindsight-coding-agents install kimi-code ``` Native hooks in `~/.kimi-code/config.toml`, plus MCP in `~/.kimi-code/mcp.json` and the companion skill. (Hooks and MCP go under `$KIMI_CODE_HOME` instead when it is set.) > Kimi's SessionStart hook cannot reach the model, so the session briefing is silent there; > recalled memory arrives on the first prompt instead, as a `` block. Sessions are > retained from every agent's `wire.jsonl` under the session directory, subagents included. #### Factory Droid ```bash npx @vectorize-io/hindsight-coding-agents install factory-droid ``` 4 hook registrations in `~/.factory/hooks.json` (user scope), including a cancellation-safe `Notification` write-back, plus a stdio MCP registration under `mcpServers.hindsight` in `~/.factory/mcp.json`, and the companion skill in `~/.factory/skills`. The installer touches only JSON files - no Droid CLI round-trip - and refuses to overwrite a user-managed MCP server already named `hindsight`. Droid's hook protocol matches Claude Code's (`session_id`/`transcript_path`/`cwd` in, `hookSpecificOutput.additionalContext` out). Recall and injection use the same protocol; write-back also handles Droid's cancellation notification because Droid does not emit `Stop` after a cancelled turn. #### ZCode ```bash npx @vectorize-io/hindsight-coding-agents install zcode ``` Three hook registrations plus a stdio MCP server under `mcp.servers.hindsight`, both in ZCode's own CLI config `~/.zcode/cli/config.json` - never your real Claude Code settings, even though ZCode embeds the Claude Code agent runtime and speaks its hook protocol. The companion skill goes to `~/.zcode/skills`. Config hooks ship **disabled**, so the installer also sets `hooks.enabled` to `true`; `uninstall` removes the whole block again when nothing else is registered there, and refuses to touch an MCP server named `hindsight` that it did not write. > ZCode's hook `timeoutMs` is in **milliseconds** (installed values `30000/30000/60000`), and > `hooks.maxOutputBytes` caps what a hook may print - anything larger is dropped, injection and > all. The installer seeds it at `32768` only when your config does not already set one. > > ZCode keeps no durable session transcript: `Stop` carries the reply plus a temp, assistant-only > file it deletes as soon as the hook returns, and no user prompt at all. So this is the one agent > whose conversation the plugin journals itself - the prompt hook records what you asked, the > `Stop` hook records the reply - and the write-back then behaves like every other agent's, > appending each new turn to the same session document. `--import-conversations` is therefore not > available for ZCode: there is no past history on disk to backfill from. #### TraeCode ```bash npx @vectorize-io/hindsight-coding-agents install traecode ``` Three hook registrations in TraeCode's user-level `hooks.json`, the companion skill under the same dot-dir's `skills/`, and two `filesystem.readWrite` rules in `sandbox.json` — one for `~/.hindsight`, without which the hooks fail silently (exit 0, no effect) because the sandbox blocks those writes, and one for Trae's per-window storage DBs (`/User/workspaceStorage`), which the SessionStart hook seeds with the workspace's MCP enable switch. Network is allowed by default. TRAE ships two editions with different brand roots — the CN build uses `~/.trae-cn` and "Trae CN", the international build `~/.trae` and "Trae" — so every path resolves by probing for the edition dir that exists and defaulting to the CN names. Plain JSON files, no CLI round-trip. TraeCode speaks Claude Code's hook protocol, so recall and injection work exactly as they do there; the event map lives under the top-level `hooks` key and the `version` field the host writes is preserved. MCP is registered per repo, never at the user level: Trae launches user-level servers with the Electron process's cwd (your home directory), where a hindsight entry either self-disables under `optInOnly` (zero tools) or resolves the home bank instead of the repo's. So the installer pre-seeds the per-repo registration for every repo opted in via `mapPathToBank` — a `mcpServers.hindsight` stdio server in `/.trae/mcp.json`, pinned to that repo via `HINDSIGHT_MCP_PROJECT_CWD` — migrates any stale user-level entry back out of `/User/mcp.json`, and seeds the per-workspace enable switch directly. The SessionStart hook re-checks both on every session and writes them only when missing or stale (idempotent fallback) — Trae's hook sandbox cannot be relied on to perform those writes itself. The per-repo file is merged not clobbered, and gitignored when the repo has a `.gitignore` (the path is machine-specific). A foreign `hindsight` entry — in either file — is the user's own server and is never touched. Trae only reads that per-repo file once the global `trae.mcp.enableWorkspaceMcp` setting is on (default off), so the installer handles the gate: an interactive run asks, a non-interactive run takes `--enable-workspace-mcp`, and either way the setting is written and Trae windows must be restarted to pick it up (declining, or a settings file with comments, prints the manual step). Registrations and enable switches take effect on the NEXT window, so the MCP tools appear when you reload after the first session; repos opted into `mapPathToBank` after install need one more `install traecode` run, and if a repo's server still shows disabled in the MCP panel, flip it on once there. > One manual step remains after install (UI state the installer cannot write): enable the hooks > under TraeCode Settings > Hooks. If you declined the workspace-MCP prompt, enable it later in > Trae settings (search "enableWorkspaceMcp"). > TraeCode keeps no readable session transcript - sessions live in an encrypted local DB or the > cloud. Like ZCode, its conversation is journaled by the plugin itself: the prompt hook records > what you asked, and the `Stop` hook closes the turn with the reply it carries in > `last_assistant_message`. `--import-conversations` is therefore not available for TraeCode: > there is no past history on disk to backfill from. #### Antigravity CLI ```bash npx @vectorize-io/hindsight-coding-agents install agy ``` Lifecycle hooks, MCP, and the `Hindsight · ` status line. #### Devin CLI ```bash npx @vectorize-io/hindsight-coding-agents install devin-cli ``` Hooks in `~/.config/devin/config.json` plus MCP. Needs Node 22.5+ — see below. #### Cline CLI ```bash npx @vectorize-io/hindsight-coding-agents install cline-cli ``` A native plugin via `cline plugin install`, plus MCP and the companion skill. #### pi ```bash npx @vectorize-io/hindsight-coding-agents install pi ``` An extension entry in `~/.pi/agent/settings.json`, plus the companion skill in `~/.pi/agent/skills` — native tools, no MCP needed. This command is the only supported route, for pi and for Prime Agent below. Installing us as a pi package (`pi install npm:@vectorize-io/hindsight-coding-agents`) is deliberately not wired: both hosts read the same `pi` key of a package's `package.json`, and that key can only name one entry — whichever host it did not name would load the other's bundle and report itself as the wrong agent, taking that harness's config section and stamping every document it retains with it. So the package carries no `pi` key at all, and each host is pointed at its own bundle by the install command above. #### Prime Agent ```bash npx @vectorize-io/hindsight-coding-agents install prime-agent ``` Prime Agent is a fork of pi, so it is wired the same way: an extension entry, here in `~/.prime/agent/settings.json`, plus the companion skill in `~/.prime/agent/skills` — native tools, no MCP needed. Installing both is fine and expected: each host loads its own entry from its own settings file, and like every other pair of agents they **share one bank per repo** (the default `coding-agent::{gitProject}`), so what you tell pi is there when you open Prime Agent. Separate entries are what keeps each side attributable — its own `harnesses.` config section, and its own agent stamped on every document it retains. #### DeepSeek Harness ```bash npx @vectorize-io/hindsight-coding-agents install dsh ``` A Cordis plugin row in `$DSH_HOME/cordis.patch.yml` (`~/.dsh` by default), which every dsh profile composes — native tools, no MCP needed. Two dsh-specific notes: one dsh process serves **several repositories** (its Web UI opens each session in whatever directory you pick), so the bank is resolved per session workspace rather than once per process; and dsh has no plugin-facing notice channel, so the seed line goes to the plugin log rather than the UI. Everything model-facing — recalled memory, the knowledge preamble, the `hindsight_*` tools — is unaffected. If you prefer the published-package route, `dsh plugin --profile web add @vectorize-io/hindsight-coding-agents` works too: the package ships the profile patch layer, so nothing else needs editing. Either route gets the companion skill — a plugin wired by the host's own plugin manager installs it itself on the first session, since that route never runs our installer. #### WorkBuddy ```bash npx @vectorize-io/hindsight-coding-agents install workbuddy ``` 3 hooks in `~/.workbuddy/settings.json`, the stdio MCP server in `~/.workbuddy/mcp.json`, and the companion skill in `~/.workbuddy/skills`. WorkBuddy (Tencent's AI workbench) is built on the shared `@genie/agent-cli` engine, so its hooks follow Claude Code's protocol — the main difference is the transcript schema (`type:"message"` records carrying top-level `role`/`content`), which the package's own reader normalizes. #### CodeBuddy ```bash npx @vectorize-io/hindsight-coding-agents install codebuddy ``` 3 hooks in `~/.codebuddy/settings.json`, the stdio MCP server in `~/.codebuddy/.mcp.json` — the recommended file: the installer follows CodeBuddy's documented fallback chain, merging into an existing deprecated `~/.codebuddy/mcp.json` or legacy `~/.codebuddy.json` rather than shadowing it — and the companion skill in `~/.codebuddy/skills`. CodeBuddy Code runs the same `@genie/agent-cli` engine as WorkBuddy — WorkBuddy merely ships it with a different home folder — so it reuses WorkBuddy's hook runtime, and differs only in the root it writes to. **Both CodeBuddy hosts are covered, and they do not store sessions alike.** CodeBuddy Code (the CLI) writes the WorkBuddy JSONL that the shared reader parses. The IDE hands the Stop hook its own per-conversation directory instead — `CodeBuddyIDE//history///`, whose `index.json` _is_ the `transcript_path` and whose prose sits one level down, in `messages/.json` — so the reader dispatches on the shape it was handed (core/transcript-codebuddy-ide.ts). Uninstall the same way: `npx @vectorize-io/hindsight-coding-agents uninstall claude-code` (or `uninstall all`). **Devin CLI needs Node 22.5 or newer.** Its hooks pass only a session id — the conversation itself lives in `~/.local/share/devin/cli/sessions.db` — so reading it depends on Node's built-in `node:sqlite`. Installing `devin-cli` checks for this first and refuses (with the reason) rather than wiring hooks that could never retain anything. Every other agent works on any supported Node. `install` copies what it needs into `~/.hindsight/coding-agents` and points each agent's wiring there, so nothing depends on where you ran it from. **Updating** is the same command again — it re-copies the runtime in place, leaving the wiring valid and every new session on the new version. `install` merges the native wiring (hooks + MCP registration where the host wants them) into each agent's own config, preserving everything already there; it is idempotent (re-run after moving the package) and backs up any pre-existing file it touches as `.hindsight-backup`. `uninstall` removes only our entries. On Claude Code the install also ships a **companion skill** (`~/.claude/skills/hindsight-coding-agent`) that teaches the agent how this memory works — what "store this in hindsight" should do, the tool surface, per-repo configuration, debugging — so users can ask the agent itself. Manual wiring per harness, if you prefer: **opencode** and **opencode 2** install directly — point `opencode.json` at the package dir: ```json { "plugin": ["/path/to/hindsight-coding-agents"] } ``` One entry, both CLIs: v1 resolves that directory through `package.json` `main`, v2 through its `index.js`, so each loads its own plugin. **Claude Code** and **Codex** get their full three-hook + MCP wiring from this package's own installer — `npx @vectorize-io/hindsight-coding-agents install claude-code` / `install codex`. This package's `bin` entries (`hindsight-claude-hook`, `hindsight-codex-hook`, `hindsight-cursor-hook`) are the individual injection-only `UserPromptSubmit` entrypoints for a minimal, hand-wired setup. Adding an agent: hook-based → write a `HookSpec` entry point (see `src/cursor-hook.ts`) and register a `hookAdapter` in `src/harness/registry.ts`; persistent-plugin → implement `HarnessAdapter` (`src/core/types.ts`) fully (see `src/harness/opencode.ts`), or bind the host's own plugin API to `RuntimeCore` directly when it is not an opencode fork (see `src/cline.ts`, `src/dsh.ts`). ## Migrating from the per-agent plugins The older per-agent integrations (`hindsight-claude-code`, `hindsight-cursor-cli`, `hindsight-codex`, …) are superseded by this package. Two things move; nothing else does. **Your server moves automatically.** If `~/.hindsight/claude-code.json` or `~/.hindsight/codex.json` exists, `install` adopts its endpoint — `hindsightApiUrl` → `apiUrl`, `hindsightApiToken` → `apiToken`, and an empty URL means the local daemon, as it did there. The agent you are installing is checked first, so wiring Codex takes Codex's server even if an old `claude-code.json` is still lying around. You already chose where your memory lives; defaulting to Cloud instead would quietly send your prompts somewhere else. Pass `--server` to override. (Those two are the only old plugins that shipped a user config — Cursor CLI, Copilot CLI, opencode and Cline have no endpoint to carry.) **Your conversations are re-imported from local disk**, as new documents: ```bash cd /path/to/your/repo npx @vectorize-io/hindsight-coding-agents install claude-code --import-conversations # or: install codex --import-conversations ``` This re-extracts the transcripts the agent already wrote, so it costs tokens roughly in proportion to the history imported, and it is safe to re-run (ingestion dedups by document id). Local transcripts are the source rather than the old bank, because the old bank cannot be split by repo. Its default was a **single static bank** — `dynamicBankId` defaults to false, so everything landed in one bank named `claude_code` — and its documents record only `retained_at`, `message_count` and `session_id`, nothing identifying the project. Working out which documents belong to which repo means joining `session_id` back to the `cwd` in the local transcript, so the transcripts are needed either way; going through them directly is simply the shorter path. **How sessions are matched.** A conversation is imported only when the session itself records the directory it ran in — never inferred from a file or folder name. Claude Code writes that directory on its entries, Codex in its `session_meta` header and DeepSeek Harness in its session-log header, and pi and Prime Agent in their session header, so all five can be attributed exactly, including sessions started in a subdirectory of the repo. Guessing was tempting (Claude names its history folders after the project path) but unsafe: `/` and `.` both encode to `-`, so `repo-sub` is either the subdirectory `repo/sub` or an unrelated sibling repo — and a wrong guess files someone else's conversation into your bank. Sessions that record nothing are skipped and the count is reported. DeepSeek Harness logs are Zstandard-framed JSONL under `$DSH_HOME/sessions`, which needs Node 22.15+ to read; an older Node skips the import with that reason rather than silently importing nothing. Dcode's transcripts record no directory at all — the working directory lives only in its LangGraph checkpoint database — so the repo comes from `dcode threads list --json`, a declared, versioned command contract rather than that internal schema; with the `dcode` CLI unavailable the import is skipped with that reason. The other harnesses (opencode, opencode 2, Kilo, Cursor, Cline, Copilot, Devin) keep history in internal SQLite databases with unversioned schemas and are skipped with a reason. **Nothing else is translated.** The old plugin's behavioural settings — 12 `recall*`, 7 `retain*`, `bankMission`/`retainMission`, `dynamicBankGranularity` — describe a pipeline this package replaced, and reinterpreting them would be guesswork. Bank naming changes too: this package uses one bank per **repo** (`coding-agent::{gitProject}`) shared by every agent. To keep the old naming instead: ```jsonc { "bankIdTemplate": "{harness}::{gitProject}" } // reproduces the old per-agent naming ``` ## Where memory lives Three modes, chosen once when you install (`install` asks on a terminal; pass `--server` to script it): | mode | what runs | needs | | ------------- | ----------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------- | | `cloud` | Hindsight Cloud (default) | an API token | | `self-hosted` | a Hindsight server you already run | its URL | | `daemon` | a local `hindsight-embed` on this machine | `uv` on PATH + an LLM key for extraction | ```bash npx @vectorize-io/hindsight-coding-agents install claude-code --server daemon npx @vectorize-io/hindsight-coding-agents install claude-code --server self-hosted --api-url http://localhost:8888 npx @vectorize-io/hindsight-coding-agents install claude-code --server cloud --api-token ``` Re-running `install` never re-asks: a config that already names a server is left alone. ### Local daemon mode Nothing to sign up for and nothing to host — memory runs on your machine. The plugin starts `hindsight-embed` on demand at `127.0.0.1:9077` and points every agent at it. - **A server already on the port is adopted, never restarted** — so one daemon serves every agent and every repo, and your own `hindsight-embed`

evidence.readmeExcerpt:
# dsh-gemini-kitten-widget 🐱

给 **DSH Web 界面**右下角常驻的一只 **Q 版 Gemini 猫娘**，实时显示 Gemini API 免费层的
**今日已用 / 剩余次数**。

```
        ╭──────────────────╮
        │ 还有 12 次额度躺着 │     ← 点一下换台词
        │ 睡觉呢，真浪费喵。 │
        ╰────────┬─────────╯
            (\_/)                   💜 蓝紫长发
           ( ^ω^ )                  👂 猫耳
           /|   |\                  👁️ 异色瞳（左蓝 #4285F4 / 右紫）
        ┌────────────┐              😼 坏笑 + 小虎牙
        │ ✦ 8 /20    │
        │ ▓▓▓▓░░░░░░ │              ← 用掉 80% 变橙、95% 变红
        │剩12次·13h后 │
        └────────────┘
```

## 配额口径（**这一节最重要**）

| 项 | 值 | 出处 |
|---|---|---|
| 限额 | **20 次 / 模型 / 天** | Google API 的 429 原文 |
| 重置 | **UTC 午夜**（= 北京次日 08:00） | 同上，由 `retry in` 反推 |
| 统计范围 | **只算 DSH 内**的调用 | 见下 |

**429 原文**（2026-10-15 两次独立实测，存放在 `~/.dsh/facts/gemini-free-tier-quota.json`）：

```
Quota exceeded for metric: generativelanguage.googleapis.com/generate_content_free_tier_requests,
limit: 20, model: gemini-3.8-flash
Please retry in 13h23m35s.
```

> ⚠️ **历史更正**：本插件最初按"250 次/天、太平洋时间午夜重置"实现（那是用户侧的口径）。
> 2026-10-15 晚拿到 API 原文后**已改正**为 20/模型/天 + UTC 午夜。
> 分母可用环境变量 `DSHK_QUOTA_PER_MODEL` 覆盖，时区用 `DSHK_QUOTA_TZ`（配额随时可能变，
> 别把它焊死在代码里）。

### 两个必须知道的局限

1. **只统计 DSH 内发起的调用**。你在 Gemini CLI / AI Studio / 其他脚本里消耗的配额，
   本挂件**看不到** —— 所以挂件数字**天然 ≤ 真实剩余**。
2. **配额是按模型分别算的**。挂件主显示盯着"**最紧的那个模型**"（用掉最多的），
   悬停可以看到各模型明细。`gemini-3.8-flash` 用完不影响 `gemini-3.7-flash`。

## 数据从哪来

两道口子，**按权威度排序**：

1. **DSH 会话日志**（权威）——`~/.dsh/sessions/**/session.v4.jsonl.zstd` 里每条
   `assistant/message` = 一次模型响应 = 一次 API 调用。
   日志是**多帧拼接的 zstd**，本插件逐帧解压、按 mtime/size 增量缓存（稳态 ~0ms）。
2. **鲸鱼娘账本**（兜底）——`~/.dsh/.dshw-usage.json` 的 `events`。
   ⚠️ 它是**按 turn 聚合**的：一个 turn 里 agent 可能问模型几十次，它只写一条。
   **所以账本条数 ≠ 调用次数**，只在日志读不到时兜底。金额（cost）也来自这里。

## 台词与梗库

内置台词写死在 `assets/kitten.js` 的 `LINES`；**私货**另存于 `~/.dsh/widget-lines.json` 的 `kitten` 段——
host 半随 `/dsh-kitten/state` 一起下发，客户端**追加**（不覆盖内置），**改完刷新页面即生效、无需重启**。

```json
{
  "kitten": {
    "ok":     ["今天也要好好写代码喵。"],
    "warn":   ["换个型号使唤本喵吧，兄弟们还有力气喵。"],
    "danger": ["换一位吧，本喵这个型号今天真没劲了喵。"]
  }
}
```

占位符：`{used}` 已用次数 · `{remaining}` 剩余 · `{limit}` 每日上限 · `{model}` 当前型号短名。

> ⚠️ **视角纪律**：这是**哈基米（Gemini）**的嘴，只说她自己的事。
> 她是**猫娘**，别让她自称别的角色（写串了会很怪）。
> 同一个文件的 `whale` 段是鲸鱼娘视角的**素材仓库**（她是第三方插件，落地方式见该段的 `note`）。

## 交互

| 操作 | 效果 |
|---|---|
| **拖动** | 移动挂件；松手后自动**吸附**到最近的屏幕边缘 |
| **单击猫娘** | 换一句台词（台词随额度状态变化） |
| **单击徽章** | **切换查看哪个型号**（配额按模型独立，一轮只放得下一行） |
| **右键** | 回到默认位置（鲸鱼挂件上方） |
| **悬停** | 全部型号的明细 / 重置时间 / 数据来源 |

位置记在 `localStorage`，刷新后保持。

## 安装

**方式一：直接从仓库装**（推荐）

```
# 在 DSH 会话里对 agent 说：
#   plugin_manager install_bundle  target = git+https://github.com/Void-LifeStream/dsh-gemini-kitten-widget
```

**方式二：先 clone 再用本地 link**

```powershell
git clone https://github.com/Void-LifeStream/dsh-gemini-kitten-widget
```

```
# 然后让 DSH 装本地目录（桌面端读 desktop profile，CLI 拒绝 --profile desktop）：
#   plugin_manager install_bundle  target = link:<clone 下来的绝对路径>
```

⚠️ **装完必须重启 DSH**：桌面端（Electron）的注入表是**宿主启动时一次性收集**的，
插件在运行期被加载时这一行进不了表 ⇒ 挂件不出现。**web 形态**（`dsh web`）走 `tapIndex`，同样建议重启一次。

⚠️ **依赖**：无。不需要任何 API key —— 本插件**只读本机数据**（DSH 会话日志 + 可选的余额账本），
**从不联网**、不写配置、不碰凭据。

⚠️ **它对"没装鲸鱼娘挂件"的环境同样可用**：账本只是兜底数据源，没有它时会话日志照常工作。

## 技术形态

```
dsh-gemini-kitten-widget/
├─ package.json          dsh.bundle.patch → cordis.patch.yml
├─ cordis.patch.yml      挂载声明（insert 一条）
├─ lib/index.js          host 半：注入行 + 三个只读路由 + 配额统计
├─ assets/kitten.js      client 半：渲染 + 拖拽吸附 + 台词 + SVG 兜底
├─ assets/kitten-art.png 形象立绘（本地生成，透明 PNG）
└─ tools/                自测与出图脚本（见下）
```

**两条注入通道**（桌面端与 web 形态各一条，各自去重）：

1. `webserver/index-inject` 推 **内联 `<script>` 行** —— 桌面端唯一通道。
   用内联行而不是 `script-src` 行：页面侧对 `script-src` 是「加载失败即 reject 整个 boot」，
   插件被关掉时路由注销 ⇒ 404 ⇒ **应用起不来**。内联行自己建 `<script src>` 并吞掉 `onerror`。
2. `webServer.tapIndex` 往 `index.html` 注入 `<script defer>` —— web 形态通道。

**路由**（都只读、不含任何凭据）：

| 路由 | 作用 |
|---|---|
| `GET /dsh-kitten/widget.js` | 客户端脚本，URL 带 **mtime 指纹**（改完刷新即生效，无需重启） |
| `GET /dsh-kitten/art.png` | 形象立绘，ETag 走 mtime |
| `GET /dsh-kitten/state` | 配额 JSON |

**安全姿态**：本插件不写配置、不碰凭据，所以没有鲸鱼娘那套写接口信任栅栏；
只做「`Sec-Fetch-Site: cross-site` 一律拒」+ 委托宿主的 `connection.requestRejection`。

### 开发

- **只改 `assets/kitten.js` 或 `kitten-art.png`** → 刷新页面即生效（mtime 指纹绕开缓存）。
- **改了 `lib/index.js`** → 需要重启 DSH。
- 改配额口径：`DSHK_QUOTA_PER_MODEL=20`、`DSHK_QUOTA_TZ=UTC`。

### 自测脚本（本机 node 不在 PATH 里，用 DSH 运行时那个）

```powershell
$node = "$env:USERPROFILE\.dsh\dsh-runtimes\dsh-primary-runtime\dependencies\node\bin\node.exe"
& $node tools\selftest.mjs   # host 半离线自测：注入行 / 路由 / 配额算法
& $node tools\logtest.mjs    # 日志计数器：增量解帧 / 半截帧 / 截断重写（13 项）
& $node tools\uitest.mjs     # 浏览器回归：立绘 / 回退 / 拖拽吸附 / 台词 / 三档变色（19 项）
& $node tools\shot.mjs <输出目录>   # 出预览图
```

抠图（重新处理形象）用 ComfyUI 自带的 python：

```powershell
& "F:\ComfyUI\ComfyUI-aki-v3.2\python\python.exe" tools\cutout.py <源图> assets\kitten-art.png 480
```

### 血泪避坑（写给下一个改它的人）

1. **客户端脚本里绝不能 `require()` 内置符号**（`styles` / `host` 是 seed word）——
   后果是**整个 web boot 失败**、应用弹「无法启动」。要插样式就自建 `<style>` 并 `appendChild`。
2. **初始化路径上任何异常都会让挂件「活着但点不动」**（被空 catch 静默吞掉）——
   此处所有早退分支都打 `console.error`，不静默。
3. **注入行必须最早注册**：桌面端的注入表一次性收集，晚一步就永远进不去。
4. **别用账本条数当"调用次数"**（按 turn 聚合，会严重低估）。
5. **多帧 zstd 要逐帧解**：`zstdDecompressSync` 只解第一帧，直接读会得到 1 行。

## 形象来源

**本地 ComfyUI（anything-v5）生成 + `transparent-background` 抠图**，纯本地、零成本、不出网。

> 为什么不用网上现成的"猫娘二创"：画师作品**默认保留全部权利**，Gemini 娘的同人图
> （如 B站 ZipZipPipe 那版）属"参考风格"而非可再分发素材；DSH 插件生态里的桌宠素材
> 多绑定各自的皮肤/角色授权。**自己生成是唯一既干净又能贴合"蓝紫发 + 猫耳 + 异色瞳"设定的路。**

灵感参考：ZipZipPipe 的「Gemini 娘」二创（B站原帖 `1233069202138464289`）。

## 授权

MIT

# logo-substitute

DSH（DeepSeek Harness）Web GUI 品牌替换插件。

> **自用声明**：本项目是作者**自用**的小工具，顺手开源给小范围的朋友共用，
> 按 **MIT** 协议授权，你可以自由使用、修改、再分发。

## 功能

在「设置」里新增一个 **Logo替换** 子菜单，把侧边栏顶部品牌行里的**鲸鱼标志**与
**deepseek 字形**换成你自己的图标与文字。

- 页面顶部是「使用默认」/「使用自定义」两个切换标签，底部固定一个「保存」按钮。
- 「使用自定义」时提供两项输入：**图标上传**（图片）与**文字标识名称**。
- 保存「使用自定义」后，侧边栏品牌行变成：**你的图标 + 你的文字 + `HARNESS`**。
  官方 `HARNESS` 标记**保留**，由本插件接在自定义文字后面重绘。
- 保存「使用默认」则恢复官方品牌（鲸鱼 + deepseek HARNESS）。这一步**不会删除**你已上传的
  图片与文字 —— 随时切回「使用自定义」继续用，无需重新上传。
- 图标只要求**宽高相等（正方形）**，对像素尺寸没有限制；非正方形会给出中文提示，
  并且**不会覆盖**已保存的设置。
- 页面底部显示插件版本号与作者信息。
- 配置存在渲染层 `localStorage`（key `logo-substitute:v1`），刷新 / 重启 GUI 后仍然生效。

## 效果

| | 品牌行显示 |
|---|---|
| 使用默认 | 🐳 `deepseek HARNESS`（官方原样） |
| 使用自定义 | 你的图标 + 你的文字 + `HARNESS` |

## 环境要求

| 项 | 值 |
|---|---|
| 插件版本 | **1.0**（`package.json` 的 `version` 为 `1.0.0`，同一个版本） |
| DSH 版本 | 在 `0.2.0-rc.2` 上验证通过；`dsh.engines.dsh` 声明 `>=0.2.0-rc.2`（**仅作声明**，宿主不强制校验） |
| 宿主平台 | Web GUI（桌面版与网页版共用同一套渲染层） |
| 运行时依赖 | **无**。浏览器半只 `require('react')`，不 `require` 任何 `@deepseek-ai/*` 包 |
| 构建步骤 | **无**。浏览器半是手写的 ModuleLoader bundle |

## 安装

DSH 的「添加插件」（**设置 → 插件 → 添加插件**）接受四类输入：**包名（可带版本）**、
**Git 地址**、**压缩包**、**本地绝对路径**。任选其一即可。

### 方式一：图形界面（不熟悉命令行的话用这个）

1. 把本目录放到本机 —— 直接拷贝、或 `git clone`、或用解压后的压缩包。
2. 打开 DSH → **设置 → 插件 → 添加插件**。
3. 填入下列任意一种，然后点「安装」：
   - 本地目录的绝对路径，例如 `/绝对/路径/logo-substitute`
   - Git 地址，例如 `https://github.com/<你的账号>/logo-substitute.git`
   - 你打好的压缩包路径，例如 `/绝对/路径/logo-substitute-1.0.0.tgz`
4. **重启 DSH 图形界面**（bundle 组成只在启动时装配）。

### 方式二：命令行

```bash
# 本地目录，link 安装：改源码即时生效，适合自己开发调试
dsh plugin --profile desktop add link:/绝对/路径/logo-substitute

# 本地目录，拷贝安装：装完与源目录无关
dsh plugin --profile desktop add /绝对/路径/logo-substitute

# Git 仓库
dsh plugin --profile desktop add https://github.com/<你的账号>/logo-substitute.git

# 压缩包
dsh plugin --profile desktop add /绝对/路径/logo-substitute-1.0.0.tgz
```

> 图形界面用的 profile 名是 **`desktop`**。装到别的 profile（比如 `web`）当前界面看不到。

装完**重启 DSH 图形界面**，再打开 设置 → 左侧应出现「Logo替换」。

## 使用

1. 打开 **设置 → Logo替换**
2. 选「**使用自定义**」
3. 上传一张**正方形**图片
4. 填「文字标识名称」
5. 点「**保存**」→ 侧边栏品牌行立即更新（不用刷新）

想还原成官方品牌：回到该页选「使用默认」，再点「保存」。

## 卸载

```bash
dsh plugin --profile desktop remove logo-substitute
```

也可以在 **设置 → 插件** 里停用 / 卸载，然后重启界面。

本插件**不修改 DSH 的任何官方文件**，卸载后侧边栏品牌自动回到官方显示；
如果你的配置想一并清掉，删掉 `localStorage` 里的 `logo-substitute:v1` 键即可。

## 外观

界面全部使用 DSH 主题 token（`--dsw-alias-*`），深浅色自动跟随，无任何硬编码颜色。
自定义图标按品牌位容器尺寸（24px）等比 `object-fit: contain` 显示。

HARNESS 字样用 10px、字距 `.12em`、三级文字色绘制，尽量贴合官方观感。

## 已知限制

- **`HARNESS` 标记是插件重绘的**，不是官方那段手绘 SVG 字形 —— 官方把「deepseek」和
  「HARNESS」焊在同一个 SVG 里，无法只保留后者。所以它**不会像素级一致**。
- 配置存在 `localStorage`，**按机器**保存，不跨机器同步；清空 DSH 的站点数据会丢配置。
- 只替换**侧边栏品牌行**。「新建会话」按钮本身以及其它界面元素不受影响。
- 插件**不支持自动更新**：升级需要先卸载再装新版。

## 故障排查

**装完看不到「Logo替换」** —— 依次检查：

1. 是否**重启了整个图形界面**。只刷新页面不够，bundle 组成在启动时才装配。
2. `~/.dsh/profiles/desktop/package.json` 里是否有**两处**条目，缺一不可：
   - `dependencies` 里有 `"logo-substitute"`
   - `dsh.profile.bundles` 数组里有 `"logo-substitute"` ← **这一处才决定插件是否被加载**
3. 个别环境下 `dsh plugin ... add` 会在写完 npm 侧（`dependencies` / `node_modules` 软链 /
   `pnpm-lock.yaml`）之后**卡住不返回**，于是 `bundles` 没被写入。此时手动把
   `"logo-substitute"` 加进 `dsh.profile.bundles` 再重启即可。**改之前先备份该文件。**

**品牌行空白而不是回落官方** —— 说明自定义图片数据坏了（例如手工改过 `localStorage`）。
删掉 `logo-substitute:v1` 这个键，刷新即可恢复。

## 目录结构

```
logo-substitute/
├── package.json          # 包清单：exports、license、files、dsh.bundle.patch、dsh.client
├── index.js              # 宿主半（exports "."），纯 UI 插件，无逻辑
├── client.js             # 浏览器半（exports "./client"），手写 ModuleLoader bundle
├── cordis.patch.yml      # bundle patch：把插件行插入 profile 的 web 组成
├── README.md
├── LICENSE               # MIT
├── .gitignore
└── tools/
    └── smoke-test.mjs    # 冒烟校验脚本（npm run smoke）
```

## 实现要点（为什么不会和官方品牌打架）

`sidebar.brand.mark`（鲸鱼）与 `sidebar.brand.name`（deepseek HARNESS）都是 `single`
席位，官方包 `@deepseek-ai/dsh-client-ui-brand-official` 以 priority 0 注册它们。

引擎在 `single` 席位上不允许**同 priority** 二次注册，但允许**不同 priority 共存**，
并且渲染时**priority 数值最小者胜出**。因此本插件以 `priority: -1` 接管这两个席位，
而且只在「已保存模式为自定义、且有图片」时才注册；一旦切回默认就立即 `dispose`，
让官方品牌自然回来 —— 本插件**不**复刻官方鲸鱼 SVG 来当"默认"，避免随 DSH 版本漂移。

## 自检

```bash
node tools/smoke-test.mjs   # 或 npm run smoke
```

纯 node、零依赖、不联网、不写盘：stub `window.__ModuleLoader__` + stub `react` + 假
`ctx.slots` + 假 `localStorage`，覆盖入口契约、`settings.section` 席位注册、
品牌席位的 `priority: -1` 与切回默认后的释放、正方形校验、持久化 round-trip、脏数据回落，
以及底部插件信息（版本 / 作者）。全部通过时打印 `SMOKE OK: n/n` 并以 0 退出。

## 示例
![Demo](demo.png)

## 免责声明
本插件**不修改 DSH 的任何官方文件**，卸载后侧边栏品牌自动回到官方显示；
如果你的配置想一并清掉，删掉 `localStorage` 里的 `logo-substitute:v1` 键即可。
仅供学习专用。

## 作者

**JakeKim@XingHaoTech** ｜ 微信：**vvip2u**

## 许可

[MIT](LICENSE) © 2026 JakeKim@XingHaoTech

本项目为作者自用工具，按 MIT 协议开源。软件按「原样」提供，不附带任何形式的担保。

# Bulk–scRNA Concordance — DSH Host plugin

Turns the TBtools `Transcriptome Integration — Bulk & scRNA Correlation` plugin
into an agent-callable analysis tool in the DeepSeek Harness.

The original `.plugin` package contained a 118 MB PyInstaller-encrypted EXE plus
a TBtools Java GUI shell. This bundle replaces both: the numerics live in a
readable Python script inside the package, and the Harness registers a tool the
agent can call directly.

- Full parameter reference, input formats and interpretation: **[docs/usage.md](docs/usage.md)**
- Runnable input fixtures: **[examples/synthetic/](examples/synthetic/)** (600 genes × 6 cells, disjoint group markers)
- Survey of the neighbouring DSH plugin ecosystem: [docs/github-survey.md](docs/github-survey.md)
- CI runs the analysis on those fixtures on Linux and Windows: [.github/workflows/checks.yml](.github/workflows/checks.yml)

---

## What it adds

One tool: **`bulk_scrna_concordance`**.

For each group (L1/L2/L3 …) it sums single-cell counts into a pseudo-bulk
profile, CPM-normalizes both sides over the shared genes, applies `log2(x+1)`,
and reports Pearson r, Spearman rho, and a linear fit.

With `discriminability: true` it also correlates **every** pseudo-bulk group
against **every** bulk group and reports:

- matched vs mismatched mean r and their gap
- whether each pseudo-bulk group best-matches its own bulk group

Do this whenever the correlation is meant as evidence. A single high r cannot
show that a correlation is meaningful, because any two transcriptomes from the
same experiment correlate strongly; the discriminability block can.

## Files

| File | Role |
|---|---|
| `package.json` | bundle manifest (`dsh.bundle.patch`), display metadata, dependency declarations |
| `cordis.patch.yml` | inserts the Host plugin row and its config |
| `index.js` | registers the tool, validates arguments, launches the analysis, reads the result JSON |
| `python/bulk_scrna_concordance.py` | the analysis itself |
| `locale/{en,zh}.json` | Plugin Manager card text |

**This bundle declares no npm dependencies and imports nothing outside `node:`.**
A Host-only bundle needs none, and a dependency would make installation require
the npm registry. The tool definition is therefore a plain registry-ready object
with JSON Schema parameters, plus the local argument check that `defineTool`
would otherwise supply. `Config` is declared as JSON Schema for the same reason.

## Prerequisite: a Python interpreter with the scientific stack

The analysis needs **`anndata`, `h5py`, `scipy`, `pandas`, `numpy`,
`matplotlib`**. The interpreter that ships inside DSH has only `numpy` and
`pandas`, so it is *not* sufficient for `.h5ad` input.

Check a candidate interpreter:

```bash
python -c "import anndata, h5py, scipy, pandas, numpy, matplotlib; print('ok')"
```

Then point the plugin at it. The shipped `cordis.patch.yml` assumes `python` on
`PATH`; override it in your profile's own `cordis.patch.yml`:

```yaml
- id: bulk-scrna-concordance
  name: "@local/dsh-bulk-scrna-concordance"
  config:
    pythonPath: /usr/bin/python3        # or C:/Python313/python.exe
    defaultTimeoutMs: 1800000
    maxLogLines: 40
```

An absolute `pythonPath` is recommended: the Host's `PATH` is not guaranteed to
match your shell's.

If the interpreter is wrong the tool returns a clean failure naming the path and
listing the packages it needs — it does not throw.

## Install

```bash
git clone https://github.com/<you>/dsh-bulk-scrna-concordance
```

Then install the checkout into a profile. In the Harness Web UI:

1. Open **Settings → Plugins**.
2. Install a bundle, with the **absolute path of the directory containing
   `package.json`** as the target (e.g. `/home/me/dsh-bulk-scrna-concordance`
   or `C:\src\dsh-bulk-scrna-concordance`).
3. Read the returned `application` field. `applied` means it is live;
   `restart-required` means it is not yet.

From a shell, where a `dsh` CLI is available:

```bash
dsh plugin --profile <profile> add /abs/path/to/dsh-bulk-scrna-concordance
```

That installs the package, links it into `node_modules` and adds it to
`dsh.profile.bundles`. It writes **no row** into the profile's
`cordis.patch.yml`, so add the config row yourself if you need a non-default
`pythonPath` (see above).

Notes:

- `@local/...` is a deliberate scope: this package is meant to be installed from
  a path or a git checkout, not published to npm.
- The installer performs package installation and bundle selection. Do not
  hand-edit the profile's `package.json` or `cordis.patch.yml` to select a
  bundle, and do not run `pnpm` in the profile directory.
- A fresh bundle can activate through HMR. **Replacing an already-installed
  package requires a restart** to load the new JavaScript generation.
- The Desktop app owns the `desktop` profile and the `dsh` CLI refuses to write
  it; install from inside the app there.

## Verify

1. The tool row exists and is enabled (Plugin Manager, or `cordis_inspect_query`).
2. Run it on real data and confirm the tool result, not just the log:

   ```
   bulk_scrna_concordance with
     sc_h5ad        /path/to/scRNA_with_celltype.h5ad
     bulk_csv       /path/to/bulk_FPKM.csv
     group_col      Group
     discriminability true
     out_dir        <somewhere writable>
   ```

   Expected on the dataset this was developed against (verified — see below):

   | group | Pearson r | Spearman rho | n_genes |
   |---|---|---|---|
   | L1 | 0.8726 | 0.8606 | 21843 |
   | L2 | 0.8844 | 0.8782 | 22206 |
   | L3 | 0.8772 | 0.8748 | 22104 |

   and `discriminability`: matched 0.8781, mismatched 0.8213, gap 0.0568,
   `correct=2/3`, `misassigned: ["L1->L2"]`.

## What was fixed relative to the original

1. **`--strip_version` was a dead switch.** It was `action="store_true"` with
   `default=True`, so it could never be turned off. It is now
   `--strip-version / --no-strip-version`, default off.
2. **Duplicate gene IDs after version stripping crashed the analysis.** The
   original truncated at the first `.` with no dedup, then
   `pseudo_df.loc[common_genes, g]` returned a DataFrame for a duplicated label
   and died with
   `ValueError: operands could not be broadcast together with shapes (n,) (m,)`.
   Duplicate IDs are now collapsed explicitly (values summed) and the count is
   reported.
3. **Bulk sample-to-group matching was ambiguous.** `startswith`/`endswith`
   /substring tests silently mis-assigned groups that are prefixes of one
   another (L1 vs L10). Matching now uses exact delimited tokens, and unmatched
   samples are reported instead of dropped quietly.
4. **The `nan` group was treated as a real group.** In the original dataset 3440
   cells have no group label, and the original built a pseudo-bulk column for
   them. They are now excluded and reported.
5. **Added the discriminability assessment** described above.
6. **Added `--results-json`** so a caller reads one structured object instead of
   scraping stdout (stdout is a log file here, for the sandbox reason below).
7. **Run parameters are recorded** in the result JSON for reproducibility.
8. **The figure no longer emits a `tight_layout` warning.**

### One deliberate numeric change

CPM normalization is computed over the genes actually used in the correlation
(the shared, informative set), not over the whole shared gene list as in the
original. **Pearson r and Spearman rho are identical** to the original for this
reason — they are invariant to a linear rescaling of either axis. The fitted
`slope`/`intercept` are on a different scale: e.g. L1 slope is 0.901 here vs
0.845 in the original. Scale-free reporting should quote r, not the slope.

### Normalization is now explicit

`--normalize {cpm,tpm,none}` (tool argument `normalize`), default `cpm`:

- **`cpm`** — the historical behaviour, and what every published number above used.
- **`tpm`** — also divides by gene length. Needs `--sc-lengths-col` (an `.h5ad`
  `var` column) and `--bulk-lengths-col` (a bulk column, excluded from the
  expression matrix). Lengths must be present on both sides or the run stops,
  rather than silently falling back.
- **`none`** — inputs already on a common scale.

The choice is recorded in the results JSON and the manifest, because it changes
the fitted slope even though it barely moves r.

## Why stdout is a file rather than a pipe

Under the Harness file sandbox, child processes may not use piped stdio
(`spawnSync ... EPERM`); `stdio: 'inherit'` and raw file-descriptor redirection
both work. The plugin opens a descriptor on `<out_dir>/<prefix>_run.log`, gives
the child a duplicate of it, then reads the tail back for diagnostics. The
machine-readable result does not travel over stdout at all — it is read from the
JSON file the script writes.

## Outputs

Everything lands in `out_dir`:

| File | Content |
|---|---|
| `<prefix>_manifest.json` | **provenance**: script hash, input/output SHA-256, params, seed, environment lock |
| `<prefix>_results.json` | schema `dsh.bulk-scrna-concordance/1`: parameters, per-group stats, discriminability matrix, warnings, environment |
| `<prefix>_bulk_scrna_correlation_stats.csv` | one row per group |
| `<prefix>_discriminability.csv` | the pseudo × bulk Pearson matrix |
| `<prefix>_bulk_scrna_correlation.{png,pdf,svg}` | density scatter with regression and y=x lines |
| `<prefix>_run.log` | full analysis log |

### Provenance

Every run writes a manifest answering *"this figure = which code + which inputs +
which parameters + which environment"*:

- **script hash** — the analysis script's own SHA-256, so a figure produced by a
  modified script is detectable;
- **input hashes** — SHA-256, byte size and mtime for the `.h5ad` and bulk matrix.
  An input that changed silently between runs is otherwise invisible;
- **environment lock** — `python`, `numpy`, `pandas`, **`scipy`**, **`anndata`**,
  `h5py`, `matplotlib` and the seed. `anndata` decides how `.X`/`.raw` are read and
  `scipy` computes every statistic here, so those two are the versions that can
  actually move a reported `r`; recording only numpy/pandas would miss them;
- **output hashes** — every produced file, so a figure can be checked against the
  run that claims to have made it;
- **command line and timestamps**.

Nothing in this analysis is stochastic. The manifest records `seed: 42` anyway, so
that is a checkable claim rather than an assumption.

This follows the provenance model of
[`poplarity/dsh-science-workbench`](https://github.com/poplarity/dsh-science-workbench)
(see [docs/github-survey.md](docs/github-survey.md)), minus the project/cell/feedback
machinery that belongs to a workbench rather than to one analysis.

Pass `--no-manifest` to skip it.

### The figure does not appear in the conversation, by platform design

A tool result **cannot** carry a picture. The Harness attachment documentation is
explicit that the role-neutral `ImageBlock` leaves assistant-side image output as
forward compatibility, and that **current production adapters declare text-only
output, so only user content carries images**. An `ImageBlock` also needs an
`attachmentId` minted by the `attachments` service, and that service is not
mounted in every profile.

The render therefore emits the path plus a Markdown image reference, and states
that surfacing the figure as a card in the Web UI needs a separate `present`
call with the file path. Without that second call a user sees only a path and may
reasonably conclude no figure was produced at all.

## Verification status

Performed, and reproducible:

- **Python layer** — full run on the real 720 MB `.h5ad` and the real bulk
  matrix; per-group r reproduced to 1e-9 against an independent recomputation;
  discriminability matrix matches an independent 3×3 computation exactly.
- **Node layer** — the registered tool was exercised through a stub `ctx.tools`
  in five cases: invalid input combinations rejected; a bad `pythonPath`
  returned a clean `failed` object; a real analysis returned `status: ok` with
  the expected statistics; `render()` produced the expected model-facing text
  for both success and failure; and disposing the registration removes the tool.
- **Manifest** — `package.json` parses, all `exports` targets exist, every file
  in the bundle validates as UTF-8, `node --check` passes on `index.js`,
  `py_compile` passes on the script.
- **Composition against the real Loader** — the bundle's patch was applied to a
  scratch profile through `dsh --profile <name> --patch … --dump-config`; the row
  appears in the composed tree with its `id`, resolved module URL and full
  `config`, and the tree composes without error.
- **Installed into the `desktop` profile** with
  `dsh plugin --profile desktop add <bundle dir>` (pnpm `link:`, no registry
  access needed). Confirmed afterwards: the bundle name is in
  `dsh.profile.bundles`, the dependency is in `package.json`, and
  `node_modules/@local/dsh-bulk-scrna-concordance` resolves to this directory.
  The profile patch carries a matching `bulk-scrna-concordance` row whose row
  `id` overrides the bundle's default `config`, so `pythonPath` points at
  `D:/Python/python.exe`.
- **API contract read from the installed Harness**, not assumed:
  `ctx.tools.register()` was read at `dsh-tools/lib/index.js:2878` and requires
  `output.{schema,render}` plus a schema accepted by
  `assertSupportedJsonSchema` — it does **not** require a `defineTool()` result,
  which is what makes the dependency-free form valid. The supported keyword set
  is `type/oneOf/properties/required/additionalProperties/items/enum/const` plus
  `description/title/default/examples`; this bundle uses only those.
- **Live activation and a live tool call**, through a real Harness agent. A
  scratch headless profile (`base` + `dsh-headless` + this bundle) was booted
  with `dsh --profile <name> "<task>"`. The agent called
  `bulk_scrna_concordance` once on the real `.h5ad` and bulk matrix and reported
  `status: ok` with r = 0.873 / 0.884 / 0.877 and gap 0.0568 (`L1→L2`
  misassigned) — matching the independently computed values exactly. All six
  output files were written to the requested directory.

## Two traps worth knowing, both hit while installing this

1. **Do not export `Config` unless its schema library resolvable from the
   plugin.** Cordis resolves an exported `Config` through schemastery
   (`resolveConfig` calls `Config.validate`). `@deepseek-ai/schemastery` is not
   resolvable from a bundle installed by path, so an exported `Config` makes the
   plugin fail to activate with:

   ```
   bulk-scrna-concordance (@local/dsh-bulk-scrna-concordance):
   TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'validate')
   ```

   `Config` is optional, so it is omitted here and the row's config is read
   defensively in `apply()`. The symptom is a **silent** missing tool: the row
   composes, but only a boot-time warning says `1 entry did not activate`.

2. **A newly installed bundle needs a restart.** `dsh plugin --profile desktop
   add <path>` installs and selects the bundle, but writes no row into the
   profile's `cordis.patch.yml` (unlike `install_bundle`), and the running app
   does not pick up the new JavaScript generation. Both were needed here: the
   install, then a restart.

## Scratch profile used for verification

`~/.dsh/profiles/concordlive` — `dsh-base` + the shipped `dsh-headless` bundle +
this bundle, with a patch row supplying `pythonPath`. It is what produced the
live verification above, and is safe to delete:

```powershell
dsh plugin --profile concordlive remove @local/dsh-bulk-scrna-concordance
```

Note `dsh plugin … add @deepseek-ai/dsh-headless` installs the **registry**
copy, which is `0.0.1-rc.1` and is rejected as incompatible with dsh
`0.2.0-rc.2`; the shipped bundle inside the installation is `0.2.0-rc.2` and is
selected by name from `dsh.profile.bundles`, which is what this profile does.


`exec.agent.session.cwd` is read defensively for relative-path resolution; if
that field is absent in the installed version, paths fall back to the Host's
working directory, so passing absolute paths always works.
